voyager-stranis.summary:
Voyager Asherah is a straightforward area damage dealer with a single-target basic. Dawn of Night adds Chill and CRIT DMG, Veil Cleave adds SPD and gains damage at full Chill, and her upgraded passive improves critical offense as the fight develops.

She is a straightforward area attacker once Chill is established. Her special checks full Chill for extra damage without listing resource consumption, so maintaining that condition matters more than repeatedly rebuilding from zero. ATK and critical stats support her offensive buffs. She brings little party protection, and enemy count, affinity and defenses still determine whether area damage solves the encounter.
voyager-stranis.watch: The passive’s level descriptions say CRIT DMG rises after each attack, but its effect tooltip names Veil Cleave specifically. Treat the exact ramp trigger as unresolved rather than promising a fixed number of attacks to maximum stacks.
voyager-stranis.dependency_note: She builds her own offensive buffs and Chill, but has no recovery or protection. A support that adds ATK or area vulnerability does more than merely matching her attribute.

skill_order.name: Veil Cleave
skill_order.why: Veil Cleave’s level-6/10 cooldown reductions improve repeat area access and SPD buff usage.

skill_order.name: Dawn of Night
skill_order.why: Dawn of Night’s level-6/10 cooldown reductions provide more area damage, Chill and CRIT DMG windows.

skill_order.name: Stranis Style Breathing
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels add on-attack CRIT Rate and the ramping CRIT DMG described in the level text.

skill_order.name: Stranis Style Slash
skill_order.why: Basic damage follows the skills; use it to fill gaps and add Chill.

rotation: Use Dawn of Night when its area damage, two Chill or CRIT DMG buff help now. There is no need to spend an arbitrary first turn on the basic.
Use Veil Cleave for area damage and two-turn SPD Up. If already near five Chill and no urgent wave clear is needed, build to five first for its 30% damage bonus.
Fill cooldown gaps with Stranis Style Slash. Recheck Chill rather than assuming any fixed basic-special-ultimate cycle is optimal.
Keep buffs and survival support available; do not depend on a precise passive-ramp timeline while its trigger wording conflicts.

best_partners.why: Bind increases damage taken from all-target attacks, directly helping both of Asherah’s cooldown attacks.
Cleaning Service supplies ATK Up and a Barrier that Asherah cannot provide herself.
Carmen can protect the highest-ATK carry and grant three Chill to a Moon ally with her targeted ultimate.

voyager-stranis.build_tip: ATK and critical damage with enough CRIT Rate to complement the upgraded passive’s 30% on-attack bonus. SPD supports repeated cooldown cycles; retain survival stats because she has no self-heal. Journey option: Faded Dream is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
voyager-stranis.tier_reason: The modest PvE and lower PvP ratings fit damage-focused wave utility without immediate team protection or enemy control. Her full-Chill bonus and ramp need time; the conflicted passive trigger should not be used to inflate either mode claim.
voyager-stranis.investment: Both area skills have cooldown reductions at levels 6 and 10; prioritize whichever is doing the needed job, with Veil Cleave favored for recurring wave damage/SPD. Passive level 1 adds ATK only; later levels add critical mechanics. No unique potential is listed. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +3 CRIT Rate; it is not part of the starting stat line.
voyager-stranis.pve_note: A usable area carry for waves when supported. Full Chill benefits Veil Cleave specifically, and its direct attribute bonus is against Sun; do not treat every stack as universal damage.
voyager-stranis.pvp_note: Needs allies to survive and establish pressure. She lacks the explicit extra-turn/control package of stronger PvP attackers, so avoid assuming a slow ramp can win against an opening burst team.

kit_explanation.name: Stranis Style Slash
kit_explanation.explanation: Stranis Style Slash attacks one enemy and adds one Chill. Chill gives a small stacking damage bonus against Sun enemies, capped at five; it also provides the full-stack condition for Veil Cleave.

kit_explanation.name: Veil Cleave
kit_explanation.explanation: Veil Cleave attacks all enemies, grants two-turn SPD Up and gains 30% damage if Chill is full on attack. It does not explicitly consume Chill. Its listed five-turn cooldown drops at levels 6 and 10.

kit_explanation.name: Dawn of Night
kit_explanation.explanation: Dawn of Night attacks all enemies, grants two-turn CRIT DMG Up and adds two Chill. Its listed six-turn cooldown drops at levels 6 and 10. Nova increases its damage and Toughness damage; it does not add team utility.

kit_explanation.name: Stranis Style Breathing
kit_explanation.explanation: Stranis Style Breathing initially adds ATK. Higher passive levels add 30% on-attack CRIT Rate and stackable CRIT DMG. Level descriptions name every attack as the ramp trigger, while the separate effect tooltip names Veil Cleave; the guide does not assume one interpretation is proven.

pros: Two area skills cover multiple enemies without a required debuff setup.
Own SPD and CRIT DMG buffs reduce dependence on offensive support.
Full Chill provides a clear conditional Veil Cleave payoff.
Her full-Chill special bonus does not list stack consumption.
cons: No listed enemy control, healing or protection.
Later passive mechanics are absent at passive level 1.
Conflicting passive trigger text prevents a trustworthy fixed ramp timeline.

teams.name: Supported Moon waves
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Voyager Luna applies area vulnerability, Emily shields/buffs Asherah and Frey heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use Bind before Asherah’s area damage where possible; use skills for current wave needs instead of delaying all damage for full Chill.

teams.name: Chill-assisted carry
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Carmen can feed Chill to Moon Asherah, Ceres disrupts enemies and dress Asherah supplies party sustain.
teams.playstyle: Make the intended carry the oath target and use Carmen’s targeted support when needed; do not assume her cleanse targets the whole team.

alternatives.why: Amora is higher-rated in both modes and offers area damage plus an explicit extra turn, Bloom penetration and conditional cleanse.
alternatives.tradeoff: Voyager Asherah retains a simpler damage kit and a full-Chill area bonus without needing a debuff to land.

alternatives.why: Ceres has stronger published ratings and adds area buff removal, Freeze and targeted Stun/gauge reduction.
alternatives.tradeoff: Asherah retains two direct area-damage cooldowns and self critical buffs when control is unnecessary or blocked.

voyager-stranis.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

voyager-smile.summary:
Voyager Smile focuses one enemy with her basic and ultimate, then adds automatic area Cat Tapdance attacks when its HP or upgraded Leap condition is met. Those attacks and the ultimate build Smile Matrix, an ATK ramp, while the ultimate also attempts DEF Down.

She fits a longer fight where a durable focus target survives her basic and the area reaction can reach other enemies. Open with useful DEF Down rather than spending several turns chasing Matrix. ATK, critical consistency and speed support both halves of the plan. A weak target that dies immediately can be worse reaction setup than a sturdier one.
voyager-smile.watch: Cat Tapdance is not a manual skill. Its basic-trigger path needs the target to survive at half HP or below, and its one-turn reaction cooldown still matters. The upgraded passive has another full-Leap trigger; passive level 1 does not.
voyager-smile.dependency_note: She supplies her own DEF Down and stack generation, but teammates that soften a durable target can make the basic-trigger condition available sooner.

skill_order.name: All Units, Open Fire!
skill_order.why: Levels 6/10 shorten the ultimate cooldown; DEF Down and three Leap support the rest of her cycle.

skill_order.name: Cat Tapdance
skill_order.why: Levels 6/10 raise Cat Tapdance’s Burn chance and damage upgrades improve automatic area follow-ups.

skill_order.name: Happy Trigger
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels add the full-Leap trigger and basic turn progress.

skill_order.name: Firing Coordinates Confirmed
skill_order.why: Basic damage matters in repeated use but comes after unlocking reliable follow-up utility.

rotation: Use All Units, Open Fire! on the priority enemy to attempt DEF Down, add a Smile Matrix stack and gain three Leap; do not insist on basic stacking first.
Use Firing Coordinates Confirmed on a target likely to survive the hit at 50% HP or below when a Cat Tapdance follow-up would help. A killing basic does not activate that HP-trigger path.
With upgraded Happy Trigger, full Leap after attacking can consume all stacks and trigger Cat Tapdance even without that low-HP basic setup. This remains automatic, not a separate cast.
Track the reaction cooldown and actual matrix buildup rather than promising repeated area attacks every time a condition appears.

best_partners.why: Star-target recovery bonuses, full targeted cleanse and team Barriers cover Smile’s lack of defenses.
Smile’s Star attacks can feed Omega’s Leap generation, while her DEF Down supports the priority target’s damage intake.
Ceres softens groups and removes a buff, making surviving low-HP targets easier for Smile to exploit.

voyager-smile.build_tip: ATK and critical stats for direct damage and Burn scaling, with SPD for frequent basics. Effect Hit helps DEF Down/Burn against susceptible enemies; do not assume her listed chances guarantee applications. Journey option: Vacation Prep: Time to Shop! is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +7% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
voyager-smile.tier_reason: The better PvE than PvP rating fits gradual Matrix ramp and conditional area follow-ups over longer fights. PvP can end or deny target access before those conditions pay off, and Smile brings little personal protection or immediate hard control.
voyager-smile.investment: Prioritize ultimate cooldown reductions at levels 6/10 and Cat Tapdance’s Burn chance at levels 6/10 if using the area follow-up. Confirm Happy Trigger’s later-level mechanics before planning gauge gain or the full-Leap trigger. No unique potential is listed. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here. Laughter Protocol belongs to Summer Smile in savior_sources; the character_id match does not establish it for this version. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 10 at level 200, listing +12 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
voyager-smile.pve_note: Useful against a durable target surrounded by enemies that can take splash damage. Very weak enemies may die to the basic before its low-HP follow-up condition activates.
voyager-smile.pvp_note: Can pressure a focus target while adding conditional area damage, but she is slower to realize her ramp than immediate control or extra-turn carries. Protect her before relying on Matrix stacks.

kit_explanation.name: Firing Coordinates Confirmed
kit_explanation.explanation: Firing Coordinates Confirmed is a single-target basic granting one Leap. The upgraded passive adds progress toward Smile’s next turn after it; that extra effect is not in the ordinary basic description itself.

kit_explanation.name: Cat Tapdance
kit_explanation.explanation: Cat Tapdance is an automatic all-target reaction with a listed one-turn cooldown. After her basic, it triggers if the attacked enemy survives at half HP or below. It attempts one-turn Burn and adds Smile Matrix, which gives 5% ATK per stack up to ten. Burn chance grows from 75% to 100% at skill levels 6 and 10.

kit_explanation.name: All Units, Open Fire!
kit_explanation.explanation: All Units, Open Fire! attacks one enemy, attempts two-turn DEF Down, adds one Smile Matrix and grants three Leap. Its listed six-turn cooldown drops at levels 6 and 10. Nova adds Toughness damage and damage dealt, not a new manually selectable follow-up.

kit_explanation.name: Happy Trigger
kit_explanation.explanation: Happy Trigger initially gives ATK only. From passive level 2 it consumes maximum Leap after attacking to trigger Cat Tapdance and grants basic-based turn progress, doubled when that basic leaves the enemy at half HP or below. The progress values scale from 9% plus 9% to 15% plus 15%.

pros: Ultimate combines DEF Down, three Leap and an additional Smile Matrix ATK stack in one action.
Low-HP basics can add an area follow-up without selecting another action.
Upgraded passive creates a second stack-based follow-up route.
The ultimate supplies a Matrix stack without the basic’s survival condition.
cons: Killing with the basic prevents its HP-condition follow-up.
Cat Tapdance has a cooldown despite being automatic.
No innate heal, Barrier or team cleanse.

teams.name: Star ramp pairing
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Smile and Roberta supply Star attacks for Omega while Frey heals the Star allies and cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Focus a durable enemy, use Smile’s DEF Down before damage and treat Cat Tapdance as conditional splash.

teams.name: Protected focus splash
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Carmen protects the selected carry, Ceres exposes targets and dress Asherah sustains/cleanses the group.
teams.playstyle: Set Smile as highest ATK if she is the intended oath carry; use surviving weakened targets for basic-trigger opportunities.

alternatives.why: Roberta has higher ratings and stronger reaction/cleanse utility when enemies repeatedly attack all targets.
alternatives.tradeoff: Voyager Smile still supplies DEF Down and area splash without needing an enemy area hit.

alternatives.why: Summer Smile is higher-rated in both modes and offers ally-triggered marked-target follow-ups.
alternatives.tradeoff: Voyager Smile is less dependent on allies focusing a particular mark and offers DEF Down directly.

voyager-smile.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

voyager-oracle.summary:
Voyager Luna is an area attacker whose Bind makes enemies take more damage from all-target attacks. She builds Insight with basics and her ultimate, then uses Hecate’s Ember as a stronger full-stack payoff. Her unique potential adds a separate random-target chain-damage mechanic.

Use Luna (Voyager Savior Party) with allies who also attack every enemy. Bind increases damage received from those attacks by 20%; it does not stop the opponent acting. Her all-target basic keeps contributing when cooldown skills are unavailable, while five Insight improve Hecate’s Ember. Give her critical consistency and ATK, then enough Effect Hit for the enabling debuff. The optional Path of Destiny adds random-target chain damage, so do not promise that all extra hits finish one priority enemy.
voyager-oracle.watch: Bind does not stop enemies acting: the local effect is 20% more damage taken from all-target attacks. Hecate’s Ember consumes Insight, so spending it early can delay the full-stack bonus. The passive’s opening stacks and critical-hit generation are absent at passive level 1.
voyager-oracle.dependency_note: She deals her own area damage and also improves other area attackers through Bind. Buff support enables an upgraded passive critical-damage bonus on the ultimate.

skill_order.name: The World I See
skill_order.why: The World I See supplies Bind, Insight and area damage; levels 4/8 improve application and level 6 reduces cooldown.

skill_order.name: Hecate's Ember
skill_order.why: Hecate’s Ember is the full-Insight payoff; levels 6/10 reduce its listed cooldown.

skill_order.name: Girl Who Sees the Future
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels add opening Insight, critical-hit stack gain and the buffed-ultimate bonus.

skill_order.name: Defensive Mana Shot
skill_order.why: Area basic investment is useful after the main skills, especially when used often between cooldowns.

rotation: Use The World I See before allied area attacks when Bind vulnerability can land. Its Nova raises the listed application chance to 100%, but does not explicitly bypass immunity or resistance.
Have a useful buff on Luna before her ultimate if the upgraded passive feature is available. Do not add an otherwise useless support turn merely for this check.

Watch Insight before Hecate's Ember: at five stacks it gains 30% damage. It consumes Insight afterward, so use it early only when immediate wave damage or the CRIT Rate buff is worth resetting the build-up.
Fill with Defensive Mana Shot, which hits all enemies and builds Insight. With Path of Destiny acquired, ally turns build a separate chain-damage stack; this is automatic, not a selectable attack.

best_partners.why: Both major Asherah attacks hit all enemies and can benefit from Bind’s all-target damage vulnerability.
Light-Forged Execution benefits from landed Bind, then Amora has her own extra-turn pressure.
Cleaning Service supplies an ATK buff and Barrier to Luna, supporting the upgraded buffed-ultimate condition.

voyager-oracle.build_tip: ATK and critical stats for area damage, accounting for Hecate’s Ember’s 30% CRIT Rate buff. Add Effect Hit when Bind is part of the plan; SPD helps place vulnerability before other area attackers. Follow the Light! supports Strength and adds one Strength during training after 50 Bond. A Midsummer Night’s Sky supports Vitality, useful for survival but a different training goal.
voyager-oracle.tier_reason: The stronger published PvP than PvE rating is consistent with area vulnerability supporting coordinated pressure, rather than a claim that Bind skips enemy turns. In PvE she remains useful for waves, but a lone immune boss removes much of her enabling value.
voyager-oracle.investment: Prioritize the ultimate’s level-6 cooldown and level-4/8 Bind chance, then Hecate’s Ember’s level-6/10 cooldowns. Path of Destiny adds ATK-scaling chain damage to a random enemy per stored opportunity stack; it is acquired separately and does not guarantee focus damage. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here.
voyager-oracle.pve_note: Plan area vulnerability before wave damage. Against a single enemy, assess her damage and support slot honestly; Bind specifically rewards attacks targeting all, not every single-target hit.
voyager-oracle.pvp_note: Useful in a coordinated area team that can act after her. Bind is a damage-taken debuff, so the opponent may still act, cleanse, resist or protect allies before your follow-up.

kit_explanation.name: Defensive Mana Shot
kit_explanation.explanation: Defensive Mana Shot is an all-target basic that adds one Insight. With the relevant passive level, a critical hit from this basic adds another Insight; do not assume one bonus per enemy hit.

kit_explanation.name: Hecate's Ember
kit_explanation.explanation: Hecate's Ember attacks all enemies and grants two-turn CRIT Rate Up. At full Insight on attack it gains 30% damage. The description then reduces its cooldown by one and consumes Insight, but its sentence structure leaves the scope of that reduction unclear; plan around the explicit full-stack payoff rather than promising an unconditional short cycle. Listed cooldown is five, with reductions at levels 6 and 10.

kit_explanation.name: The World I See
kit_explanation.explanation: The World I See attacks all enemies, adds two Insight and attempts two-turn Bind. Application chance rises from 50% to 75%; Nova raises the listed chance to 100%. Bind means 20% more damage taken from all-target attacks, not a stun. Its listed five-turn cooldown drops at level 6.

kit_explanation.name: Girl Who Sees the Future
kit_explanation.explanation: Girl Who Sees the Future initially raises ATK. From passive level 2 it also grants two Insight at the first battle’s start, adds Insight when the basic or ultimate critically hits and increases ultimate CRIT DMG if Luna has a buff. These extra mechanics require the appropriate passive level.

pros: Bind supports multiple allied area attackers instead of only Luna’s own damage.
All three attack buttons hit all enemies.
Critical-hit Insight generation and Path of Destiny can reward an active team once acquired/unlocked.
The ultimate’s Nova raises Bind’s application chance from 75% to 100%.
cons: Bind does not deny turns and may fail to apply.
Full-stack Ember and its stack consumption require planning.
Unique-potential chain damage selects random enemies rather than guaranteeing the priority target.

teams.name: Area vulnerability core
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Luna sets Bind, Amora supplies area execution, Emily buffs/protects and Frey heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Try to place Bind before Amora’s area attack and preserve Luna’s full Insight for Ember when the wave survives long enough.

teams.name: Sustained wave pressure
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Asherah exploits area vulnerability, Carmen sustains the main carry and Lydia slows enemies while lowering Effect RES.
teams.playstyle: Use vulnerability and slows where enemies permit them; keep the intended carry highest ATK for Carmen’s oath.

alternatives.why: Amora is higher-rated in both modes and offers immediate area pressure with an explicit extra turn and conditional self-cleanse.
alternatives.tradeoff: Luna retains Bind’s teamwide area-damage enabling role and an all-target basic.

alternatives.why: Ceres has higher published ratings and offers area dispel plus targeted Stun/turn reduction when disruption matters.
alternatives.tradeoff: Luna supplies area vulnerability and repeated area damage rather than Ceres’s control package.

voyager-oracle.research_note: Public character build reviewed; gear details were image-only or gated, so no unseen set or slot recommendation is claimed.

maid-lantern.summary:
Carnelia is an area-damage caster with a strong opening and a once-per-battle survival response. Umbral Echo improves her area ultimate and makes Guiding Twilight repeat once against a random enemy. Her special also blocks buffs and reduces enemy progress toward the next turn, giving her control beyond damage.

Open around the first Umbral Echo window instead of waiting for a crisis to unlock her damage. Its presence adds 50% damage to Dissonance Break and allows the special to repeat automatically once, although the additional target is random. ATK and critical stats support both attacks. Her lethal-hit response creates a second opportunity; it is not a substitute for healing or a plan to survive repeated focused attacks.
maid-lantern.watch: Spoke prevents a lethal defeat once, restores only 1% maximum HP, then gives temporary Immortality and resets cooldowns. This is not a repeatable revive. The repeated Guiding Twilight hits a random enemy, and Buff Block does not strip buffs already present.
maid-lantern.dependency_note: She starts with her own Umbral Echo window and can attack independently. Healing is still valuable after the lethal-hit response; a buff provider improves damage but is not a required trigger.

skill_order.name: Dissonance Break
skill_order.why: For an area carry, prioritize the level-6 cooldown, level-8 turn-progress improvement and damage.

skill_order.name: Guiding Twilight
skill_order.why: For control, prioritize this instead: cooldown level 6 and Buff Block chance through level 8.

skill_order.name: Spoke
skill_order.why: Passive upgrades strengthen ATK scaling; survival remains a once-per-battle tool.

skill_order.name: Gesture of Dawn
skill_order.why: Basic damage follows the two major cooldown attacks.

rotation: During the opening Umbral Echo, choose Dissonance Break for area damage or Guiding Twilight for an urgent Buff Block/turn delay; do not claim both fit inside a one-turn buff without checking actual turn order.
After Spoke activates, reassess reset cooldowns and the longer Echo window, then heal or protect Carnelia before temporary survival expires.
Use Gesture of Dawn in gaps. Never deliberately require lethal damage as a safe rotation step, and never manually queue the random Guiding Twilight repeat.

best_partners.why: Ceres can heal Carnelia after Spoke leaves her near minimum HP and adds cleanse and team ATK Up.
Emily's targeted Barrier and ATK buff protect Carnelia before or after her survival response.
Seira can grant Carnelia Greater ATK Up and progress toward her next turn, supporting a selected damage window.
Bell removes existing buffs while Carnelia blocks future buffs, covering different parts of enemy buff management.

maid-lantern.build_tip: ATK and reliable CRIT Rate/CRIT DMG for area damage, SPD for opening timing, and Effect Hit if Buff Block is the priority. Her listed maximum 93 SPD needs consideration; Immortality does not remove the need for survival stats. Use Strength training for her ATK attacks. Death for the Flowers is an Endurance supplement, with a 5% Condition Effect bonus after 30 Bond; it is not an ATK card.
maid-lantern.tier_reason: The S PvE / S+ PvP ratings fit strong area pressure plus Buff Block, turn delay and a second damage window after lethal-hit prevention. Single-target fights or control immunity narrow the advantage, and the survival tool is finite.
maid-lantern.investment: Choose area damage or control as the first job, then buy the matching level-6 cooldown and level-8 utility upgrade. No unique potentials are listed. Do not build around repeated lethal saves or assume all final passive ATK scaling is available immediately. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
maid-lantern.pve_note: Area attacks are useful for waves; the Nova ultimate gives personal recovery if resource use is justified. On a lone boss, random follow-up targeting is less awkward, but Buff Block and turn delay still depend on the encounter. Demoraigis is listed as Buff Block-immune, so her damage remains useful but that control attempt cannot be the boss plan.
maid-lantern.pvp_note: Opening Echo supports either immediate damage or disruption; check the enemy's buff state before choosing. A lethal-hit save can produce a reset window, but damage after Immortality expires and control can still defeat her.

kit_explanation.name: Gesture of Dawn
kit_explanation.explanation: Gesture of Dawn attacks one target and adds Agitation. Nova adds Toughness damage. It is downtime filler, not a way to manually reapply Umbral Echo.

kit_explanation.name: Guiding Twilight
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 4 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Guiding Twilight attacks one enemy, attempts two turns of Buff Block, reduces its progress toward its next turn by 25%, and adds Agitation. Buff Block chance rises from 75% to 100% at levels 4/8. While Umbral Echo is present, it automatically repeats once that turn against a random enemy; you cannot select that follow-up target.

kit_explanation.name: Dissonance Break
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Dissonance Break hits all enemies, adds Agitation and advances Carnelia's next turn by 15%, increasing to 30% at level 8. Umbral Echo increases its damage dealt by 50%. Level 6 reduces cooldown. Nova adds Toughness damage and heals Carnelia for 15% of damage dealt, not the whole party.

kit_explanation.name: Spoke
kit_explanation.explanation: Spoke grants one turn of Umbral Echo at battle start, providing ATK and Effect RES bonuses. Agitation also increases ATK on attack, from 2% to 6% per stack across passive levels. Once per battle, a lethal hit is prevented: she recovers 1% maximum HP, gains one turn of Immortality and three turns of Umbral Echo, and resets skill cooldowns. This happens automatically and does not resurrect a previously defeated ally.

pros: Strong area damage gains a clear bonus during Umbral Echo.
Special combines Buff Block and direct enemy turn delay.
Once-per-battle lethal-hit prevention resets cooldowns and creates another Echo window.
Echo lets the special repeat automatically once each turn.
cons: The extra special target is random.
Survival response leaves very little HP and cannot be repeated freely.
No party healing and no removal of existing buffs.

teams.name: Protected area carry (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily shields Carnelia, Ceres heals and cleanses, and Seira supplies a stronger ATK buff and ally turn progress.
teams.playstyle: Buff before the chosen area attack when possible; after Spoke, prioritize Carnelia's recovery instead of treating Immortality as lasting protection.

teams.name: Buff suppression (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell strips existing buffs, Carnelia blocks new ones, Emily protects the carry and Frey supplies recovery.
teams.playstyle: Use Bell on the already-buffed threat and Carnelia on the next dangerous buff user; healing stays available after the survival response.

alternatives.why: Lacy has a higher PvE rating and brings fast single-target pressure, a broad ATK-reducing mark and conditional self-healing.
alternatives.tradeoff: She sacrifices Carnelia's area ultimate and Buff Block; a separate build should be justified by the encounter, not the rating alone.

alternatives.why: Bell is a useful control alternative when removing existing buffs and applying Silence are more important.
alternatives.tradeoff: She lacks Carnelia's lethal-hit save and direct ordinary-special turn delay; her PvE rating is lower.

maid-lantern.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

maid-bell.summary:
Bell is a fast control attacker whose main value is disrupting enemy buffs and cooldown skills. Condolence hits the whole team, lowers ACC when it lands and grants Bell SPD Up. Encoffin strips one target's buffs and attempts Silence, while any other unit's defeat feeds her next-turn progress and ATK.

Choose Bell when an enemy buff package or a dangerous cooldown skill is the problem. Her ultimate removes every buff and attempts two turns of Silence on one target; her special instead spreads ACC Down and supplies her own SPD Up. She can act again sooner after any other unit falls, but that payoff needs an actual defeat. She has no recovery, and raid bosses listed as Silence-immune still demand a separate damage and survival plan.
maid-bell.watch: Silence disables active skills with cooldowns; it is not a blanket skipped turn and does not stop every passive. ACC Down peaks at a listed 75% chance, and immunity or cleansing can weaken both control tools. Ally deaths can trigger her passive, but sacrificing allies is not a recommended plan.
maid-bell.dependency_note: Her disruption functions without a specific attribute team. ACC Down has real synergy with Fei's evasion, and Star attacks support Dana, while healers protect Bell's relatively offensive build.

skill_order.name: Encoffin
skill_order.why: For control, take level-6 cooldown and level-8 Silence reliability before marginal damage.

skill_order.name: Condolence
skill_order.why: Then get level-6 cooldown and chance upgrades for area ACC Down; reverse the first two if wave damage is the main job.

skill_order.name: Approaching Rest
skill_order.why: Passive upgrades increase momentum after defeats, but do not guarantee a first kill.

skill_order.name: Obituary
skill_order.why: Basic damage is secondary; Nova utility can matter without maxing damage.

rotation: Use Encoffin immediately on a dangerous buffed enemy if stripping or Silence is urgent; do not delay it only to reach maximum Leap.
Use Condolence for broad damage, SPD Up and ACC Down. If control is not urgent, its three Leap can help prepare a later full-Leap Encoffin.
Reassess after each defeat because Bell may reach her next turn sooner. Do not assume that progress is an instant extra turn or plan around losing allies.

best_partners.why: Kyra's Price of Silence gains damage against a Silenced target, giving Bell's Silence a direct offensive payoff.
Bell's ACC Down can help Fei evade attacks and trigger Lunar Shadow.
Bell's Star attacks feed Dana's Leap; Dana can buff Bell if Bell is the highest-ATK other ally.
Ceres heals and cleanses Bell while adding team ATK Up, preserving the control slot through incoming area damage.

maid-bell.build_tip: SPD and appropriate Effect Hit for disruption, then enough HP/DEF to act. ATK and crit are sensible for a damage hybrid, but do not trade away reliable control timing solely for a larger displayed attack. Deep Mourning supports Focus for Effect Hit; its unique improves Sensory Training chance after 40 Bond. Add Strength training when damage is the priority.
maid-bell.tier_reason: The A PvE / S+ PvP split fits buff stripping and Silence being more influential against opposing teams than many bosses. Defeat momentum helps waves too, but boss immunity and lack of deaths reduce that part of the kit.
maid-bell.investment: Encoffin's cooldown and Silence-chance upgrades are the first control investments, then Condolence's cooldown/chance. No potentials are listed. Passive final-level gauge and ATK numbers are upgraded values, not starting-copy promises. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
maid-bell.pve_note: Useful in waves with buffed enemies and multiple defeats; full-Leap damage can help single-target pressure. Against an immune lone boss, rate her on direct damage and any buffs she can actually remove. Demoraigis lists Silence immunity, so Encoffin’s control is not a substitute for managing that boss’s attacks.
maid-bell.pvp_note: Her published S+ PvP role is consistent with dispel, Silence and fast momentum. Build to act before the target's important skill, while checking resistance, immunity and undispellable buffs rather than assuming Encoffin wins automatically.

kit_explanation.name: Obituary
kit_explanation.explanation: Obituary attacks one enemy and adds Leap. Its Nova adds a one-turn ACC Down attempt and Toughness damage, providing a single-target option when the area special is unavailable.

kit_explanation.name: Condolence
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 4 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Condolence attacks all enemies, attempts two turns of ACC Down, grants Bell two turns of SPD Up and adds three Leap. ACC Down chance rises from 50% to 75% through levels 4 and 8; level 6 shortens cooldown. The skill's flavor mentions binding, but its listed control is ACC Down, not Bind.

kit_explanation.name: Encoffin
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Encoffin hits one target, attempts two turns of Silence and attempts to remove all its buffs. Silence chance grows from 75% to 100% at levels 4/8; level 6 improves cooldown. Full Leap gives 30% more damage without a listed Leap-consumption clause. Dispel does not establish removal of undispellable buffs.

kit_explanation.name: Approaching Rest
kit_explanation.explanation: Approaching Rest automatically advances Bell's next turn when another ally or enemy is defeated, from 30% to 50% across levels. Each defeat also adds an ATK stack, up to three, with 6% to 10% per stack depending on passive level; later levels add baseline ATK. It does not require Bell to land the finishing blow.

pros: Combines broad ACC Down with targeted buff removal and Silence.
Defeats advance her turn even when someone else scores the kill.
Her special provides both resource buildup and personal SPD Up.
The ultimate removes all buffs rather than just one.
cons: Area ACC Down remains probabilistic even at the highest listed level.
Silence and dispel are much less useful against immune or undispellable effects.
No self-heal or Barrier protects an offensive build.

teams.name: Silence payoff (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell supplies Silence for Kyra's bonus damage, Emily protects a carry and Ceres restores the party.
teams.playstyle: Strip or Silence the dangerous target first, then use Kyra's conditional attack while Silence remains; speed order must be checked.

teams.name: Star wave control (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell feeds Dana's Star passive, Haydee protects and lowers ACC, and Frey covers healing and Barriers.
teams.playstyle: Spread damage with Dana and Condolence, preserve Encoffin for a meaningful buffed enemy and heal Haydee after shared damage.

alternatives.why: Carnelia has a higher PvE rating and offers area damage, Buff Block and direct enemy turn delay without waiting for defeats.
alternatives.tradeoff: Buff Block prevents new buffs rather than removing existing ones, so she cannot replace Bell's dispel one-for-one; a new build is required.

alternatives.why: Kyra is a single-target alternative when Stealth and an independent Silence application fit better.
alternatives.tradeoff: She has lower published ratings and no broad ACC Down or all-buff removal; Bell remains the stronger general control package.

maid-bell.research_note: Public character build reviewed; gear details were image-only or gated, so no unseen set or slot recommendation is claimed.

maid-twohander.summary:
Emily is an HP-scaling defender who protects a chosen attacker while building repeated area damage. Cleaning Service supplies ATK Up and a Barrier without giving up Emily's next action, and incoming attacks reduce her ultimate cooldown. Turn-Down Service builds Awakened Memory, making later ultimates more threatening.

Build maximum HP first: her basic and ultimate both use it, and her barriers also depend on it. Cleaning Service protects and strengthens one carry, while its extra turn belongs to Emily and lets her continue into an attack. Incoming hits shorten her long ultimate cooldown and repeated ultimates accumulate Awakened Memory. She still needs a healer for lasting recovery; the cleaning-themed skill name does not mean that it removes debuffs.
maid-twohander.watch: Cleaning Service's flavor says she cleanses, but its actual description and effects list no debuff removal. Emily also has no ordinary heal or Taunt. She must survive attacks to gain cooldown value, and taking damage is not automatically a safe plan.
maid-twohander.dependency_note: Her targeted Barrier and ATK buff fit a damage carry, while a real healer/cleanser covers attrition and debuffs. Incoming area attacks feed her loop; allies do not need to share her attribute to use the Barrier.

skill_order.name: Turn-Down Service
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces a very long base cooldown; improve damage for the repeated-area role.

skill_order.name: Cleaning Service
skill_order.why: Then get level 6 for Barrier/ATK-buff uptime and improve Barrier strength; prioritize this first if protection is the immediate need.

skill_order.name: Ready Maid
skill_order.why: Passive HP and area-hit Chill reliability support the cooldown engine.

skill_order.name: Commence Combat Cleanup
skill_order.why: Basic damage is lower priority than protection and the scaling ultimate.

rotation: Use Cleaning Service on the ally who needs both protection and ATK, then spend Emily's extra turn on an appropriate attack.
If safe, enter Turn-Down Service with maximum Chill to trigger its extra cooldown reduction; do not delay urgent party DEF Up or a needed finish just for the resource threshold.
Use Commence Combat Cleanup to build Chill in gaps. Let Ready Maid reduce cooldowns automatically and heal Emily before repeated hits overwhelm her.

best_partners.why: Ceres supplies real healing and cleansing while Emily supplies a targeted Barrier and party DEF Up.
Carnelia is a useful recipient for Cleaning Service's ATK buff and Barrier, including after her lethal-hit response.
Emily can protect the marked attacker or Lydia; her own area ultimate also feeds Lydia if Emily actually receives Passing the Buck.
Seira can accelerate another carry with Greater ATK Up while Emily protects it; avoid treating overlapping ATK buffs as automatically additive.

maid-twohander.build_tip: HP supports Emily's Barrier, attack scaling and survival. Add SPD for timely protection, then DEF and damage stats appropriate to a hybrid role. Her maximum 41,634 HP is not measured equal-investment superiority. A Quiet Moment of Rest supports Vitality and adds 7% Training Effectiveness after 70 Bond; its HP direction fits both damage and Barriers.
maid-twohander.tier_reason: The S+ PvE / S PvP ratings fit broad support plus scaling area damage, especially where repeated incoming attacks shorten her ultimate cooldown. Her support is still targeted protection and DEF Up, not an all-purpose heal/cleanse package.
maid-twohander.investment: Take the two level-6 cooldown upgrades before expensive basic damage; balance Barrier strength against ultimate damage according to role. No unique potentials are listed. Passive final-level HP and guaranteed area-hit Chill require their respective upgrades. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
maid-twohander.pve_note: Excellent kit fit for sustained waves and encounters where survivable area attacks feed repeated ultimates. If enemies never attack Emily, discount the cooldown response and judge her on targeted protection and HP-scaling damage. Mogulus checks for missing Barriers when applying Fallen Will, giving her targeted protection a concrete encounter use.
maid-twohander.pvp_note: Can protect a carry before burst if she acts in time and threaten later area turns. She cannot cleanse that carry or force opponents to attack her, so speed order and a separate sustain/control answer matter.

kit_explanation.name: Commence Combat Cleanup
kit_explanation.explanation: Commence Combat Cleanup hits one enemy with ATK and maximum-HP scaling and adds Chill. Nova adds Toughness damage and a one-turn self Barrier based on HP. It is not a listed heal.

kit_explanation.name: Cleaning Service
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Cleaning Service gives one ally ATK Up and an HP-based Barrier for three turns, adds three Chill to Emily, and gives Emily an extra turn. The target does not receive the extra turn. No cleanse is listed despite the introductory wording; level 6 improves cooldown.

kit_explanation.name: Turn-Down Service
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 8 turns, falling to 7 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Turn-Down Service attacks all enemies with ATK and HP scaling, gives the party DEF Up for two turns and adds Awakened Memory to Emily. Each Memory stack increases ultimate damage by 50%, up to three stacks. If Chill is full after the attack, it spends all Chill and reduces this skill's cooldown by two turns. The newly gained Memory should not be assumed to boost the hit that grants it.

kit_explanation.name: Ready Maid
kit_explanation.explanation: Ready Maid starts the first battle with a one-turn HP-based self Barrier. Being attacked reduces Turn-Down Service's cooldown by one; an attack targeting everyone reduces it by one additional turn and can add Chill. That Chill chance rises from 50% to 100% across passive levels, which also add up to 15% HP. These are automatic responses, not extra casts.

pros: Targeted ATK buff and Barrier come with Emily's own extra turn.
Incoming attacks reduce a powerful area ultimate's cooldown.
HP investment helps protection, damage and survival together.
Turn-Down Service gives the entire party two turns of DEF Up.
cons: No actual cleanse or ordinary heal is listed.
No Taunt guarantees attacks into her cooldown engine.
Ultimate starts on a long cooldown and grows stronger over repeated uses.

teams.name: Protected caster (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily protects Carnelia, Ceres heals/cleanses, and Seira supplies offensive turn support.
teams.playstyle: Shield the exposed carry, use Emily's extra turn for useful damage, and keep recovery available after a heavy area hit.

teams.name: Marked carry cover (theorycraft)
teams.why: Carnelia can feed Lydia's marked-ally engine while Emily shields the linked pair and Ceres heals.
teams.playstyle: Verify Carnelia is Lydia's highest-ATK other ally; Emily's Barrier should protect whichever of the two is actually threatened.

alternatives.why: Wedding Carmen is higher-rated in PvP and offers Oath-based damage sharing, reactive heal/Barrier and turn progress for a marked ally.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not reproduce Emily's scaling area ultimate or targeted ATK buff; obtain/build the separate variant only if that protection role fits better.

alternatives.why: Maid Ceres is higher-rated in PvP and a stronger fit when the missing job is actual healing and cleansing.
alternatives.tradeoff: Replacing Emily loses a proactive targeted Barrier and her area-damage engine; Ceres is often a complementary partner rather than a direct substitute.

maid-twohander.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

kingdom-knight.summary:
Charlotte mixes single-target damage with a buff for one ally. Vow of Victory gives CRIT Rate Up, an upgrade-dependent ATK buff and an extra turn for Charlotte herself. Unyielding Strike weakens enemy ATK, advances Charlotte's next turn and gradually improves her basic through the higher-level passive.

Use Charlotte (Monastir Knights) as a modest offensive supporter when one ally benefits from both ATK and critical chance. At maximum level Vow of Victory gives 30% of each for two turns, followed by Charlotte’s own extra turn. Her attacks add focused damage and an ATK Down attempt. This is a different job from Charlotte (Heart of Monastir): she does not share that variant’s repeated-basic engine. Keep a healer or protector alongside her rather than counting the buff as survival support.
kingdom-knight.watch: Vow of Victory does not give the target an immediate turn. At low skill levels its ATK buff can fail, and her ramp requires repeated ultimate uses. She has no listed healing, Barrier or area damage.
kingdom-knight.dependency_note: Use her beside an attacker who needs CRIT Rate and ATK, with a healer covering survival. Pairing only with fully self-buffed attackers wastes much of Vow's value.

skill_order.name: Vow of Victory
skill_order.why: Invest here first if Charlotte is selected as a buffer: cooldown levels 6/10 and ATK-buff reliability through level 9.

skill_order.name: Unyielding Strike
skill_order.why: For damage/support hybrid use, take level 6 for cooldown and eventually level 10 for more turn progress.

skill_order.name: Unshaken Grand Master
skill_order.why: Passive improvements support the repeated-ultimate ramp; level 1 does not contain that whole loop.

skill_order.name: Honest Thrust
skill_order.why: Raise basic damage after the utility milestones, especially in a longer fight.

rotation: Use Vow of Victory on the carry who actually needs its buffs, then spend Charlotte's own extra turn on Unyielding Strike if appropriate.
Use Unyielding Strike when ATK Down can reduce an important enemy's pressure; its repeated uses build Honest Thrust's later damage.
Fill with Honest Thrust. Do not wait for maximum Ignition just to use Unyielding Strike: its passive stacks come from repeated uses, not consuming full Ignition.

best_partners.why: Charlotte's attacking Sun ultimate feeds Cristelle's Ignition and supplies ATK Down for the chain-damage debuff count.
Carnelia can receive Vow's CRIT Rate and ATK buffs to support an area-damage turn.
Ceres provides healing and cleanse; stagger team ATK Up with Vow rather than assuming duplicate ATK buffs stack.
Emily adds a Barrier for the carry and party DEF Up while Charlotte supplies CRIT Rate.

kingdom-knight.build_tip: SPD helps Charlotte buff before the intended carry; ATK and CRIT stats support her own attacks. Keep enough HP/DEF to complete repeated ultimate cycles rather than chasing raw database ATK. A Clumsy Way to Relieve Desire supports Strength, with two additional Strength during training after 50 Bond; A Knight’s Oath offers Vitality for survival.
kingdom-knight.tier_reason: The A PvE / A+ PvP ratings suit a hybrid with an extra-turn buff sequence and ATK Down, rather than a pure damage leader. Long encounters can realize her basic ramp; short fights mainly value the opening buff and control.
kingdom-knight.investment: Choose a role before spending: Vow cooldown and chance upgrades for a buffer, or Unyielding Strike's cooldown followed by damage for a hybrid. No potentials are listed, and the passive's added mechanics appear by skill level rather than a documented star threshold. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
kingdom-knight.pve_note: Single-target fights allow repeated ultimates to build Honest Thrust, while wave clearing needs an area partner. ATK Down is useful only when applicable; immune enemies leave her as a buff-and-damage slot.
kingdom-knight.pvp_note: Buff a carry before its action when speed order allows, then use Charlotte's extra turn to attack. She cannot cleanse a disabled carry and does not promise an immediate ally turn.

kit_explanation.name: Honest Thrust
kit_explanation.explanation: Honest Thrust attacks one enemy and adds one Ignition. Damage upgrades are somewhat more relevant after the passive's repeated-ultimate basic-damage stacks are active. Nova adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Vow of Victory
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Vow of Victory gives a chosen ally two turns of CRIT Rate Up and attempts two turns of ATK Up, then gives Charlotte an extra turn. ATK Up chance rises from 75% to 100% by level 9; cooldown improvements occur at levels 6 and 10. The extra turn belongs to Charlotte, not the buffed ally.

kit_explanation.name: Unyielding Strike
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 5 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Unyielding Strike attacks one enemy, attempts two turns of ATK Down, adds Ignition and advances Charlotte's next turn by 20%, rising to 30% at level 10. Level 6 shortens the cooldown. Its Nova increases damage and Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Unshaken Grand Master
kit_explanation.explanation: Unshaken Grand Master starts as an ATK increase. At passive level 2 onward, each Ignition stack gives 3% damage dealt on attack, up to five, and each Unyielding Strike adds a basic-damage stack, up to three. That basic boost rises from 6% to 10% per stack at higher passive levels.

pros: Can buff another attacker and still take her own extra action.
ATK Down adds defensive value to the ultimate.
Repeated ultimates improve basics in longer encounters.
Vow grants its extra turn to Charlotte even when she buffs another ally.
cons: ATK Up on Vow is probabilistic until its later upgrades.
No group damage or recovery in the listed kit.
Basic-damage ramp requires multiple long-cooldown ultimate uses.

teams.name: Sun chain support (theorycraft)
teams.why: Cristelle rewards Burn and debuffs, Scarlet adds Burn, and Ceres heals; Charlotte contributes an attacking Sun ultimate and targeted CRIT Rate.
teams.playstyle: Buff the attacker who needs crit support, then use Unyielding Strike; remember Vow itself does not trigger Cristelle's attacking-skill resource.

teams.name: Area carry support (theorycraft)
teams.why: Charlotte supplies CRIT Rate, Emily shields the carry and Ceres restores the team around Carnelia's area damage.
teams.playstyle: Put Vow on Carnelia before a damage turn if she needs it, and avoid overlapping every ATK buff with no gain in uptime.

alternatives.why: Seira is a higher-rated support attacker whose ally buff gives Greater ATK Up and progress toward the ally's next turn.
alternatives.tradeoff: Seira does not grant Vow's CRIT Rate Up; building her is a separate resource commitment, not a free substitution.

alternatives.why: Emily brings higher-rated general utility through a targeted ATK buff and Barrier, plus party DEF Up and area damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: She replaces offensive crit support with protection and has no listed ordinary healing or cleansing.

kingdom-knight.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

kingdom-shielder.summary:
Carmen in her ordinary knight variant is an HP-scaling defender who tries to force one enemy into a basic attack through Taunt. Her ultimate also gives everyone DEF Up, while Shock Therapy reinforces her own DEF and Effect Hit. Chill makes her tougher at higher passive levels.

Use her when three turns of party DEF Up and single-target Taunt address the incoming threat. HP, DEF and speed support that job more directly than attack stats. A healer such as original Frey still needs to restore damage Carmen draws. Against Taunt immunity, evaluate the party buff alone before committing further resources to this defensive slot.
kingdom-shielder.watch: She has no normal heal, Barrier or damage-sharing Guard in this variant. Taunt cannot be treated as guaranteed control against resistance or immunity. Composed Response is internally inconsistent: its description and effect record disagree on counterattack conditions and rates.
kingdom-shielder.dependency_note: She needs a healer because drawing attacks does not restore HP. Pairing with a damage dealer who needs DEF Up makes more sense than stacking several protectors without enough damage.

skill_order.name: Monastir Mobile Bulwark
skill_order.why: First obtain the party DEF skill's level-6 cooldown and levels 4/8 Taunt chance when enemies are susceptible.

skill_order.name: Shock Therapy
skill_order.why: Then improve Rule of Monastir access and the second Taunt attempt.

skill_order.name: Knights' Shield
skill_order.why: Passive HP and Chill-based defense help her survive the attacks she attracts.

skill_order.name: Knights Standard Swordsmanship
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a low priority on a defensive build.

rotation: Use Monastir Mobile Bulwark for party DEF Up when a group hit is coming, selecting a Taunt-susceptible threat.
Use Shock Therapy to reinforce Carmen or attempt to redirect a different dangerous turn; avoid wasting both Taunts on a target already controlled for that turn.
Use Knights Standard Swordsmanship to build Chill during gaps. Heal Carmen before she absorbs more forced attacks; do not rely on the disputed counterattack potential.

best_partners.why: Ceres supplies the healing and cleansing Carmen lacks, with party ATK Up to compensate for a defensive slot.
Frey heals and shields Carmen, and can fully cleanse the defender when control threatens her next Taunt.
Carnelia supplies area damage and Buff Block while party DEF Up reduces incoming pressure.
Bell provides buff removal and Silence, giving control options beyond a single Taunt.

kingdom-shielder.build_tip: HP improves both durability and attack scaling; add DEF, SPD for buff uptime and Effect Hit if Taunt is usable. Do not substitute effect investment for survival or assume Rule makes Taunt unavoidable. Journey option: A Drowsy Afternoon Interlude is Vitality-tagged, supporting HP for recovery or HP scaling; its listed training effectiveness is +8% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
kingdom-shielder.tier_reason: The B PvE / C+ PvP ratings fit a straightforward defender with no ordinary heal or Barrier, reliant on susceptible targets for redirection. Party DEF Up still has value when Taunt fails, but stronger protectors combine more functions.
kingdom-shielder.investment: Get the party-defense cooldown milestone before damage. Composed Response's main description says 25% counter chance with Rule and 100% against a Taunted attacker, while its effect text says 25% against Taunt. Treat the rate as unresolved; no exact potential unlock threshold is supported. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. Wedding March belongs to Wedding Carmen in savior_sources and is excluded from this ordinary build. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 6 at level 120, listing +8 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
kingdom-shielder.pve_note: Use her when DEF Up and a single Taunt meaningfully reduce damage. Against Taunt immunity she is mostly an HP-scaling attacker with a party defense buff and needs to justify that slot.
kingdom-shielder.pvp_note: She can redirect a susceptible enemy's next turn, but accuracy/resistance checks, cleansing and burst can defeat that plan. Her lower published PvP rating is consistent with that limited protection rather than proof she can never work.

kit_explanation.name: Knights Standard Swordsmanship
kit_explanation.explanation: Knights Standard Swordsmanship hits one enemy using ATK and maximum HP, and adds Chill. Nova adds Toughness damage and a short Rule of Monastir buff, which improves DEF and Effect Hit.

kit_explanation.name: Shock Therapy
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Shock Therapy attacks one enemy with HP scaling, grants two turns of Rule of Monastir and attempts one turn of Taunt. The listed chance rises from 75% to 100% through levels 4 and 8. Taunt makes a susceptible target use its basic against Carmen; it is not a universal boss interrupt.

kit_explanation.name: Monastir Mobile Bulwark
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Monastir Mobile Bulwark attacks one enemy with HP scaling and attempts Taunt, while giving the whole party DEF Up for three turns. It has the same chance upgrades and a level-6 cooldown reduction. Despite its name, the listed skill does not give a Barrier.

kit_explanation.name: Knights' Shield
kit_explanation.explanation: Knights' Shield adds HP, from 5% to 15%. From passive level 2 onward, Chill also increases Carmen's DEF when she is attacked, growing from 2% to 4% per stack up to five. This reinforces personal durability but does not redirect damage away from allies by itself.

pros: Party DEF Up lasts three turns in the stored description.
Two separate skills attempt Taunt.
HP investment supports both survival and attack scaling.
Chill provides additional personal defense at upgraded passive levels.
cons: No ordinary healing or Barrier in this variant.
Taunt-based protection can fail or be immune.
Unique-potential counterattack data conflicts, so its reliability is unknown.

teams.name: Basic defense core (theorycraft)
teams.why: Frey supplies recovery and Barriers while Carnelia and Bell provide damage and control; Carmen contributes DEF Up and targeted Taunt.
teams.playstyle: Shield before group pressure, Taunt only a meaningful target and leave Frey's cleanse ready for a disabled ally.

teams.name: Sustained control (theorycraft)
teams.why: Ceres supplies group sustain, Bell strips buffs and Silences, and Kyra can exploit Silence while Carmen covers DEF Up.
teams.playstyle: Stagger control rather than spending every effect on the same already-controlled enemy; heal Carmen after successful redirection.

alternatives.why: Wedding Carmen is higher-rated and offers marked-ally damage sharing, reactive healing/Barrier and turn progress plus broader sustain.
alternatives.tradeoff: This is a separate profile with a separate build, and its protection follows the Oath recipient rather than Carmen's ordinary Taunt plan.

alternatives.why: Emily is higher-rated and combines a targeted Barrier/ATK buff, an extra turn and scaling area damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not force enemy targeting and is not an ordinary healer; a sustain slot may still be required.

kingdom-shielder.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

kingdom-pray.summary:
Frey is an HP-scaling healer with two different jobs: Rapid Resupply fully cleanses one ally, while Monastir's All-Out Support heals and shields the group. Star allies receive more healing. At higher passive levels maximum Leap also turns her basic into an automatic small party recovery and self turn-progress tool.

Choose Frey for prevention plus targeted rescue: a three-turn party Barrier handles predictable pressure, while Rapid Resupply removes every removable debuff from one ally. HP improves both recovery and barriers, with speed helping those effects arrive in time. Her group heal is not a group cleanse, and a Star bonus is secondary to filling the team’s missing roles.
kingdom-pray.watch: Her party ultimate does not directly remove debuffs. The all-debuff removal is single-target, and the passive's healing/turn-progress mechanics are absent from its level-1 description. Effect RES Up is resistance, not immunity.
kingdom-pray.dependency_note: Star allies get extra healing, but she can heal any attribute. Choose her for Barrier coverage and one-target cleansing rather than filling a team with Star units that have no other synergy.

skill_order.name: Monastir's All-Out Support
skill_order.why: Get level 6 for more frequent group defense; later healing and level-10 Barrier strength matter when group damage is the problem.

skill_order.name: Rapid Resupply
skill_order.why: Prioritize this first instead if one-target cleansing is the encounter's main requirement.

skill_order.name: No-Loss Deal
skill_order.why: Passive improvements enable the Leap/basic-heal loop beyond its simple level-1 HP increase.

skill_order.name: Negotiation Failed
skill_order.why: Basic damage is last; the healing trigger does not require expensive damage upgrades.

rotation: Use Rapid Resupply on the ally whose debuffs or HP threaten their next useful action.
Use Monastir's All-Out Support before a dangerous group hit for Barriers, or after damage for recovery and the conditional allied turn-progress bonus.
When no urgent support skill is needed, use Negotiation Failed with the unlocked passive and full Leap to gain its automatic group heal. Do not treat the ultimate as a party cleanse.

best_partners.why: Haydee shares damage and needs healing; Frey's enhanced Star-ally recovery and full cleanse help keep the protector functioning.
Dana is a Star attacker who receives stronger healing and adds ally ATK support that Frey lacks.
Bell benefits from enhanced Star healing, while providing Silence and buff removal in return.
Emily supplies offensive support and area damage; Frey supplies the healing and cleansing Emily does not actually list.

kingdom-pray.build_tip: HP improves heals and Barriers; add SPD so cleansing arrives before an ally loses value, then DEF/resistance. Her listed maximum 42,251 HP is a database endpoint rather than an attainable guarantee at equal account cost. Journey option: The Princess Ascends the Throne is Vitality-tagged, supporting HP for recovery or HP scaling; its listed training effectiveness is +11% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
kingdom-pray.tier_reason: Her B/B ratings reflect a useful basic sustain package with limited offensive support and a long party cooldown. She can still fit targeted-cleanse or Barrier needs; broad heal/cleanse/turn-support alternatives offer more utility in demanding encounters.
kingdom-pray.investment: Spend first on the relevant heal, especially the ultimate's level-6 cooldown, before basic damage. No unique potentials are listed. No-Loss Deal's basic-trigger healing is a higher passive-level feature, not a proven zero-star baseline. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 6 at level 120, listing +8 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
kingdom-pray.pve_note: Good for a single heavily debuffed ally or a predictable group hit. Choose group cleanse elsewhere when several allies need multiple debuffs removed at once; do not overvalue the Star bonus over essential team roles.
kingdom-pray.pvp_note: Barriers can cushion an opening and Rapid Resupply can rescue a controlled ally if Frey acts. Resistance does not guarantee prevention, and she may be too late without appropriate speed and bulk.

kit_explanation.name: Negotiation Failed
kit_explanation.explanation: Negotiation Failed is the basic attack and adds Leap. At the appropriate passive level it can trigger group healing when it leaves Leap full. Nova gives a two-turn HP-based Barrier to the ally with the lowest current HP ratio and adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Rapid Resupply
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 3 turns. Rapid Resupply heals one ally based on Frey's maximum HP, removes all that ally's debuffs and adds two Leap to Frey. Its healing is increased on a Star ally; the effect lists a 20% incoming-healing bonus for that use. This is the emergency cleanse, not the ultimate.

kit_explanation.name: Monastir's All-Out Support
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 5 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Monastir's All-Out Support heals everyone, grants a three-turn HP-based Barrier and two turns of Effect RES Up, and adds two Leap to Frey. Star recipients receive a larger heal, with a separate listed 30% bonus. Level 6 improves cooldown and level 10 improves Barrier strength. It does not list a direct cleanse.

kit_explanation.name: No-Loss Deal
kit_explanation.explanation: No-Loss Deal begins as a 5% HP increase. At level 2 onward it adds Leap each turn and, after Negotiation Failed reaches maximum Leap, spends the stacks to advance Frey's next turn by 30% and heal everyone. It also conditionally advances allied turns when using the ultimate with an ally at 75% HP or below, rising from 9% to 15%. The multi-target wording does not establish repeated gauge gains per injured ally.

pros: Full debuff removal on a chosen ally.
Group heal, Barrier and resistance in one ultimate.
Higher passive levels add basic-triggered group recovery.
Her Nova basic shields the lowest-HP-ratio ally.
cons: No direct party cleanse in the ultimate.
Little offensive support compared with stronger sustain options.
Long group cooldown and a passive loop dependent on investment.

teams.name: Star sustain core (theorycraft)
teams.why: Haydee protects the team, Dana deals area damage and shares ATK Up, and Bell adds dispel/Silence; all three qualify for Frey's Star healing bonus.
teams.playstyle: Use Rapid Resupply on Haydee after shared damage or on a controlled attacker, and reserve the group Barrier for known pressure.

teams.name: Shielded area carry (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily shields Carnelia or Bell; Frey heals, cleanses one ally and adds group Barriers around two damage/control slots.
teams.playstyle: Protect the exposed carry before incoming damage, then cleanse the ally whose next action is most important.

alternatives.why: Maid Ceres is higher-rated general sustain with repeatable conditional party cleansing and a direct team ATK buff.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her ordinary cleanse removes one debuff at a time; Frey's full one-target removal and group Barriers remain distinct. Only switch if you can obtain and invest in the separate profile.

alternatives.why: Waltz Asherah offers two-debuff party cleansing, healing and progress toward other allies' next turns.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not reproduce Frey's group Barrier or Star-specific heal bonus; changing healers costs a separate build.

kingdom-pray.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

nightmare-reaper.summary:
Seira is a support attacker who gives one ally Greater ATK Up and progress toward its next turn, then gains an extra turn herself. She can follow with single-target damage and SPD Down. Her unique potential, if obtained, turns the non-attacking buff skill into additional Nova Force and personal Toughness damage.

Choose Seira when the carry needs a stronger ATK buff and help reaching its next turn. Starlit Butterflies grants 50% ATK and 25% Action gauge to one ally, while the extra turn belongs to Seira. She can immediately follow with an attack rather than losing her whole turn to setup. Build her to act before that carry, then preserve enough durability to repeat the buff. She supplies neither healing nor a Barrier, so another slot must handle survival.
nightmare-reaper.watch: The buff is for one ally and the extra turn belongs to Seira. Her ultimate spends all Insight even below maximum; it receives the 20% damage bonus only at full stacks. Greater ATK Up should not be assumed to stack additively with every ordinary ATK buff.
nightmare-reaper.dependency_note: Choose a carry whose next attack benefits from a stronger ATK buff and turn progress. Seira supplies no listed healing or Barrier, so a sustain/protection partner remains important.

skill_order.name: Starlit Butterflies
skill_order.why: Prioritize the support skill: level-6/10 cooldowns and its ally turn-progress improvements.

skill_order.name: Invitation to the Phantasm
skill_order.why: Then improve damage on the single-target follow-up if she contributes meaningful damage.

skill_order.name: Blessing of Premonition
skill_order.why: Passive levels support damage into healthy targets but do not improve Greater ATK Up.

skill_order.name: Fleeting Dream
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a lower priority than enabling the actual carry.

rotation: Use Starlit Butterflies before the carry's useful damage window, then spend Seira's extra turn deliberately.

If Insight is already full, Invitation to the Phantasm gains its bonus. Starting from empty, Butterflies gives only three stacks; use a basic or accept a below-full ultimate if urgent rather than claiming the bonus is automatic.
Use Fleeting Dream during gaps. With Butterfly's Lullaby actually obtained, the buff skill automatically grants Nova Force and Sweet Dream; do not queue the potential as a manual cast.

best_partners.why: Carnelia can turn Greater ATK Up and ally turn progress into an earlier or stronger area-damage window.
Lydia benefits from offensive support, and Seira can instead buff Lydia's marked attacker to help its turns; verify who receives Passing the Buck separately.
Emily shields the chosen carry and adds party DEF Up while Seira supplies stronger offensive support.
Ceres supplies healing and cleanse, leaving Seira free to use her non-attacking support skill.

nightmare-reaper.build_tip: SPD to act before the intended carry, then enough HP/DEF to survive and ATK/crit if using hybrid damage. Her listed maximum 107 SPD and five Toughness are source traits, not proof of actual turn order. When Slumber Comes Calling supports Vitality and adds one Vitality during training after 40 Bond. Include Strength if Seira is also expected to deal meaningful damage.
nightmare-reaper.tier_reason: The A+ PvE / S PvP ratings fit strong targeted offensive support and flexible extra-turn sequencing. Her rating case is enabling a carry, not claiming her single-target ultimate matches dedicated area attackers or works optimally in every opener.
nightmare-reaper.investment: Starlit Butterflies' cooldown and ally turn-progress upgrades come first. Butterfly's Lullaby, if obtained, grants two Nova Force after a non-attacking skill and three turns of Sweet Dream, whose effect increases her Toughness damage by one. No reliable acquisition or star threshold is supplied. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
nightmare-reaper.pve_note: Supports a chosen damage dealer and can add SPD Down to a susceptible boss. Do not delay the carry's useful buff window just to maximize Seira's own Insight damage.
nightmare-reaper.pvp_note: Targeted turn progress can help a carry act sooner, while Seira's own extra turn permits follow-up pressure. It does not guarantee that carry moves immediately or bypass enemy control.

kit_explanation.name: Fleeting Dream
kit_explanation.explanation: Fleeting Dream hits one enemy and adds one Insight. Insight's ordinary attribute bonus is against Chaos enemies. Nova adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Starlit Butterflies
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Starlit Butterflies gives a chosen ally two turns of Greater ATK Up, listed as 50% ATK, and advances that ally's next turn by 10%, rising to 25% by level 9. It grants Seira three Insight and an extra turn. Levels 6/10 shorten cooldown. Nova additionally restores her Toughness and advances her own next turn by 50%; that Nova progress is not an extra 50% for the ally.

kit_explanation.name: Invitation to the Phantasm
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns. Invitation to the Phantasm hits one enemy, attempts two turns of SPD Down and gives Seira Light of the Phantasm, a two-turn ATK/SPD buff. At full Insight it deals 20% more damage; it removes all Insight after attacking. No ordinary cooldown reduction appears in its upgrade track.

kit_explanation.name: Blessing of Premonition
kit_explanation.explanation: Blessing of Premonition increases ATK. From level 2 onward it also increases damage against an enemy at 75% HP or above, rising from 9% to 15%. That opening-health bonus does not last for every attack once the target's HP falls.

pros: Strong targeted ATK support with allied next-turn progress.
Support cast grants Seira an extra turn instead of ending her contribution.
Obtained unique potential links her non-attacking skill to Nova resources and Toughness damage.
Light of the Phantasm increases her own ATK and SPD by 15%.
cons: No healing, cleanse or Barrier.
Only single-target damage in the listed attacks.
Ultimate consumes Insight even when its full-stack bonus is unavailable.

teams.name: Area carry accelerator (theorycraft)
teams.why: Seira strengthens and advances Carnelia, Emily supplies a Barrier and Ceres covers healing/cleansing.
teams.playstyle: Time Butterflies before Carnelia's desired attack, then use Seira's extra action without assuming the ally's turn is immediate.

teams.name: Linked offense (theorycraft)
teams.why: Carnelia can be Lydia's marked attacker, Seira accelerates the relevant attacker, and Ceres supplies sustain.
teams.playstyle: Verify Carnelia receives the highest-ATK mark, then use Butterflies to support a useful attack; Lydia still needs five Clocking Out and an available skill.

alternatives.why: Emily has a higher PvE rating and supplies a targeted ATK buff with Barrier, party DEF Up and area damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: She gives ordinary ATK Up rather than Seira's Greater ATK Up and does not advance the buffed ally's turn; a separate build changes the role.

alternatives.why: Waltz Asherah is higher-rated in PvE and offers healing, two-debuff party cleansing and allied turn progress when sustain is the missing job.
alternatives.tradeoff: She lacks Seira's targeted Greater ATK Up; compare team needs and existing investment rather than treating every support as interchangeable.

nightmare-reaper.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

stellar-thief.summary:
Trish is a single-target finisher who builds Leap, advances her own turns and spends stacks on DEF penetration. Killing with Continuous Cuts resets that skill, so choosing a finishable target is more important than using the ultimate as soon as it lights up.

Her best target is one she can actually finish, rather than simply the enemy with the highest defense. Three upgraded opening Leap plus the special’s two stacks prepare maximum penetration, but the 50% action fill does not promise an immediate turn. Invest in dependable critical hits and enough protection to reach that window. Bosses without adds offer fewer reset opportunities.
stellar-thief.watch: No kill means no full reset. Her upgraded opening stacks and kill rewards are absent at passive level 1, and a 50% gauge fill means progress toward another turn, not an explicit extra turn.
stellar-thief.dependency_note: She can build her own stacks and buffs, but teammates that soften targets or protect her make kill-based resets more plausible.

skill_order.name: Continuous Cuts
skill_order.why: Levels 6 and 10 reduce the expensive ultimate cooldown; damage upgrades help reach a kill.

skill_order.name: Top-Tier Hunter
skill_order.why: Later passive levels add opening Leap, accuracy and rewards on defeat, rather than just CRIT DMG.

skill_order.name: Accelerated Assault
skill_order.why: Accelerated Assault supplies critical chance, two Leap and turn progress regardless of enemy debuffs.

skill_order.name: Phantom Step
skill_order.why: Use as stack filler; damage investment follows the finisher and passive.

rotation: Use Accelerated Assault to gain two Leap, CRIT Rate Up and 50% progress toward the next turn. With upgraded Top-Tier Hunter’s three opening stacks, this can prepare five Leap without assuming a star threshold.
Aim Continuous Cuts at a target that is both worth removing and realistically within reach. It ignores Preemptive Guard and consumes Leap for 10% DEF penetration per stack, up to five.
If the target survives at 25% HP or below, the skill shortens its cooldown by one rather than resetting. A kill resets it; rebuild Leap with the passive reward/basic/special before the next finisher.
Use Phantom Step when setup or cooldowns demand it; do not give up a necessary early kill solely to reach maximum penetration.
