best_partners.why: Cleaning Service adds ATK Up and a Barrier to improve Trish’s survival and finishing damage.
Area damage can soften targets while dispel and Isolation reduce enemy protection before Trish commits.
Oath protects Trish if she is highest ATK; healing and Barriers help keep the finisher alive.

stellar-thief.build_tip: ATK and critical stats, counting Accelerated Assault’s 30% CRIT Rate buff. SPD helps secure a finishing window; preserve enough HP/DEF to survive before the first kill. Journey option: Choosing the Next Prey is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +5% at Arcana level 1. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
stellar-thief.tier_reason: The low PvE and modest PvP ratings fit a narrow execute specialist whose best recycling needs kills. Preemptive Guard bypass and stack-based penetration can matter in PvP, but do not turn an unfed Trish into a universal tank killer.
stellar-thief.investment: Continuous Cuts level 6/10 cooldown upgrades reduce punishment when a kill fails. Confirm Top-Tier Hunter’s later-level opening stacks before planning the fast five-Leap setup. No unique potential is listed. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
stellar-thief.pve_note: Can chain through weakened enemies when her own hit secures kills. A boss without adds offers fewer reset opportunities, so the long ultimate cycle matters more.
stellar-thief.pvp_note: Choose a vulnerable carry instead of blindly hitting the toughest target. Enemy survival, damage reduction and turn order can deny the kill and therefore the reset.

kit_explanation.name: Phantom Step
kit_explanation.explanation: Phantom Step is a single-target basic granting one Leap. Use it as stack filler while stronger actions cool down; its Nova Burst adds one Toughness damage rather than extra Leap.

kit_explanation.name: Accelerated Assault
kit_explanation.explanation: Accelerated Assault attacks one enemy on a listed two-turn cooldown, adds two Leap and gives two-turn CRIT Rate Up plus 50% progress toward Trish’s next turn. It prepares the finisher without relying on a kill.

kit_explanation.name: Continuous Cuts
kit_explanation.explanation: Continuous Cuts has a listed six-turn cooldown with reductions at levels 6 and 10. It ignores Preemptive Guard, spends Leap for up to 50% DEF penetration and gives ATK Up. A target left at or below 25% HP shortens cooldown by one; defeating it resets the skill.

kit_explanation.name: Top-Tier Hunter
kit_explanation.explanation: Top-Tier Hunter initially gives only CRIT DMG. Higher levels add three opening Leap, 50% attack accuracy and kill rewards of turn progress plus three Leap. The gauge reward rises from 20% to 30%; these are passive rewards, not separate selectable actions.

pros: Preemptive Guard bypass gives her a specific protected-target niche.
Special supplies stack setup and substantial turn progress.
A successful ultimate kill refreshes the finisher for another opportunity.
At five Leap, the ultimate reaches its listed 50% DEF penetration.
cons: Reset depends on her actually defeating the target.
Long fallback cooldown when the enemy survives.
No innate party protection or healing.

teams.name: Protected finisher
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Emily buffs Trish, Ceres softens/disrupts targets and Frey heals or cleanses her.
teams.playstyle: Set up critical chance and Leap, then finish an exposed enemy; do not assume every target is killable.

teams.name: Single carry recovery
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Carmen protects the highest-ATK carry, Elisa offers revival and Lydia slows key opponents.
teams.playstyle: Use slows to create a finishing chance and keep rescue available if the first attempt fails.

alternatives.why: Amora is a higher-rated offensive choice with area damage, an explicit extra turn and conditional self-cleanse.
alternatives.tradeoff: Trish retains direct Preemptive Guard bypass and kill-based ultimate resets.

alternatives.why: Roberta is higher-rated and offers reaction pressure plus personal cleanse against area attackers.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not reproduce Trish’s Leap-based DEF penetration or kill-reset finisher.

stellar-thief.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

eastern-swordmaster.summary:
Lyn is a Star attacker with two purposeful branches. Phantom Blade Dance first grants Bright Moon for a stronger focused ultimate; Clear Wind Bright Moon first stays area damage and grants Star-team crit-damage support plus Clear Wind, enabling later Leap support. Skill order changes what the team gets.

Choose Lyn when one damage slot must handle waves and a surviving priority target. Her two forms reward different orders: Bright Moon turns the ultimate into a focused hit with extra critical damage and Toughness damage, while Clear Wind supports Star allies and shortens her special cooldown after her own-turn special. The paired extra turns require the other cooldown skill to be usable. Check both buttons before committing rather than assuming every cast starts a free chain.
eastern-swordmaster.watch: The same ultimate name can describe an area or single-target form. Do not promise both branches' team buffs and focused damage in one action. Extra turns require the other cooldown skill to be usable; they are not unconditional or infinite.
eastern-swordmaster.dependency_note: She can run a personal focused-damage branch alone, but the support branch specifically rewards other Star allies who use Leap or crit damage. Choose the branch for the fight rather than automatically stacking identical attributes.

skill_order.name: Clear Wind Bright Moon
skill_order.why: Upgrade the main attack used in either branch; damage upgrades apply without inventing cooldown milestones not listed in ordinary levels.

skill_order.name: Phantom Blade Dance
skill_order.why: Improves the area attack and complements branch sequencing; utility comes from the actual stance and cooldown availability.

skill_order.name: Fivefold Slash
skill_order.why: Basic damage is later, though its Leap and Nova SPD Up support downtime.

rotation: For a priority single target, use Phantom Blade Dance without Clear Wind to gain ATK Up and Bright Moon; if the ultimate is available the skill grants an extra turn, letting you use its focused form.

For waves or Star-team support, use Clear Wind Bright Moon without Bright Moon to keep its area form, buff other Star allies' CRIT DMG and gain Clear Wind; if the special is available it grants an extra turn.
In Clear Wind, Phantom Blade Dance supplies three Leap to Star allies instead of its Bright Moon setup. In Bright Moon, the ultimate becomes single-target with extra critical and Toughness damage.
Watch active states and actual cooldowns before each action. Use Fivefold Slash for Leap when neither branch action is available; Nova can provide a brief SPD Up.

best_partners.why: Lyn's Clear Wind special can give Tanya three Leap toward Demolition Mode; the team crit-damage buff also supports Tanya's attacks.
Star Mina can receive distributed Leap to reach her special's extra-Bleed condition and CRIT DMG support for her direct attacks.
Kingdom Frey supplies healing, a full single-target cleanse and party barriers, with increased recovery for Star allies such as Lyn.

eastern-swordmaster.build_tip: Build reliable CRIT Rate before heavy CRIT DMG, then ATK and SPD. Leap adds passive ATK on attack; Bright Moon's critical payoff still requires a crit. Stored 106 SPD does not guarantee the desired sequence against geared opponents. Under the Glass Moon, Over the Pavilion supports Strength and adds one Strength during training after 70 Bond.
eastern-swordmaster.tier_reason: The stored S+ PvE / S PvP ratings fit wave/focused flexibility, conditional extra turns and meaningful Star support. PvE allows branch planning; PvP rewards immediate appropriate targeting but can disrupt cooldown and stance timing. No tested optimal rotation is claimed.
eastern-swordmaster.investment: Ordinary attack upgrades are damage nodes rather than listed level-based cooldown reductions. Blade Dancer supplies conditional one-turn cooldown reductions tied to the matching state; its per-Leap ATK increases from 2% to 4% across passive levels with later base ATK additions. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
eastern-swordmaster.pve_note: Choose area/support first for waves or Star allies that need Leap; choose Bright Moon setup first for a durable priority target. Do not infer a fixed number of hits or breaks from the cinematic skill name or stored attack coefficient.
eastern-swordmaster.pvp_note: Use the branch that addresses the actual enemy arrangement. Focused form sacrifices area coverage; support form sacrifices that focused critical bonus. A conditional extra turn is valuable but can fail to occur if the paired skill is unavailable.

kit_explanation.name: Fivefold Slash
kit_explanation.explanation: Fivefold Slash is a single-target basic adding one Leap. Leap modestly boosts damage against Moon enemies and supplies Blade Dancer's on-attack ATK scaling. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and one-turn SPD Up.

kit_explanation.name: Phantom Blade Dance
kit_explanation.explanation: Phantom Blade Dance attacks all enemies on a five-turn cooldown. With Clear Wind, it grants three Leap to Star allies. Without Clear Wind, it gives Lyn three-turn ATK Up and Bright Moon. If used on her own turn with Clear Wind Bright Moon usable afterward, it grants an extra turn. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Clear Wind Bright Moon
kit_explanation.explanation: Clear Wind Bright Moon has a five-turn cooldown. Without Bright Moon it attacks all enemies, grants two-turn CRIT DMG Up to other Star allies and gives Lyn three-turn Clear Wind, a SPD buff. With Bright Moon it instead attacks one enemy with 50% extra CRIT DMG and one extra Toughness damage. If Phantom Blade Dance is usable afterward on her own turn, it grants an extra turn. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Blade Dancer
kit_explanation.explanation: Blade Dancer adds 2–4% ATK per Leap on attack, capped at five stacks, depending on passive level. After her own-turn Phantom Blade Dance with Clear Wind it shortens that skill's cooldown by one; after her own-turn ultimate with Bright Moon it shortens that cooldown by one. Higher levels add ATK. These are state-conditioned reductions, not an unconditional refresh.

pros: Can choose area support or stronger focused damage through actual skill order.
Clear Wind branch distributes Leap and crit damage support to Star allies.
Conditional extra turns can connect the two skills when both are ready.
Her special can distribute three Leap to other Star allies in Clear Wind.
cons: Wrong branch can trade away needed wave coverage or team buffs.
Extra turns depend on paired-skill availability.
No healing, cleanse or protection, and focused critical payoff needs reliable crits.

teams.name: Star Leap support
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Tanya receives Leap toward Demolition Mode and Star crit support; Emily protects Lyn, while Kingdom Frey heals and cleanses with Star recovery bonuses.
teams.playstyle: Use the area/Clear Wind branch when Tanya needs resources, then leave a useful break for Tanya rather than following a rigid damage script.

teams.name: Star wave pressure
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Mina uses Star Leap and critical support, Hilde shields the opening and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Select the support branch for wave damage and Leap; switch to focused setup for the durable survivor when the states/cooldowns allow.

alternatives.why: Rosaria is a higher-rated PvP sidegrade when immediate area DEF Down, 50% turn progress and a one-time survival safeguard matter.
alternatives.tradeoff: Lyn retains Star support and deliberate focused-form critical damage; Rosaria does not supply her Leap distribution.

alternatives.why: Professor M is a sidegrade for carrying one powerful basic attacker through dual attacks and special vulnerability.
alternatives.tradeoff: Lyn supplies her own flexible damage and Star buffs, while Professor M needs relative-ATK tuning and allied attacks.

eastern-swordmaster.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

incognita-landgrave.summary:
Cristelle is a Sun debuff-and-chain-damage specialist. Allies' attacking cooldown skills build her Ignition, then Seething Vengeance triggers automatically at maximum stacks to spread Burn and advance her next turn. Her ultimate rewards an already debuffed target with extra chain-damage instances and longer Burn.

Choose Cristelle for a prepared Sun team that attacks with its cooldown skills. One qualifying Sun attack can supply two Ignition, reaching her five-stack reaction faster than a non-attacking support turn. The automatic special spreads two Burn stacks and grants other Sun allies two Ignition. Her ultimate then exploits up to five debuffs on one enemy. ATK supports both direct and Burn damage; Effect Hit supports application, but neither stat removes an encounter’s debuff restrictions.
incognita-landgrave.watch: Seething Vengeance is a React skill, not a button to open with. Chain damage depends on debuffs actually being present; immunity, cleansing and missing Burn reduce the payoff. Its 100% listed chances at high levels do not override immunity.
incognita-landgrave.dependency_note: Other allies must attack to trigger Seething Vengeance. Attacking Sun special/ultimate skills accelerate Ignition more than non-Sun ones; a healer's non-attacking support cast does not meet that condition.

skill_order.name: Seething Vengeance
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves the automatic skill's cooldown; levels 4 and 8 improve Burn chance, and later levels improve turn progress.

skill_order.name: Nightmare Unleashed
skill_order.why: Then improve the level-6 cooldown and damage of the debuff-payoff attack.

skill_order.name: Festering Resentment
skill_order.why: Passive upgrades improve basic-attack turn progress and ATK.

skill_order.name: Vengeance and Retribution
skill_order.why: Basic damage matters in downtime but does not replace the reactive Burn engine.

rotation: Have an attacking Sun partner use a special or ultimate to build Ignition; once maximum stacks are reached, a qualifying ally attack triggers Seething Vengeance automatically if ready.
Use Nightmare Unleashed on an enemy with Burn and several useful debuffs when available; do not spend turns adding irrelevant debuffs just to reach the five-instance cap.
Use Vengeance and Retribution on a debuffed enemy during cooldown gaps. Reserve its Nova Burn for a valuable target when the resource cost is justified.

best_partners.why: Scarlet applies Burn and her attacking Sun cooldown skills feed Cristelle's Ignition; Cristelle can extend Burn on their shared target.
Kyra's Sun cooldown attacks feed Ignition and add Silence and ATK Down for Nightmare Unleashed's debuff count.
Charlotte's Unyielding Strike is an attacking Sun ultimate and adds ATK Down; Vow of Victory is non-attacking and should not be counted as an Ignition trigger.
Ceres supplies healing, cleanse and team ATK Up, but her support skills do not count as attacking Sun cooldown skills.

incognita-landgrave.build_tip: ATK improves attacks, Burn and chain damage. Add SPD and suitable Effect Hit if debuffs are relevant; do not treat CRIT stats as proven scaling for every chain or Burn instance. Bound for Eternity is a Focus fit for Burn application; its unique adds one Focus during training after 40 Bond. Pair it with Strength for ATK-scaled damage.
incognita-landgrave.tier_reason: Her value in both modes comes from ally-triggered Burn, turn progress and chain damage against debuffed enemies. Frequent attacking Sun partners support the loop; immunity and cleansing can remove much of its payoff.
incognita-landgrave.investment: Start with Seething Vengeance's cooldown and Burn-chance milestones, then Nightmare Unleashed's cooldown and ATK investment. No unique potentials are listed. The effect entries commonly show final-level chances, so use current skill descriptions for a less-developed copy. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
incognita-landgrave.pve_note: Strongest on paper when Burn stays active and multiple debuffs can be maintained. Debuff-immune phases remove much of the chain/extension value; use a more direct attacker if that dominates the encounter.
incognita-landgrave.pvp_note: A partner-driven Burn trigger and self turn progress can pressure a team, but enemies can cleanse Burn or prevent the setup. Select targets for meaningful debuffs rather than assuming chain damage wins through every defense.

kit_explanation.name: Vengeance and Retribution
kit_explanation.explanation: Vengeance and Retribution hits one enemy and adds Ignition. Her passive also advances her next turn after this basic and adds chain damage if the target has a debuff. Nova adds a Burn attempt that explicitly ignores Effect RES; that wording still does not establish bypassing debuff immunity.

kit_explanation.name: Seething Vengeance
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 4 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Seething Vengeance automatically checks after another ally's attack when Cristelle has maximum Ignition and the React cooldown permits it. It grants Drive for Revenge, attempts two Burn stacks on every enemy, advances her next turn, gives other Sun allies two Ignition, and spends her own Ignition. Across levels Burn chance rises from 75% to 100% and turn progress from 30% to 50%. Drive for Revenge raises ATK and Effect Hit.

kit_explanation.name: Nightmare Unleashed
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 4 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Nightmare Unleashed hits one enemy, attempts to extend that enemy's Burn by one turn, and adds ATK-based chain damage for each debuff, up to five instances. It also advances Cristelle's next turn by 30%. Prefer a target with established debuffs rather than assuming the ultimate applies Burn itself.

kit_explanation.name: Festering Resentment
kit_explanation.explanation: Festering Resentment starts the first battle with three Ignition. Other allies' special or ultimate attacks add one Ignition, plus another if that attacking ally is Sun. Her basic advances her next turn by 18%, rising to 30%, and adds chain damage against a debuffed target. Higher passive levels also add ATK.

pros: Ally attacks can start her Burn engine without using Cristelle's own turn.
Nightmare Unleashed rewards several debuffs and can preserve Burn.
Basic and ultimate both improve progress toward her next turn.
The reactive special grants two Ignition to every other Sun ally.
cons: Reactive special cannot be manually scheduled independently of allies.
Debuff immunity and cleansing undermine several linked damage sources.
Non-attacking Sun supports do not feed the passive's attacking-skill condition.

teams.name: Sun Burn pressure (theorycraft)
teams.why: Scarlet supplies Burn, Kyra supplies two other debuffs, and Ceres heals and buffs ATK.
teams.playstyle: Let the two attacking Sun partners build Ignition, then focus Nightmare Unleashed on a debuffed target; cleanse with Ceres when needed.

teams.name: Sun support offense (theorycraft)
teams.why: Charlotte shares offensive buffs and contributes an attacking Sun ultimate; Scarlet supplies Burn and Ceres keeps the team alive.
teams.playstyle: Use Charlotte's buff on the damage dealer who needs it, but count only actual attacking special/ultimate skills toward Cristelle's passive.

alternatives.why: Scarlet offers a simpler self-contained Burn application if you only need that debuff.
alternatives.tradeoff: She lacks the automatic team-wide Burn attempt, chain-damage payoff and turn progress.

alternatives.why: Bell has a higher published PvP rating and offers immediate buff removal and Silence when direct disruption is more important than Burn.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not extend Burn, distribute Ignition or replicate chain damage, and has a lower PvE rating. Availability and the cost of a separate build matter.

alternatives.why: Rosaria is a stronger immediate area-damage option when the fight may end before Cristelle builds a useful Burn and debuff cycle; her ultimate also applies DEF Down.
alternatives.tradeoff: She replaces Cristelle's Sun Ignition support and repeated Burn interactions with direct burst. Against a durable debuffable target in a prepared Sun team, that is not automatically the better outcome.

incognita-landgrave.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

incognita-flower.summary:
Haydee is a DEF-scaling protector who takes part of allies' damage through Guard, shields herself, and attacks with DEF scaling. Her useful sequence is to maintain a Barrier, then use Thorned Grave for Guard and stronger damage; she can turn maximum Leap into an extra turn with Spiked Armor.

Choose her when a team needs someone to share incoming damage while staying behind a personal barrier. DEF serves both that barrier and her attacks, so an ordinary ATK build misses her purpose. Leap management lets her defensive special grant an extra turn; she still needs a healer for sustained pressure.
incognita-flower.watch: Guard redirects damage rather than removing it, and only the strongest damage-sharing effect applies. She needs healing to cover transferred damage. Her passive's opening Guard and Barrier are absent from its level-1 description, so do not assume every copy starts protected.
incognita-flower.dependency_note: Her self-sustain tools are Barriers, not healing. Pair her with a healer and attackers who benefit from the damage she absorbs; piling on another Guard source does not add their percentages together.

skill_order.name: Thorned Grave
skill_order.why: Prioritize the level-6 cooldown improvement and eventually level-10 Guard duration for the actual team-protection tool.

skill_order.name: Spiked Armor
skill_order.why: Take cooldown reductions at levels 6 and 10 for more frequent Barriers and resource-spending extra turns.

skill_order.name: Eroded Emotions
skill_order.why: DEF and the opening protection are important passive improvements when available.

skill_order.name: Steel Hail
skill_order.why: Leave basic damage until the defensive loop is established.

rotation: Use Thorned Grave while a Barrier is already present when possible, including the opening passive Barrier if unlocked.
Refresh a missing Barrier with Spiked Armor; at maximum Leap, use the granted extra turn for Thorned Grave or an urgent attack.
Do not postpone Guard if an ally is about to take lethal damage just to gain the Barrier damage bonus. Heal Haydee after repeated redirected hits.

best_partners.why: Frey heals Haydee, can fully cleanse her, and grants Barriers; Haydee is also eligible for Frey's enhanced Star-ally healing.
Ceres's party healing helps cover shared damage and her cleanse supports Haydee's defensive uptime.
Haydee's ACC Down can help Fei evade attacks and trigger Lunar Shadow when the debuff sticks.
Carnelia supplies damage and Buff Block while Haydee shares incoming damage to protect her outside Spoke's survival window.

incognita-flower.build_tip: DEF improves her main Barrier and Thorned Grave, then HP keeps redirected damage survivable. Add enough SPD for Guard uptime and Effect Hit only if ACC Down is important in the encounter. Journey option: Silent Hatred is Endurance-tagged, supporting DEF for personal durability; its listed training effectiveness is +6% at Arcana level 1. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
incognita-flower.tier_reason: DEF scaling, Guard and self Barriers support a useful conditional protector in either mode. She needs outside healing and Guard uptime, and offers less value when another damage-sharing effect already covers the same job.
incognita-flower.investment: Upgrade Thorned Grave's cooldown and Guard duration before basic damage, then Spiked Armor's cooldowns and Barrier. Her potentials arrays are empty, so the data supports no additional unique-potential claim. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
incognita-flower.pve_note: Useful for protecting damage dealers through repeated hits, provided a healer can keep her alive. Against an ACC Down-immune boss, assess her on Guard and Barriers alone.
incognita-flower.pvp_note: Opening protection at the appropriate passive level can help against burst, but short durations and redirected damage can overwhelm her. ACC Down can help evasive allies without making them untouchable.

kit_explanation.name: Steel Hail
kit_explanation.explanation: Steel Hail is a single-target basic that builds one Leap. It scales with ATK, unlike Thorned Grave's added DEF component. Nova adds Toughness damage and a short DEF-based self Barrier, useful when the defensive skill is unavailable.

kit_explanation.name: Spiked Armor
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Spiked Armor gives Haydee a DEF-based Barrier and DEF Up for three turns. At maximum Leap it consumes all Leap and gives her an extra turn, allowing a protected follow-up without waiting for her next normal turn.

kit_explanation.name: Thorned Grave
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Thorned Grave attacks one enemy using ATK and DEF, gives Haydee Guard, and attempts two turns of ACC Down. Its damage is 20% higher while she has a Barrier. Guard lasts two turns initially and three at skill level 10; the listed 100% debuff chance is not immunity bypass.

kit_explanation.name: Eroded Emotions
kit_explanation.explanation: Eroded Emotions adds DEF, from 5% to 15%. At passive level 2 onward it also starts the first battle with one turn of Guard and a DEF-based Barrier, and gives Leap after she is attacked at a chance that rises from 50% to 100%. That resource gain is automatic; it is not a taunt.

pros: Guard protects allies while leaving their own actions free.
DEF contributes to both a self Barrier and her main attack.
Maximum Leap turns a defensive refresh into an extra-turn opportunity.
An upgraded passive supplies opening Guard and a personal barrier.
cons: No listed heal replenishes damage taken through Guard.
Spiked Armor only shields herself, not the entire party.
Early passive levels and short Guard windows reduce opening safety.

teams.name: Guard and recovery (theorycraft)
teams.why: Haydee shares damage, Frey heals and shields, and Bell plus Carnelia cover disruption and damage.
teams.playstyle: Refresh Guard before exposed allies are hit; use Frey's direct heal on Haydee when redirected damage accumulates.

teams.name: Accuracy pressure (theorycraft)
teams.why: Haydee lowers ACC for Fei's evasion plan while Ceres heals and Kyra adds single-target control.
teams.playstyle: Try to land ACC Down before attacks into Fei, but keep healing available because evasion is probabilistic.

alternatives.why: Emily is higher-rated in both modes and adds a targeted ATK buff/Barrier, an extra turn and repeated area damage when that broader role is needed.
alternatives.tradeoff: Emily has no Guard damage sharing or ACC Down and is not a healer. Building a separate defender costs resources; keep Haydee when her particular protection fits better.

alternatives.why: Carmen offers party DEF Up and single-target Taunt instead of sharing damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: Taunt can fail or be immune, and she lacks Haydee's ordinary self-Barrier skill.

incognita-flower.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

eastern-owl.summary:
Serpang is an HP-scaling Sun healer who weakens one enemy and protects himself plus a low-HP teammate from skill damage. His upgraded passive links Burn on enemies to Ignition generation, then spends five Ignition to move much closer to another turn.

Choose Serpang when repeated healing and enemy weakening solve the fight more directly than cleansing. HP and speed support both heals, and his three-turn special can set up allied debuffs with Effect RES Down. Sun attackers receive the ultimate’s healing bonus. Check the automatic nullification recipient carefully; a low-health support may receive protection that you wanted on the main carry.
eastern-owl.watch: Skill DMG Nullification does not stop debuff damage and only covers Serpang plus one other lowest-HP-ratio ally. He has no cleanse or revive. The Burn/resource loop is absent at passive level 1, so ordinary first-copy healing should not be advertised as the complete loop.
eastern-owl.dependency_note: Bring damage dealers and protection appropriate to the encounter. Sun allies receive more healing from his ultimate; a Burn user can feed his upgraded passive, and a separate cleanser is important against heavy debuffs.

skill_order.name: I Trust You!
skill_order.why: Recovery nodes improve a three-turn attacking party heal, with extra recovery for the most injured ally and two enemy debuffs.

skill_order.name: Let's Show Them, Toto!
skill_order.why: Improve the larger recovery tool if broad healing and targeted skill nullification are the reason to select him.

skill_order.name: I Choose You!
skill_order.why: Basic damage is last; Nova basic is a targeted recovery option and higher-passive Burn is automatic.

rotation: Use I Trust You! for routine party recovery and an attempt to lower the dangerous enemy's ATK and Effect RES before allied debuffs.
Use Let's Show Them, Toto! when broader healing or protecting the lowest-HP-ratio other ally from a skill is useful; the target is automatic and not necessarily your chosen carry.

Between heals use I Choose You!; at upgraded passive levels it can apply Burn. Burning enemies starting turns add Ignition, and five stacks at a turn end convert into 50% progress toward Serpang's next turn.
Use Nova basic for an additional lowest-HP-ratio heal when needed. Bring an actual cleanse if recovery reduction or damage-over-time effects threaten the group.

best_partners.why: Serpang's Sun turns feed Charlotte's Ignition and his ultimate heals Sun allies more effectively; Charlotte supplies team ATK Up for offense.
Marcille applies Burn, which can feed Serpang's upgraded passive on enemy turns, while he heals and can lower resistance for her debuffs.
Hilde supplies opening ally barriers and self-protection; Serpang restores lost HP and can weaken a threatening enemy's ATK.

eastern-owl.build_tip: Max HP and SPD are the sensible recovery priorities, followed by DEF and useful resistance. Effect Hit helps ATK Down/Effect RES Down and later Burn, but do not build ATK primarily to inflate Burn at the expense of healing. Journey option: The Princess Ascends the Throne is Vitality-tagged, supporting HP for recovery or HP scaling; its listed training effectiveness is +11% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
eastern-owl.tier_reason: The stored B PvE / D+ PvP ratings fit useful sustained healing and Sun-team recovery with limited fast defensive control. PvE can exploit Burn-fed turns and repeated heals; PvP exposes automatic protection targeting, no cleanse and a slower 95-SPD starting profile.
eastern-owl.investment: I Trust You! has recovery upgrades at levels 2/3/6/8/10; prioritize them if healing is inadequate. The ultimate upgrades recovery without a listed cooldown-reduction node. Rise, Phoenix! level 1 is HP only; level 2 adds the Burn/turn-progress loop, with Burn application rising from 50% to 100% by passive level 4. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
eastern-owl.pve_note: Best kit fit is a sustained Sun-oriented team where the ultimate's enhanced recovery matters and enemies can remain burned. A Burn-immune boss still permits healing but removes passive fuel from that route.
eastern-owl.pvp_note: Nullification can protect against a skill hit but not ongoing debuff damage, and its other recipient follows HP ratio. Faster cleanse/healing supports can be more useful into heavy control; Serpang's enemy resistance reduction remains a specific reason to choose him.

kit_explanation.name: I Choose You!
kit_explanation.explanation: I Choose You! hits one enemy and adds Ignition. From a later passive level it can also apply Burn. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and heals the lowest-HP-ratio ally based on Serpang's Max HP.

kit_explanation.name: I Trust You!
kit_explanation.explanation: I Trust You! attacks one enemy on a three-turn cooldown, grants Ignition and heals all allies, with extra recovery for the lowest-HP-ratio ally. It attempts two-turn ATK Down and Effect RES Down on the target, both at a listed 100% application chance. Recovery scales with Serpang's Max HP; enemy resistance and Immunity can still matter. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Let's Show Them, Toto!
kit_explanation.explanation: Let's Show Them, Toto! is a non-attacking party heal on a five-turn cooldown that grants two Ignition. It gives one stack of Skill DMG Nullification to Serpang and the lowest-HP-ratio other ally; that protection does not stop debuff damage. Sun allies receive increased healing, and recovery scales with his Max HP. Nova restores his Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: Rise, Phoenix!
kit_explanation.explanation: Rise, Phoenix! starts as a 5% Max HP bonus. From passive level 2, the basic can burn for two turns at 50–100% application chance by passive level, burning enemies' turn starts grant Ignition, and five Ignition at turn end are consumed for 50% next-turn progress. Higher passive levels also add Max HP.

pros: Routine heal also attacks and attempts ATK/Effect RES Down.
Ultimate gives enhanced Sun recovery and limited skill-damage protection.
External Burn can help the upgraded passive generate another healing turn.
HP improves both ordinary recovery skills and the Nova basic heal.
cons: No cleanse, revive or party barrier.
Nullification has automatic limited targeting and does not stop debuff damage.
Passive cycling depends on upgrades and Burn remaining on enemies until their turns.

teams.name: Sun survival and damage
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Hilde buys opening time, both attackers receive Sun-enhanced ultimate recovery, and Serpang's turns feed Charlotte.
teams.playstyle: Heal routine damage with I Trust You!; reserve the larger heal/nullification for a real incoming skill threat.

teams.name: Burn-fed recovery
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Marcille supplies Burn, Emily supplies targeted barrier/DEF support and Dress Asherah covers the missing cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Use when extra sustain is necessary; two healers lower damage, so replace one only after checking the encounter's survival needs.

alternatives.why: Dress Asherah is a higher-rated general sustain choice with party cleanse, attacking heals and explicit allied turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: Serpang keeps enemy ATK/Effect RES Down, Sun-enhanced recovery and limited skill nullification, which she does not provide.

alternatives.why: Kingdom Frey adds a full single-ally cleanse and party barriers, often more useful when debuffs or preventive protection are the problem.
alternatives.tradeoff: Serpang retains a routine attacking party heal and enemy resistance reduction; Frey's healing bonus favors Star rather than Sun allies.

eastern-owl.research_note: Community build checked against the stored skills; advice is kit-based, and paid details were unavailable.

apostle-gille.summary:
Gille is a break-team coordinator who also deals area damage. She turns Shatter users into a small orchestra: Overture adds Toughness damage, Imperfect Deathcry upgrades that state, and Malice rewards attacks into broken targets. Her value depends more on the team maintaining these conditions than on her high stored ATK alone.

Pick her after choosing Shatter users, not before. Her ultimate gives qualifying allies 20% action progress, then repeated Deathcry uses advance the orchestra states. Speed helps line up that support before the damage window; ATK and critical stats follow. A break-proof encounter or a party without Shatter removes much of her value, so the provisional rating is not permission to force her into every lineup.
apostle-gille.watch: Her team buffs need allies who already have Shatter, and progressing the orchestra states takes setup. She has no healing or cleanse; do not assume her attacks can generally remove enemy buffs.
apostle-gille.dependency_note: Bring an ally who supplies their own Shatter, and enough survival to exploit break windows. Dark Asherah and Tyria qualify through their ultimates; an arbitrary Chaos ally does not.

skill_order.name: Star-Scorching Cataclysm
skill_order.why: First priority: cooldown reductions at skill levels 4 and 8 improve access to Shatter and Overture setup.

skill_order.name: Imperfect Deathcry
skill_order.why: Next improve the attack that advances Overture to Rhapsody and Rhapsody to Finale, including automatic copies.

skill_order.name: Liquefy
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later purchase; its Agitation and Nova Shatter access already support setup.

rotation: Have allied Shatter users establish their own buffs before Star-Scorching Cataclysm if you want them to receive Overture and 20% action gauge, meaning progress toward their next turn.
Use Imperfect Deathcry to advance existing Overture/Rhapsody. Its Finale damage bonus checks her state on attack; do not assume the upgrade granted after that hit boosts that same hit.
Coordinate the next allied break with an Overture/Rhapsody/Finale holder; Malice then triggers Imperfect Deathcry automatically, once per turn, without chaining from its own follow-up break.
Use Liquefy between cooldowns for Agitation. A Nova basic can establish her own brief Shatter, but do not spend scarce Nova purely to follow a fixed sequence.

best_partners.why: Lucula Noctis supplies her own three-turn Shatter; Phantom Sever has extra boss Toughness damage while it lasts, directly supporting Gille's break-state loop.
Crescendo of Sorrow supplies Shatter, allowing Overture access; Tyria's marked-target attacks can exploit the resulting broken window.
Bal Doré heals while attacking and Lumière Sonnet cleanses and advances teammates, helping the team reach another break cycle.

apostle-gille.build_tip: Favor enough SPD to act inside allied Shatter windows, then ATK and reliable critical hits for damage. Add HP/DEF if she cannot survive setup; her 93 stored SPD is not an opener guarantee. Journey option: Never Ending Dance is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +10% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
apostle-gille.tier_reason: The stored PvE NEW / PvP NEW status is provisional. Her Shatter-specific support and broken-target damage suggest a useful PvE boss-break role, especially alongside Dark Asherah. Short PvP rounds or teams without Shatter may not realize those benefits; no settled tier or measured superiority is claimed.
apostle-gille.investment: Buy the ultimate cooldown milestones before chasing small damage steps. Malice scales from 2% to 6% team break damage per Agitation stack and gains ATK at later passive levels; prioritize that only through verified available upgrades. The profile has no listed unique/basic/special potentials. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +6 CRIT DMG; it is not part of the starting stat line.
apostle-gille.pve_note: Plan around bosses whose Toughness can be broken. Her benefits shrink when break windows cannot be created or when the group dies before Overture progresses; no boss immunity bypass is established for SPD Down.
apostle-gille.pvp_note: The highest-ATK enemy is the SPD Down target. Finale says to ignore Effect RES for the ultimate attack, but this does not explicitly bypass Immunity or every defensive rule. Team setup is vulnerable to a faster enemy.

kit_explanation.name: Liquefy
kit_explanation.explanation: Liquefy is a single-enemy basic that adds one Agitation stack. Agitation itself adds small damage against Order enemies, up to five stacks; Nova adds one fixed Toughness damage and grants Gille one-turn Shatter.

kit_explanation.name: Imperfect Deathcry
kit_explanation.explanation: Imperfect Deathcry is a single-enemy attack with a listed three-turn cooldown. After the hit it upgrades allied Overture to Rhapsody and Rhapsody to Finale; these states do not stack together. If Gille already has Finale, this hit gains 30% damage against a broken enemy. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Star-Scorching Cataclysm
kit_explanation.explanation: Star-Scorching Cataclysm attacks all enemies on a listed six-turn cooldown, reduced by upgrades at levels 4 and 8. It gives Gille two-turn Shatter, then grants Overture and 20% next-turn progress to Shatter allies. It attempts two-turn SPD Down on the highest-ATK enemy; with Finale the attack ignores Effect RES. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Malice
kit_explanation.explanation: Malice is automatic: each own turn adds Agitation; allied attacks gain broken-target damage based on Gille's stacks, from 2% per stack at passive level 1 to 6% at level 4. A Shatter ally attacking gives Shatter allies one-turn SPD Up. An eligible orchestra-state ally breaking Toughness triggers Imperfect Deathcry once per turn; its own follow-up break cannot recursively trigger it.

pros: Shatter partners gain both turn progress and extra Toughness pressure from one area attack.
Orchestra states are undispellable and improve damage during break windows.
Agitation turns time spent setting up into a teamwide broken-target damage bonus.
A qualifying allied Break triggers an automatic state-advancing attack once per turn.
cons: Allied Shatter is a real selection constraint, not a benefit given to every teammate.
Listed 93 SPD and multi-stage buffs make timing an investment concern.
No heal or cleanse; a break-resistant encounter can remove much of her purpose.

teams.name: Shatter boss window
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Dark Asherah breaks under Shatter, Emily supplies a targeted barrier, and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses. Gille turns the Shatter window into extra break pressure.
teams.playstyle: Set Dark Asherah's Shatter before Gille's ultimate; retain healing for the boss response.

teams.name: Two Shatter attackers
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Both attackers create Shatter themselves and can receive Gille's Overture. The healer keeps a fragile, attack-heavy group going.
teams.playstyle: Use only if a dedicated defender is unnecessary; stagger Shatter setup and orchestra upgrades rather than assuming synchronized cooldowns.

alternatives.why: Tanya offers direct Toughness pressure and, at upgraded passive levels, advances allies when she personally breaks.
alternatives.tradeoff: Simpler team requirements, but no Overture progression or Shatter-specific team bonus.

alternatives.why: Professor M supports frequent allied attacks with a forced dual attack and a special-skill vulnerability mark.
alternatives.tradeoff: Useful without Shatter, but relies on allied attacks and a mark rather than Gille's break-state amplification.

apostle-gille.research_note: community’s new November 11 build was reviewed. Its settled rating differs from the local provisional snapshot; no equal-investment combat test validates the ranking here.

magician-druid.summary:
Dana is an area-damage caster who also buffs the highest-ATK other ally. Star allies' attacks build her Leap at higher passive levels, and full Leap becomes Roroca!, an ATK/CRIT DMG boost. Critical hits can grant SPD Up, so her damage, team composition and turn frequency support one another.

Use Dana with attacking Star allies and another carry who can receive Rapid Bloom. Five Leap become Roroca! at turn start, giving 15% ATK and 20% CRIT DMG, while critical hits can supply one-turn SPD Up. Her area ultimate attempts a short SPD Down on the opposing team. With stored 90 SPD, she needs gear and turn-order planning before that control arrives. She offers an offensive ally buff, but no recovery or protection for a team under pressure.
magician-druid.watch: Pure Heart's resource and critical-hit mechanics are absent at passive level 1. Her listed maximum SPD is 90, and a damage-only build may act too late. Power of Nature grants its low-HP-target Roroca! after damage, so that new buff should not be counted on the hit that earns it.
magician-druid.dependency_note: She can attack alone, but attacking Star allies accelerate her specific Leap engine. Healing and protection remain external; choose Star partners for actual useful attacks and support, not only their attribute.

skill_order.name: Power of Nature
skill_order.why: Take level 6 for the area skill's cooldown and levels 4/8 for SPD Down if applicable.

skill_order.name: Rapid Bloom
skill_order.why: Improve the dual ATK-buff attack next; its three-turn listed cooldown has no cooldown upgrades.

skill_order.name: Pure Heart
skill_order.why: Passive levels enable and improve her Star-ally and critical-hit engine.

skill_order.name: Leaf Barrage
skill_order.why: Basic damage follows the main area attack and utility priorities.

rotation: Use Rapid Bloom before an important Power of Nature when Dana needs ATK Up and the other buff recipient can also benefit.
Check Roroca! and enemy HP before the area attack; use an available buff window if practical, but do not delay a useful wave clear solely to fill Leap.
Let Star allies' attacks build Leap; at full stacks the turn-start passive spends it automatically. Use Leaf Barrage during cooldown gaps.

best_partners.why: Bell's Star attacks feed Dana's Leap while providing Silence, buff removal and area damage.
Haydee's Star attacks feed Leap and her Guard protects Dana through her slower start.
Frey supplies Barriers and enhanced healing for Star Dana; her basic attacks can feed Leap, but her non-attacking heals do not.
Carnelia offers complementary area pressure and can receive Rapid Bloom's ally ATK buff if she is the highest-ATK other ally.

magician-druid.build_tip: ATK and enough CRIT Rate to support Pure Heart, then CRIT DMG and SPD. The listed maximum 14% CRIT Rate and 68% CRIT DMG are not proof her passive will trigger consistently without investment. A Stroll with Friends supports Strength and improves Sensory Training chance after 50 Bond. That direction fits Dana’s ATK scaling.
magician-druid.tier_reason: The A/A ratings fit a useful hybrid area attacker and ally buffer rather than a universal top carry. Star attacking partners and reliable crits improve her engine; a low-investment passive or debuff-immune enemy reduces its extra utility.
magician-druid.investment: Prioritize Power of Nature's cooldown, then damage and Rapid Bloom. Passive levels matter because the full-Star resource engine is missing at level 1. No potentials are listed; use current crit stats rather than treating stored maxima or Nova crit as permanent. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
magician-druid.pve_note: Useful for waves and a dual-attacker team. Against a single boss, Rapid Bloom's ally buff remains relevant, while SPD Down and the half-HP follow-up buff depend on encounter conditions.
magician-druid.pvp_note: She needs enough speed or protection to reach her area attack. SPD Down is only one turn and can be resisted or cleansed, so it is pressure rather than reliable turn denial.

kit_explanation.name: Leaf Barrage
kit_explanation.explanation: Leaf Barrage hits one enemy and grants one Leap. It fills cooldown gaps but has no listed team buff. Nova adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Rapid Bloom
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 3 turns. Rapid Bloom hits one enemy, grants Leap, and gives ATK Up to Dana and the highest-ATK other ally for two turns. Check who actually receives the automatic ally buff after equipment changes. Nova adds Toughness damage and temporary CRIT Rate on this attack.

kit_explanation.name: Power of Nature
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Power of Nature hits all enemies, adds Leap and attempts one turn of SPD Down. Application rises from 75% to 100% through levels 4 and 8; level 6 shortens cooldown. If the target is at half HP or below after the attack, Dana receives one turn of Roroca!, which increases ATK and CRIT DMG. The multi-target text does not establish multiple Roroca! stacks per enemy.

kit_explanation.name: Pure Heart
kit_explanation.explanation: Pure Heart begins with ATK. From level 2 onward, critical hits can give one turn of SPD Up, with chance rising from 70% to 100%; other Star allies' attacks add Leap. Full Leap at Dana's turn start is consumed for two turns of Roroca!. Later passive levels increase ATK as well. These are automatic checks, not separate skills to cast.

pros: Area damage also attempts to slow the enemy team.
Rapid Bloom buffs another attacker as well as Dana.
Star ally attacks can enable Roroca! without spending extra Dana turns.
Rapid Bloom grants its ATK buff to Dana and the highest-ATK other ally.
cons: Low listed maximum SPD makes opening order a build concern.
Full passive utility is unavailable in the first stored passive level.
No healing, Barrier or direct ally protection.

teams.name: Star attack engine (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell and Haydee supply Star attacks for Leap; Haydee shares damage and Frey heals and shields.
teams.playstyle: Keep Dana alive through her first turn, use Rapid Bloom for offensive coverage, and spend Power of Nature when it can clear or slow a wave.

teams.name: Dual caster pressure (theorycraft)
teams.why: Carnelia supplies control and area damage, Emily protects a carry, and Ceres heals while Dana shares ATK Up.
teams.playstyle: Verify the intended Rapid Bloom recipient. Stagger duplicated ATK buffs and use protection to survive until the casters act.

alternatives.why: Carnelia has higher published mode ratings and adds Buff Block, turn delay and once-per-battle lethal-hit survival to area damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not buff the highest-ATK ally or use Dana's Star-attack resource engine; a separate build is required.

alternatives.why: Maid Lydia is a higher-rated area-payoff alternative when another attacker can feed her marked-ally engine.
alternatives.tradeoff: She requires correct highest-ATK marking and resource timing rather than Dana's simpler direct area ultimate; availability is not assumed.

saintess-demon.summary:
Muriel combines area damage and ATK Down with a single-target debuff extender. She is most useful when teammates place several meaningful debuffs first, then she keeps one target’s debuffs alive while Sun allies help build Ignition for her Burn condition.

Use Muriel after allies have already applied debuffs worth preserving. Holy Bombardment extends all debuffs on one enemy by one turn and gains damage per debuff, making target selection more important than using it on cooldown. Sun allies help her reach the five Ignition needed for the ultimate’s Burn attempt. Her 25% passive CRIT DMG does not establish critical consistency by itself. Build Effect Hit for application, then enough speed to place extension before the useful effects expire.
saintess-demon.watch: Her area ATK Down only reaches a listed 75% application chance, not guaranteed success. Holy Bombardment extends debuffs already present; it cannot create a missing debuff or prove an immune boss can be controlled.
saintess-demon.dependency_note: Debuff partners supply both the special’s damage bonus and effects worth extending. Sun allies’ attacks feed Ignition only after the passive gains that feature.

skill_order.name: Holy Bombardment
skill_order.why: Levels 4/8 improve extension chance and level 6 reduces cooldown; prioritize this if her job is maintaining debuffs.

skill_order.name: I'll Be Good From Now On
skill_order.why: Levels 4/8 improve ATK Down from 50% to 75%, and level 6 shortens cooldown.

skill_order.name: Triumphant
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels improve CRIT DMG and Sun-ally Ignition generation.

skill_order.name: Divine Flame
skill_order.why: Basic damage is secondary to extension uptime and the area skill.

rotation: Let partners apply DEF Down, Unknown Hex or other useful effects, then use Holy Bombardment on the priority enemy before those debuffs expire.
Use I'll Be Good From Now On for immediate area damage or to reduce incoming ATK; at five Ignition stacks it also attempts Burn. Delay for stacks only when the current fight allows it.
Use Divine Flame while cooldowns recover. Sun ally attacks add Ignition through upgraded Triumphant; do not assume those extra stacks at passive level 1.

best_partners.why: Unknown Hex and SPD Down provide several useful effects for Muriel to extend on the priority target.
Sun attacks feed upgraded Triumphant while Luna supplies DEF Down, ATK Down and defensive support.
Harley can grant three Ignition to the highest-ATK Sun ally and provides speed/turn control; ensure that recipient is Muriel.

saintess-demon.build_tip: ATK and critical stats for damage; Effect Hit for extension and debuffs when enemies permit them. SPD helps act before debuffs expire. Do not sacrifice all survival for Burn scaling. Divine Judgement supports Strength, with 9% Training Effectiveness after 40 Bond. Include Focus training when landing the extension matters more than raw damage.
saintess-demon.tier_reason: The stronger PvE rating fits sustained debuff extension and area pressure when enemies permit useful debuffs. PvP cleansing and short fights make the setup less dependable, consistent with the lower PvP rating. She is a team-oriented extender, not a standalone guarantee that every debuff can be prolonged.
saintess-demon.investment: Secure Holy Bombardment’s level-6 cooldown and level-8 extension chance when using her as an enabler. Improve the ultimate’s application and cooldown next. No unique potential is listed; passive ally-stack behavior starts above its first level. All quoted upper effects require the corresponding skill/passive level; stored maximum stats are not equal-investment combat results or a zero-star promise. The local star rows do not establish a combat unlock threshold.
saintess-demon.pve_note: Extend valuable boss debuffs only where the boss permits those effects and extension. Her area attack is useful for waves, but the extension hits one target rather than refreshing the whole enemy team. Despair of Night removes one personal debuff with Macrovoid; extension does not prevent that removal.
saintess-demon.pvp_note: Pairs with debuff pressure, but enemy cleanse can erase several turns of setup. Use the area ATK Down defensively when needed rather than assuming an ideal five-stack Burn opener.

kit_explanation.name: Divine Flame
kit_explanation.explanation: Divine Flame is a single-target basic granting one Ignition, a stacking small damage bonus against Star enemies, capped at five.

kit_explanation.name: Holy Bombardment
kit_explanation.explanation: Holy Bombardment attacks one target on a listed four-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. Each debuff on that target adds 3% damage, and it attempts to extend all its debuffs by one turn. Extension chance grows from 75% to 100% at levels 4 and 8.

kit_explanation.name: I'll Be Good From Now On
kit_explanation.explanation: I'll Be Good From Now On attacks all enemies on a listed six-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. It attempts two-turn ATK Down with 50% to 75% chance and, if Ignition is full on attack, also attempts two-turn Burn. Burn scales with the caster’s ATK.

kit_explanation.name: Triumphant
kit_explanation.explanation: Triumphant gives CRIT DMG. From passive level 2 onward, another Sun ally’s attack can add one Ignition, progressing from 50% to 100% chance at the upper level. Passive level 1 contains only the CRIT DMG bonus.

pros: Can lengthen multiple useful debuffs on one important target in a single action.
Area ATK Down combines wave damage with pressure reduction.
Sun allies can accelerate the conditional Burn setup.
Her ultimate’s Nova raises the ATK Down application chance to 100%.
cons: Extension has little value without useful existing debuffs.
ATK Down remains probabilistic even at its upper skill level.
No healing or protection and no documented immunity bypass.

teams.name: Sun debuff pressure
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Summer Luna seeds debuffs, Harley feeds the intended Sun carry and Frey supplies missing recovery and cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Keep Muriel highest ATK among Sun allies for Harley’s feed; extend the priority target’s debuffs after they land.

teams.name: Layered debuff waves
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Lydia supplies Hex/slow, Voyager Luna supplies Bind’s area vulnerability and Carmen sustains the carry.
teams.playstyle: Apply area vulnerability before area damage, then extend the most important surviving enemy rather than pretending Holy Bombardment refreshes every target.

alternatives.why: Voyager Luna has a higher published PvP rating and offers area vulnerability plus repeated all-target attacks when coordinated immediate area pressure matters more than extension.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not extend allies’ debuffs, and her Bind application is also chance-based.

alternatives.why: Lydia is a better fit when the missing job is slowing turns and lowering Effect RES.
alternatives.tradeoff: She gives up Muriel’s debuff extension and conditional area Burn.

alternatives.why: Carnelia offers more self-contained area pressure, Buff Block and a once-per-battle lethal-damage safeguard when the team cannot maintain Muriel's debuff-extension plan.
alternatives.tradeoff: Carnelia does not extend allied debuffs or gain Muriel's Sun-attack resource feed. Her stronger PvP source rating does not prove superior sustained damage in every PvE debuff team.

saintess-elf.summary:
Elisa is a targeted healer and reviver whose Holy Blessing reduces damage and raises Effect RES. Her ultimate can rescue a fallen ally or accelerate a living one, while her upgraded passive rewards staying healthy and managing Agitation for an extra turn.

Choose Elisa when recovering a fallen carry is worth reserving an entire cooldown. Let Us Pray Together revives with 50% HP and 80% Action gauge; using it on a living ally instead heals and gives 40% gauge. Holy Blessing combines 25% damage reduction with 25% Effect RES. Keep Elisa above half HP to improve her targeted special’s recovery, and add a cleanser elsewhere. She cannot remove the debuffs that caused the emergency in the first place.
saintess-elf.watch: She is not a party-wide cleanser or area healer. Effect RES is not debuff immunity, and spending Let Us Pray Together on a living ally means its revive may be unavailable when someone falls.
saintess-elf.dependency_note: She keeps an important ally fighting but needs damage dealers and preferably another source of party-wide recovery or cleanse.

skill_order.name: A Futile Attempt to Help
skill_order.why: Levels 6 and 10 reduce the targeted heal cooldown; reliable routine recovery comes before basic damage.

skill_order.name: Let Us Pray Together
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces rescue cooldown and levels 4/8 improve living-target Holy Blessing chance.

skill_order.name: Timid Prayer
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels add recovery and the full-stack extra-turn interaction.

skill_order.name: Please Go Back
skill_order.why: Basic damage is low priority; its Nova can grant a short Holy Blessing to the lowest-HP ally.

rotation: Use A Futile Attempt to Help on the ally most at risk before the next attack; keeping Elisa herself above half HP enables the upgraded passive’s recovery bonus.
Reserve Let Us Pray Together for a revive when the fight is dangerous. Use it on a living carry for healing and 40% turn progress only when the faster action is worth losing the rescue cooldown.
With the relevant Timid Prayer level, use Please Go Back on her own turn at five Agitation to consume the stacks for an extra turn. Without that passive feature, do not plan this sequence.
Use the basic Nova for its one-turn Holy Blessing when that prevents damage; ordinary basics do not grant it.

best_partners.why: Her non-attack heal and ultimate feed Lugh’s Snow Blossom before Swift Decree.
Carmen supplies party recovery through basics and targeted cleanse, covering gaps in Elisa’s support.
Ceres disrupts enemy turns while Elisa restores or revives the damage/control carry.

saintess-elf.build_tip: HP for recovery scaling, SPD for timely rescue, then DEF and resistance for Elisa’s own survival. Damage stats do little for her main job; Effect RES still does not prevent every debuff. Divine Trial supports Endurance and gives 3% Condition Effect after 60 Bond. Include Vitality training first for her HP-scaled recovery.
saintess-elf.tier_reason: The PvE rating fits targeted recovery and revive insurance but also reflects her lack of party healing and cleanse. The stronger PvP rating is consistent with bringing a carry back with high turn progress, while long cooldowns and support interruption remain real limits.
saintess-elf.investment: Targeted-heal cooldown levels 6/10 and ultimate level 6 are sensible milestones. Passive level 1 gives only HP; confirm the later recovery/extra-turn effects are present before building around them. No unique potential is listed. All quoted upper effects require the corresponding skill/passive level; stored maximum stats are not equal-investment combat results or a zero-star promise. The local star rows do not establish a combat unlock threshold.
saintess-elf.pve_note: Useful insurance for a key carry in difficult stages. Pair with broader sustain for repeated area damage; reviving one ally does not restore a collapsed team.
saintess-elf.pvp_note: Living-target turn progress can create a pressure opportunity, while revive punishes an opponent who cannot finish the team. Her targeted tools and long rescue cooldown leave openings against repeated burst or control.

kit_explanation.name: Please Go Back
kit_explanation.explanation: Please Go Back is a single-target basic that adds one Agitation. Its Nova Burst also gives a one-turn Holy Blessing to the ally with the lowest HP ratio; that support is not part of the ordinary basic.

kit_explanation.name: A Futile Attempt to Help
kit_explanation.explanation: A Futile Attempt to Help heals one ally using Elisa’s maximum HP, grants two-turn Holy Blessing and adds two Agitation. Holy Blessing reduces damage taken by 25% and adds 25% Effect RES. The listed five-turn cooldown is reduced at levels 6 and 10.

kit_explanation.name: Let Us Pray Together
kit_explanation.explanation: Let Us Pray Together has two branches: revive a fallen ally at 50% HP with 80% progress toward its next turn, or heal a living ally with 40% progress and a chance of two-turn Holy Blessing. The latter chance grows from 75% to 100%. Its listed six-turn cooldown drops at level 6.

kit_explanation.name: Timid Prayer
kit_explanation.explanation: Timid Prayer raises maximum HP. From passive level 2, it also improves A Futile Attempt to Help while Elisa is at least half HP and consumes maximum Agitation when she uses her own-turn basic to grant an extra turn. The recovery bonus grows with passive level.

pros: Revive returns an ally with both HP and substantial turn progress.
Holy Blessing prevents damage as well as helping resist debuffs.
Upgraded stack management can give Elisa an extra action for recovery.
A living ultimate target also receives two turns of Holy Blessing.
cons: No listed cleanse in her own kit.
Main recovery skills target one ally rather than the full party.
Using the revive skill offensively exposes its cooldown if a teammate falls.

teams.name: Protected slash rescue
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Elisa and Carmen provide non-attack setup for Lugh, with Carmen’s basic party healing covering Elisa’s limited coverage.
teams.playstyle: Use routine targeted healing first; save the revive unless Lugh’s immediate accelerated turn is necessary.

teams.name: Area carry insurance
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Asherah deals area damage, Summer Luna reduces pressure and dress Asherah adds party healing and cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Keep Elisa healthy, Bless the exposed carry and use the revive to recover from a single loss rather than expecting party restoration.

alternatives.why: Frey is preferable when party healing, Barriers and a full targeted cleanse are the missing jobs.
alternatives.tradeoff: Frey cannot revive a fallen carry.

alternatives.why: Carmen is higher-rated in both modes and adds automatic highest-ATK carry protection, targeted full cleanse and party recovery on basics.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her protection is tied to the oath recipient, and she also lacks Elisa’s revive.

saintess-elf.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

apostle-tyria.summary:
Tyria is a mark-driven attacker with both area setup and focused finishing damage. Crescendo of Sorrow seeds Thorns of Ruin, then her basic adds marks and can automatically trigger Requiem of Ruin at three stacks. Defender-class targets give her an additional damage condition.

Use Tyria to pressure a marked Defender rather than treating her as an unconditional armor bypass. Her ultimate places Thorns, gives two Ignition and creates a Shatter window with extra Toughness damage. The basic can then trigger an automatic special against a fully marked enemy. Nova on the ultimate grants an extra turn, making that setup available sooner. Keep the published Thorns wording conflict in mind: an exact multiplier forecast would promise more certainty than the records support.
apostle-tyria.watch: Requiem's wording refers to Thorns on self for its per-stack bonus even though her application skills place Thorns on enemies. Treat that particular multiplier as ambiguous; the explicit enemy-mark trigger is clearer. Thorns alone explicitly states immunity/resistance bypass.
apostle-tyria.dependency_note: She supplies her own marks, Ignition and Shatter, but needs protection and benefits from extra basic attacks rather than teammates with matching names or attributes alone.

skill_order.name: Crescendo of Sorrow
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces the setup ultimate cooldown; its area marks and Shatter drive the kit.

skill_order.name: Requiem of Ruin
skill_order.why: Level 6 also reduces Requiem cooldown; damage upgrades improve both selected and passive-triggered uses.

skill_order.name: Prelude to the End
skill_order.why: Improve the basic after setup because it is the repeatable mark builder and follow-up trigger.

rotation: Open with Crescendo of Sorrow when area setup or the highest-DEF target's three marks matter. Nova grants an extra turn; the ordinary version does not.
Use Prelude to the End against an enemy close to three Thorns to let Guillotine Executor trigger Requiem automatically; check whether the ultimate already capped that target.
Use manual Requiem when a priority enemy must be finished or its Defender bonus is useful. It consumes Ignition, so waiting for five stacks is a damage option, not a mandatory delay.
Protect Tyria between windows: Thorns are removed if their caster dies. Do not schedule a second manual action for the passive-triggered Requiem.

best_partners.why: Song of the Toast gives team ATK Up; Charlotte also gains Ignition when Tyria's Sun turn starts, creating a concrete reciprocal interaction.
A highest-ATK Tyria can be pulled into a dual attack after Black or White, giving Prelude another opportunity to apply Thorns.
Party healing and a two-debuff cleanse protect the caster whose death removes Thorns.

apostle-tyria.build_tip: Build ATK and dependable CRIT Rate before adding CRIT DMG. Add SPD for mark cycling and survival against burst. Do not prioritize Effect Hit solely for Thorns, whose own effect text says it ignores ACC, Effect RES and Immunity. Customized Training to Cover Weaknesses is a Strength fit, with 8% Training Effectiveness after 30 Bond.
apostle-tyria.tier_reason: The stored S PvE / S+ PvP ratings fit her self-contained marks, conditional DEF penetration and automatic focused finisher, particularly into Defender-class targets. PvE remains useful for priority enemies, while the Defender interaction gives a specific PvP rationale. Target selection, survival and the conflicting per-Thorns damage wording still limit exact forecasts.
apostle-tyria.investment: Prioritize level-6 cooldown milestones for both cooldown attacks, then the damage source used most often. Guillotine Executor improves marked-target penetration from 15% to 25% across passive levels, with ATK added later. No potentials are listed, and the unusual one-piece star rows do not establish a real acquisition plan. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
apostle-tyria.pve_note: Use area setup to prepare a boss or sturdy elite, then keep basic attacks focused to reach the automatic finisher. Her Defender bonus should not be assumed for every boss class.
apostle-tyria.pvp_note: The highest-DEF mark target may differ from the enemy you want to kill. Check targeting before committing; Nova can connect setup into an immediate action, but does not prove an unstoppable combo.

kit_explanation.name: Prelude to the End
kit_explanation.explanation: Prelude to the End is a single-target basic adding one Ignition. Guillotine Executor adds a Thorns mark after this basic, so the basic is an engine piece rather than filler. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Requiem of Ruin
kit_explanation.explanation: Requiem of Ruin is a single-target attack on a listed five-turn cooldown, shortened at level 6. It has extra damage against Defenders and at five Ignition, consumes Ignition and removes the target's Thorns afterward. Manual use gives three-turn SPD Up; additionally triggered copies do not. Its per-Thorns damage wording conflicts about who holds the marks, so do not budget an exact multiplier. Nova adds one fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Crescendo of Sorrow
kit_explanation.explanation: Crescendo of Sorrow is an area attack on a listed six-turn cooldown, shortened at level 6. It grants two Ignition and two-turn Shatter, applies one Thorns mark to enemies and specifies three on the highest-DEF enemy, with Thorns capped at three. Nova additionally grants an extra turn after attacking.

kit_explanation.name: Guillotine Executor
kit_explanation.explanation: Guillotine Executor automatically gives Prelude and Requiem DEF penetration against marked enemies, scaling from 15% to 25% with passive levels. Prelude adds a mark and triggers Requiem when the enemy reaches the three-mark cap. The Thorns effect specifically ignores ACC, Effect RES and Immunity and disappears when Tyria is defeated; that exception should not be generalized to other debuffs.

pros: Basic attacks contribute marks and can produce a separate finisher.
Ultimate supplies her own Shatter and quickly marks a high-DEF target.
Marked-target DEF penetration and a Defender-specific bonus address durable enemies.
Nova on her ultimate grants an explicit extra turn.
cons: Losing Tyria also removes her Thorns from enemies.
Requiem consumes the Ignition resource and enemy marks, so timing affects the next window.
Per-Thorns damage wording conflicts, preventing a trustworthy exact damage forecast.

teams.name: Sun pressure with sustain
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Charlotte provides ATK Up, Hilde opening barriers and self-protection, and Serpang heals Sun allies more strongly. Tyria's turns feed Charlotte's Ignition.
teams.playstyle: Establish Hilde's protection and preserve Serpang's emergency heal while Tyria marks a kill target.

teams.name: Marked-target dual attacks
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Professor M can pull the highest-ATK Tyria into basics, Emily buffs and shields her, and Dress Asherah heals and cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Tune Tyria to be the intended highest-ATK ally; use basics on a nearly capped mark target rather than expecting a fixed turn sequence.

alternatives.why: Charlotte offers team ATK Up and a Sun-fed single-target attack cycle without enemy mark management.
alternatives.tradeoff: Trades Tyria's area marking and Defender bonus for a self-buff/stack loop.

alternatives.why: Dark Asherah explicitly rewards broken bosses with large conditional chain damage and special-skill resets.
alternatives.tradeoff: Better suited to a break-focused boss plan; requires break access instead of Tyria's Thorns setup.

recon-knuckle.summary:
Roberta is a single-target attacker who retaliates automatically against all-target attacks. Critical hits make that reaction cycle faster, while her skills push her toward her next turn and her unique potential can turn critical skill damage into self-healing.

Choose Roberta to punish enemies that repeatedly attack the whole party. Fast Track responds automatically, removes one personal debuff and returns 30% Action gauge; a critical hit shortens that reaction’s cooldown. Her passive supplies 50% CRIT Rate on attack, so account for it before spending heavily on more crit chance. The below-half-HP damage bonus is not a reason to refuse healing: a defeated Roberta produces no reactions, and her self-recovery requires an obtained Unique Potential.
recon-knuckle.watch: Fast Track is a reaction, not an opener you can select. Her larger low-HP damage bonus is not a reason to leave her near death; the passive already provides substantial on-attack CRIT Rate.
recon-knuckle.dependency_note: Her basic and ultimate function without a special ally, but frequent enemy area attacks are what unlock the reaction’s value. Team healing remains useful.

skill_order.name: Fast Track
skill_order.why: At levels 4 and 8 Fast Track gains more turn progress; critical hits also shorten its own cooldown.

skill_order.name: On-Site Emergency Judgment
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces ultimate cooldown, and levels 4/8 improve gauge gain.

skill_order.name: Veteran's Instinct
skill_order.why: ATK and conditional damage improve; count its 50% on-attack CRIT Rate before gearing.

skill_order.name: Commence Operation
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later investment; Nova Burst adds turn progress when resources allow.

rotation: Use On-Site Emergency Judgment for ATK Up and turn progress; if already at five Leap stacks, it consumes them for an additional 20% progress.
Use Commence Operation between ultimate uses to build Leap. Its Nova Burst adds 20% progress toward Roberta’s next turn, not an unconditional extra turn.
Fast Track fires on its own after Roberta is hit by an all-target attack when available. It cleanses one personal debuff and accelerates her next action; do not insert a manual Fast Track cast.
Keep her alive through enemy area attacks rather than deliberately sitting below half HP for the larger damage modifier.

best_partners.why: Oath can protect Roberta if she is highest ATK; reaction healing and Barriers help her survive incoming pressure.
Star-target healing bonuses and a full targeted cleanse complement Roberta’s one-debuff self-cleanse.
Roberta’s attacks on a surviving Aqua Bomb target can enable Smile’s reaction when Smile has enough Leap.

recon-knuckle.build_tip: ATK and CRIT DMG after enough CRIT Rate to complement the passive’s 50% on-attack bonus. Include HP/DEF for surviving area hits; SPD improves ordinary turns but does not manufacture reaction triggers. Responsibility Atop a Pile of Paperwork supports Vitality and Support Quest income. Pair it with Strength training for her ATK attacks rather than assuming matching art means maximum damage.
recon-knuckle.tier_reason: Both mode ratings fit a strong response to frequent all-target enemy attacks: reaction damage, personal cleanse and turn progress reinforce each other. In PvE the enemy attack pattern decides the value; in PvP opponents that avoid the reaction trigger reduce that advantage. These are kit-based conditions, not measured matchup wins.
recon-knuckle.investment: Fast Track’s level-4/8 gauge upgrades and the ultimate’s level-6 cooldown reduction are practical priorities. Disaster Response Protocol adds one maximum Toughness and heals for 20% of damage on special/ultimate critical hits if acquired; it is not innate team healing. All quoted upper effects require the corresponding skill/passive level; stored maximum stats are not equal-investment combat results or a zero-star promise. The local star rows do not establish a combat unlock threshold.
recon-knuckle.pve_note: Good fit for encounters with repeated all-target attacks. Against a boss that rarely uses them, compare her ordinary single-target damage role with other carries rather than assuming constant reactions.
recon-knuckle.pvp_note: Punishes area attackers if she survives the hit and the reaction is ready. Enemy targeting, control and cooldown timing determine the payoff; she cannot choose when the opponent triggers Fast Track.

kit_explanation.name: Commence Operation
