kit_explanation.explanation: Commence Operation is a single-target basic granting one Leap. Its Nova Burst adds one Toughness damage and 20% progress toward her next turn.

kit_explanation.name: Fast Track
kit_explanation.explanation: Fast Track has a listed two-turn reaction cooldown. Being hit by an all-target attack triggers it against that attacker; it removes one personal debuff before attacking, grants Leap and 15% to 30% turn progress, and reduces its own cooldown by one on a critical hit.

kit_explanation.name: On-Site Emergency Judgment
kit_explanation.explanation: On-Site Emergency Judgment attacks one enemy, gives two-turn ATK Up and 15% to 30% turn progress. At maximum Leap it consumes the stacks for another 20%. Its listed five-turn cooldown has a level-6 reduction.

kit_explanation.name: Veteran's Instinct
kit_explanation.explanation: Veteran's Instinct supplies 50% CRIT Rate on attacks. Damage is increased both above and below half HP, with the larger bonus below half; higher passive levels add ATK and improve these bonuses. This is automatic and does not make taking lethal damage worthwhile.

pros: All-target enemy attacks can produce extra damage, cleanse and turn progress together.
Large innate on-attack CRIT Rate reduces the amount needed from gear.
Her unique potential can add critical-skill self-recovery and maximum Toughness.
At full Leap her ultimate grants a total 50% Action gauge.
cons: Fast Track loses relevance if enemies avoid all-target attacks.
Reaction survival matters; she has no innate team protection.
Only one personal debuff is removed by Fast Track, and its cooldown still matters.

teams.name: Anti-area focus
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Carmen and Frey keep Roberta alive, and her attacks can help Smile trigger on Aqua Bomb.
teams.playstyle: Focus Smile’s marked survivor; let Fast Track react automatically and keep healing available for enemy area bursts.

teams.name: Debuff-supported brawler
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Summer Luna provides DEF support, dress Asherah heals/cleanses the party and Lydia slows enemies.
teams.playstyle: Keep Roberta healthy, use enemy area turns as opportunities for reaction pressure, and avoid overlapping unnecessary support cooldowns.

alternatives.why: Amora has the higher published PvP rating and offers proactive area pressure, an explicit extra turn and conditional full self-cleanse when the opponent will not trigger Fast Track.
alternatives.tradeoff: Roberta retains direct anti-area retaliation, one-debuff reaction cleanse and potential-based critical-skill recovery; Amora does not reproduce that reaction package.

alternatives.why: Carmen is higher-rated in both modes and fills a missing carry-protection role with damage sharing, reactive recovery and targeted cleanse when the team already has damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: This replaces an attacker with support. Roberta still provides direct single-target damage and punishes enemy all-target attacks.

alternatives.why: Fei is another focused reaction attacker when the opponents can miss rather than repeatedly use all-target attacks.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her damage trigger depends on evasion instead of taking an area hit; she lacks Roberta’s one-debuff reaction cleanse and innate on-attack critical chance.

recon-knuckle.research_note: Public character build reviewed; gear details were image-only or gated, so no unseen set or slot recommendation is claimed.

recon-amulet.summary:
Lugh turns allies’ non-attack skills into Snow Blossom, then activates Swift Decree to replace her basic with Subdual Slash. Her damage window depends on managing those stacks and Nova Force, with DEF Down and ultimate delay as added utility.

This is a team-dependent carry, with non-attacking allies supplying the flowers his enhanced attacks consume. Start by checking flowers and Swift Decree, then decide whether to extend the sequence with Nova. ATK and critical investment pay off only if the engine stays supplied. A party of four attackers makes that engine much harder to sustain.
recon-amulet.watch: Her own-turn restrictions exclude additional triggered skills. Snow Blossom is spent by Subdual Slash, and a non-Nova slash resets its growing burst bonus; do not promise an endless extra-turn loop.
recon-amulet.dependency_note: Non-attack allies build Snow Blossom before Swift Decree. Nova Force availability and turn order determine how much of the slash window is usable.

skill_order.name: Way of the Exorcist
skill_order.why: Passive levels improve Winterborne Quartet’s turn progress per Snow Blossom from 20% to 40%; they also add ATK.

skill_order.name: Winterborne Quartet
skill_order.why: Levels 4 and 8 increase Banishing Mark application chance; this is the switch into Swift Decree.

skill_order.name: Subdual Charm
skill_order.why: The basic becomes Subdual Slash during the window, making its damage investment relevant.

skill_order.name: Heaven Forbids Evil, Justice Strikes
skill_order.why: Levels 4 and 8 improve DEF Down reliability; invest after the core window unless ultimate delay is your main need.

rotation: Have allies use useful non-attack support before Winterborne Quartet, while Lugh does not yet have Swift Decree; do not waste healing just to feed stacks.
Use Heaven Forbids Evil, Justice Strikes outside Swift Decree when its DEF Down, ultimate delay, Nova Force and one Snow Blossom are useful; its listed cooldown is ten turns.
Once Snow Blossom is available, use Winterborne Quartet on Lugh’s own turn to activate Swift Decree. More stored flowers give more progress toward her next turn.

During Swift Decree, Subdual Charm automatically becomes Subdual Slash on her own turn. Budget Nova Bursts and flowers; the basic Nova only grants an extra turn when both named buffs are present. Stop assuming the chain when flowers run out.

best_partners.why: Her two non-attack support skills can seed Snow Blossom while healing and cleansing.
Targeted heal and revive/support are non-attacks that feed flowers before Swift Decree.
Cleaning Service is a non-attack that adds a Barrier and ATK Up while helping the flower setup.

recon-amulet.build_tip: ATK, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG for slash damage; SPD to enter the prepared window. Add Effect Hit for marks and DEF Down rather than assuming 100% listed chance bypasses resistance. Journey option: The Indomitable Masterpiece is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
recon-amulet.tier_reason: Both mode ratings fit a conditional single-target attacker who needs flower setup, Nova resources and careful own-turn sequencing. PvE allows planning a damage window if the enemy permits debuffs; PvP can interrupt the support setup. Her mark and ultimate delay do not make the kit a universal control solution.
recon-amulet.investment: Prioritize the passive turn-gain levels, then the basic and Winterborne Quartet according to whether damage or debuff reliability is limiting you. Both debuff skills improve application at levels 4 and 8. No unique potential is listed. All quoted upper effects require the corresponding skill/passive level; stored maximum stats are not equal-investment combat results or a zero-star promise. The local star rows do not establish a combat unlock threshold. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 2 at level 40, listing +4 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
recon-amulet.pve_note: Plan a supported single-target damage window. Ultimate cooldown increase only matters on enemies with a susceptible ultimate cooldown; do not count it as boss control by default.
recon-amulet.pvp_note: Can pressure one target through extra own turns and ultimate delay. Interrupting the support setup or denying debuffs makes the window less valuable; listed burst percentages do not prove a lethal combo.

kit_explanation.name: Subdual Charm
kit_explanation.explanation: Subdual Charm adds Chill on a basic attack. On her own turn with Swift Decree it becomes Subdual Slash, which consumes one Snow Blossom, gains a successive-Nova damage bonus, and applies a one-turn Banishing Mark. A non-Nova hit or losing Swift Decree resets that bonus; additional triggered skills do not inherit the mark effects.

kit_explanation.name: Winterborne Quartet
kit_explanation.explanation: Winterborne Quartet is a single-target attack with a listed five-turn cooldown and Banishing Mark chance rising from 75% to 100% at levels 4 and 8. Each mark increases basic-skill damage taken by 5%, up to three applications; this is not general DEF Down.

kit_explanation.name: Heaven Forbids Evil, Justice Strikes
kit_explanation.explanation: Heaven Forbids Evil, Justice Strikes has a listed ten-turn cooldown. On her own turn it attempts two-turn DEF Down and adds one turn to the target’s ultimate cooldown. Without Swift Decree it also grants three extra Nova Force and a flower; with Swift Decree it grants an extra turn. These bonuses exclude additional triggered casts.

kit_explanation.name: Way of the Exorcist
kit_explanation.explanation: Way of the Exorcist starts the first battle with two Nova Force and adds damage per Chill stack. Other allies’ non-attacks grant flowers while Swift Decree is absent. Her own-turn Winterborne Quartet converts that preparation into Swift Decree and turn progress per flower, with the passive’s upper level reaching 40% per flower, capped at three flowers.

pros: Non-attack support skills become offensive setup rather than downtime.
Banishing Mark specifically rewards repeated basic/slash damage.
DEF Down and ultimate cooldown delay can support the rest of the team.
His passive begins battle with two Nova Force.
cons: Depends on support timing, flower supply and shared Nova resources.
Ten-turn listed ultimate cooldown makes careless usage costly.
Own-turn restrictions and burst-reset rules limit additional-attack shortcuts.

teams.name: Prepared slash carry
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Frey and Emily offer non-attack setup, Emily buffs Lugh and Lydia supplies a second source of debuffs.
teams.playstyle: Build flowers with needed support, switch with Winterborne Quartet, then spend only the Nova Force the window can sustain.

teams.name: Rescue-supported focus
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Elisa and Carmen have non-attack support, while Ceres supplies dispel and single-target disruption.
teams.playstyle: Protect Lugh as the intended highest-ATK oath target, prepare flowers, and attack after Ceres has attempted to remove enemy protection.

alternatives.why: Trish offers a simpler single-target finisher with Leap-based DEF penetration.
alternatives.tradeoff: She depends on kills for resets and does not offer Lugh’s flower conversion or ultimate delay.

alternatives.why: Ceres has higher published ratings in both modes and offers area dispel plus single-target stun/turn reduction when the team cannot afford flower setup.
alternatives.tradeoff: She trades Lugh’s supported slash window for control that may be resisted or ineffective on bosses.

recon-amulet.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

independent-vagabond.summary:
Fei is an evasive single-target attacker. A successful evasion triggers Lunar Shadow against the attacker, builds Chill and grows her passive ATK. Her ultimate spends Chill for a burst with DEF penetration at full stacks; she is strongest when enemies attack her and can actually miss.

Choose Fei for fights where opponents can miss and you can survive the attempts that connect. Evasion triggers her special automatically, giving Sure Hit, two Chill and an ATK Down attempt against the attacker. Five successful evasions can build a further 20% ATK through the passive. Her ultimate spends Chill even below five, so check the resource before expecting its 20% DEF penetration. A protector or healer remains valuable because evasion is not guaranteed damage prevention.
independent-vagabond.watch: Evasion Up is not immunity. Sure Hit and other accuracy tools can undermine her plan, and allies who force every attack away from her reduce Lunar Shadow opportunities. Her listed maximum SPD is only 90 despite the evasive identity.
independent-vagabond.dependency_note: She supplies her own evasion and ATK buff, but does not heal. ACC Down from Haydee or Bell is a functional partner effect; a healer is still needed when evasion fails.

skill_order.name: Silent Wind Lucent Moon
skill_order.why: Take level 6 for the ultimate cooldown, then damage upgrades if she is the carry.

skill_order.name: Lunar Shadow
skill_order.why: Improve her reactive damage and ATK Down application at levels 4/8.

skill_order.name: Path of the Celestial Art
skill_order.why: Passive levels improve ATK gained from evasion; they cannot make a dodge certain.

skill_order.name: Lunar Eclipse
skill_order.why: Basic damage is useful but less distinctive than the reaction and stack-spending attack.

rotation: If safe, build Chill with Lunar Eclipse and automatic Lunar Shadow reactions before Silent Wind Lucent Moon.
Use Silent Wind Lucent Moon at maximum Chill when the DEF penetration matters; use it earlier for a needed finish or ATK buff rather than following a fixed turn script.
Never queue Lunar Shadow manually. If opponents prevent evasion or avoid Fei, assess her as a slower direct attacker and protect or replace her accordingly.

best_partners.why: Haydee's ACC Down can support evasion, and Guard shares damage when Fei is hit.
Bell's area ACC Down can make multiple enemies less accurate; her Silence and buff removal can disrupt an accuracy-buffer.
Ceres heals failed dodges and cleanses debuffs that interfere with Fei's next action.
Frey offers a direct full cleanse and Barriers instead of relying on evasion to prevent every hit.

independent-vagabond.build_tip: Prioritize ATK and damage consistency, then SPD and survival. If Lone Seeker is available, its conditional 100% CRIT Rate buff changes crit needs during the post-evasion window; it is not permanent coverage. Today’s Step Forward supports Vitality for durability, adding one Vitality during training after 50 Bond. Include Strength training for the ATK attacks.
independent-vagabond.tier_reason: The A+ PvE / S PvP split fits an evasion-and-counter kit that can punish susceptible opponents but is inconsistent against bosses or accuracy tools. Full-Chill penetration is useful even when evasion is unreliable, but does not replace lost reactions.
independent-vagabond.investment: Prioritize the ultimate cooldown and Lunar Shadow's application/damage upgrades. Lone Seeker adds one maximum Toughness and grants Essence of the Celestial Art after evasion; that one-turn buff lists +100% CRIT Rate. Its exact unlock requirement is not supplied. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
independent-vagabond.pve_note: Useful against enemies that attack Fei repeatedly and can miss. Against unavoidable hits or fights where she is never attacked, the reactive engine contributes much less; do not deliberately expose her to lethal damage for stacks.
independent-vagabond.pvp_note: ACC Down support can help her punish attackers with Lunar Shadow. Sure Hit opponents, removed Evasion Up and burst through failed dodges remain practical counters; this is a matchup plan, not tested dodge reliability.

kit_explanation.name: Lunar Eclipse
kit_explanation.explanation: Lunar Eclipse is the basic single-target hit and adds one Chill. Its Nova grants a one-turn ATK buff on attack and adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Lunar Shadow
kit_explanation.explanation: Lunar Shadow fires automatically at the attacker after Fei evades an attack. It adds two Chill, gives one turn of Sure Hit and attempts one turn of ATK Down. ATK Down chance rises from 75% to 100% through levels 4 and 8. No cooldown is listed; do not invent a selectable cast or an extra per-turn cap.

kit_explanation.name: Silent Wind Lucent Moon
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Silent Wind Lucent Moon hits one target and grants ATK Up for two turns. At maximum Chill it penetrates 20% of the target's DEF; it then removes all Chill even if cast below maximum. This is a payoff to inspect, not a reason to delay every available finish.

kit_explanation.name: Path of the Celestial Art
kit_explanation.explanation: Path of the Celestial Art grants Evasion Up at battle start and at the end of each turn. Successful evasion after being attacked adds an ATK stack, up to five; each stack rises from 2% to 4% across passive levels, and later levels add baseline ATK. The Evasion Up effect lists 50% evasion, not a guaranteed dodge.

pros: Automatic Lunar Shadow adds damage and Chill when evasion succeeds.
Maximum-Chill ultimate penetrates part of enemy DEF.
Repeated evasion increases ATK rather than only preventing damage.
Lunar Shadow supplies Sure Hit for the next attack window.
cons: Miss-dependent reactions can disappear against accuracy tools.
No listed self-heal covers failed evasion.
Chill is spent by the ultimate even below its penetration threshold.

teams.name: Accuracy pressure (theorycraft)
teams.why: Haydee and Bell attempt ACC Down while Ceres heals; Haydee also shares some damage that evasion fails to avoid.
teams.playstyle: Keep ACC Down on dangerous attackers, heal Fei after failed dodges, and spend full Chill on an important target.

teams.name: Protected duelist (theorycraft)
teams.why: Frey handles Barriers and cleansing, Bell provides ACC Down, and Dana can buff Fei if she is the highest-ATK other ally.
teams.playstyle: Let Fei take only survivable pressure; use support buffs for her actual damage window and never assume every attack misses.

alternatives.why: Lacy is a stronger PvE-rated alternative with SPD Up, a broad ATK-reducing mark and conditional self-healing.
alternatives.tradeoff: Building or obtaining a separate profile costs resources; Lacy's mark-dependent recovery does not reproduce Fei's evasion reactions.

alternatives.why: Carnelia has higher published PvP utility through Buff Block, turn delay and a lethal-damage survival response.
alternatives.tradeoff: She is an area/control attacker, not an evasive duelist, and needs a different damage and survival plan.

independent-vagabond.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

grace-dualsword.summary:
Ordinary Epindel is a Moon focused attacker who rewards attacking while free of debuffs. Relentless Effort removes two debuffs from herself, grants ATK Up/Immunity and an extra turn; Hawk of Orlan then gains damage if she is clean. Moon ally crits feed Chill for her basic payoff.

Play the self-cleanse into the clean-state ultimate window rather than spending every turn on basics. The setup removes two debuffs, so check whether anything remains before counting the 30% damage bonus. ATK and critical investment support her focused role, while Moon allies help feed Chill. Her personal recovery option costs Nova and cannot serve as the team’s routine healing plan.
grace-dualsword.watch: Her cleanse and Immunity are self-only, and Immunity can be removed by buff removal. The basic spends Chill even when it is below five, so repeatedly basic attacking can prevent the full-stack bonus. She is distinct from the Sun wedding variant.
grace-dualsword.dependency_note: She manages her own debuffs and attack buffs. Moon allies with reliable crits help build Chill, while a defender/healer supplies the team utility and sustain her self-focused kit lacks.

skill_order.name: Relentless Effort
skill_order.why: Level 6 and 10 reduce cooldown; level 9 completes the listed chance to gain three Chill, improving self-clean setup.

skill_order.name: Hawk of Orlan
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown and level 10 extends SPD Up to three turns; the clean-self bonus is central to focused damage.

skill_order.name: Orlan Style Swordmanship
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later investment unless the team regularly supplies full Chill for its passive payoff.

rotation: Use Relentless Effort when two removals can clear important self debuffs or when ATK Up/Immunity prepares a damage window; it grants an extra turn.
Use Hawk of Orlan while no debuffs remain for its 30% damage bonus. Check that a third debuff did not survive the self-cleanse before counting the bonus.
If Moon ally crits have filled Chill, use Orlan Style Swordmanship for the passive's full-stack bonus. Otherwise a needed attack is still valid, but it spends the existing Chill and restarts buildup.
Use Nova basic for self lifesteal when necessary; ordinary basics do not heal. Keep external recovery available rather than treating Immunity as damage prevention.

best_partners.why: All In improves Moon teammates' crit consistency, helping feed Noble Bearing; Epindel's Moon attacks also feed Frey's Cash In.
Claire's own crit ramp makes her a plausible Moon critical-hit source for Chill, while the pair focus a durable target.
Moon Emily supplies targeted barrier/ATK Up and party DEF Up, filling defensive jobs Epindel's self-cleanse cannot cover.

grace-dualsword.build_tip: Use ATK, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG, with enough SPD to act before Immunity expires. Add durability for damage she cannot prevent. Self resistance is not a substitute for reading whether her two-debuff removal actually clears the harmful effects. Journey option: Till Death Do Us Part is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
grace-dualsword.tier_reason: The stored B PvE / C PvP ratings fit a functional but self-focused single-target kit with little team utility or enemy denial. PvE can allow clean-self attack windows and Moon crit resource support; faster PvP disruption, buff removal and area pressure expose her limits.
grace-dualsword.investment: Relentless Effort level 6/10 cooldown and level-9 stack reliability are more actionable than inventing a star target. Hawk level 6 improves cooldown; level 10 extends SPD Up. Noble Bearing's full-Chill basic bonus rises from 10% to 20% across passive levels, with ATK added later. No potentials are listed; an unrelated resistance description conflicts with the passive prose, so do not build around an unverified extra resistance ramp. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
grace-dualsword.pve_note: Use her self-clean setup against fights that allow a focused clean-state hit. If the team needs area clear, party cleanse or a breaker, another slot choice may solve more of the encounter even if Epindel can survive individually.
grace-dualsword.pvp_note: Relentless Effort can recover from removable self debuffs only if she is allowed to use the skill. It cannot save controlled teammates, remove every stacked debuff or prevent buff stripping; these limits explain a more modest PvP role.

kit_explanation.name: Orlan Style Swordmanship
kit_explanation.explanation: Orlan Style Swordmanship is the exact stored basic name. It attacks one enemy and grants Chill; Noble Bearing then spends Chill for its basic-damage rule. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and 30% lifesteal for the attack, rather than permanent recovery.

kit_explanation.name: Relentless Effort
kit_explanation.explanation: Relentless Effort is a self-only non-attacking skill on a listed six-turn cooldown, reduced at levels 6 and 10. It removes two self debuffs, grants three-turn ATK Up and Immunity, attempts three Chill with chance rising from 75% to 100% by level 9, and grants an extra turn. Nova restores her Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: Hawk of Orlan
kit_explanation.explanation: Hawk of Orlan hits one enemy on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It deals 30% more damage if Epindel has no debuffs on attack and grants two-turn SPD Up, extended to three at level 10. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Noble Bearing
kit_explanation.explanation: Noble Bearing grants Chill when a Moon ally critically hits. At five Chill, her basic gets 10–20% extra damage by passive level; using the basic consumes Chill, so partial stacks can also be lost. Higher levels add ATK. The local descriptions conflict about an additional resistance benefit; treat the stated Chill/basic loop as the usable plan and do not rely on an extra resistance ramp.

pros: Self-cleanse plus Immunity helps establish a clean attack window.
Setup grants an extra turn to use the buff window immediately.
Moon ally crits can feed a full-Chill basic without needing to build only through her own turns.
Nova basic offers a conditional self-recovery option.
cons: No area attack, party recovery or team cleanse.
Basic use spends partial Chill, making the full-stack payoff timing-sensitive.
Immunity can be dispelled and the clean-self ultimate bonus fails if debuffs remain.

teams.name: Moon crit pursuit
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Frey helps Moon crits feed Chill, Emily protects Epindel and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses the party.
teams.playstyle: Use self-clean setup before Hawk when safe; inspect Chill before basics and avoid confusing Frey's crit support with healing.

teams.name: Two focused Moon attackers
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Claire supplies Moon crit opportunities, Emily protects the carry and Serpang provides party recovery plus enemy weakening.
teams.playstyle: Choose one priority target; Serpang does not cleanse, so use this only when self-cleanse and prevention cover the actual debuff threat.

alternatives.why: Claire is a higher-rated focused Moon attacker with crit ramp, next-turn progress and a triggered special loop.
alternatives.tradeoff: Epindel retains self-cleanse, three-turn Immunity and an explicit clean-self damage window, which Claire's ordinary skills do not replace.

alternatives.why: Lyn is a higher-utility PvE damage slot when the team needs both area clearing and a focused form plus Star support.
alternatives.tradeoff: Epindel keeps a simpler self-cleanse/Immunity plan and Moon critical-hit synergy; Lyn has different attribute and stance requirements.

grace-dualsword.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

starpiercer-omega.summary:
Omega builds Leap from her attacks and other Star allies’ attacks, then converts full Leap at turn start into Power-Up Star. Those stars make Mega Punch! repeat, so she is a ramping area attacker rather than an immediate opening nuke.

Build a Star attacking core before treating repeated punches as dependable damage. The next turn-start conversion matters even if allies have already supplied five Leap, so speed and protection support the ramp alongside ATK and critical stats. Use the repeat skill when it solves the current wave. Waiting for three stars can waste more time than their final bonus saves.
starpiercer-omega.watch: The repeat attacks only occur on her own turn and do not inherit Mega Punch!’s Nova Toughness bonus. Full Leap converts at the start of her turn, not immediately when a teammate adds the fifth stack.
starpiercer-omega.dependency_note: Star allies directly feed Auto-Hunt System. Include attackers who take turns, not just a full roster of non-attack supports.

skill_order.name: Auto-Hunt System
skill_order.why: The passive raises allied-attack Leap chance from 70% to 100% and adds ATK at later levels.

skill_order.name: Mega Punch!
skill_order.why: Mega Punch! is the repeat payoff; level 6 reduces its listed cooldown.

skill_order.name: The Biggest and Coolest One!
skill_order.why: The ultimate supplies three Leap and ATK Up, with another cooldown reduction at level 6.

skill_order.name: Pew Pew!
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later upgrade after the ramp and repeat skill.

rotation: Use The Biggest and Coolest One! when its three Leap help reach the next turn-start conversion, or when immediate single-target damage matters.

Track Power-Up Star before Mega Punch!: one star adds one repeat, two stars add two repeats, and three stars retain two repeats plus 10% more damage. Do not delay a needed wave clear indefinitely for the final star.
Use Pew Pew! while cooldowns recover and let Star allies attack to supply more Leap. At three Power-Up Star, full Leap is no longer consumed by the passive.
Budget Nova Burst for the initial Mega Punch! hit only; its Toughness bonus is explicitly excluded from additional repeated instances.

best_partners.why: A Star attacker whose basic and reaction pressure can supply allied attack opportunities while DEF Down helps damage.
Star single-target pressure and automatic reactions can feed Omega’s passive when the appropriate attacks occur.
Frey’s recovery is enhanced on Star allies and supplies the cleanse Omega lacks; her support turns themselves are non-attacks.

starpiercer-omega.build_tip: ATK and critical stats for repeated damage, with SPD to reach turn-start conversions. Power-Up Star grants SPD, so monitor actual turn order rather than assuming every stack instantly grants an action. Journey option: The Imaginary Pioneer is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +6% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
starpiercer-omega.tier_reason: The PvE rating fits repeated-wave payoff after ramping; the much lower PvP rating reflects delayed Power-Up Star conversion and a damage kit without immediate hard control. Star-heavy team setup matters in both modes.
starpiercer-omega.investment: Prioritize Auto-Hunt System’s allied trigger reliability and Mega Punch!’s level-6 cooldown. The ultimate’s level-6 cooldown supports more frequent three-Leap setup. Potential arrays are empty; do not budget around an unlisted unique effect. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 10 at level 200, listing +6 SPD; it is not part of the starting stat line.
starpiercer-omega.pve_note: Best considered for encounters long enough to build Power-Up Star and then hit multiple enemies. Against a short wave or lone boss, compare the setup cost with a more immediate attacker.
starpiercer-omega.pvp_note: Vulnerable to pressure before enough stars exist. She does not bring a team cleanse or reliable opening disruption, so protect her and treat the repeat window as conditional.

kit_explanation.name: Pew Pew!
kit_explanation.explanation: Pew Pew! is a single-target basic granting one Leap. Leap’s direct benefit is a small stacking damage bonus against Moon enemies, but Omega also uses it as fuel for her passive.

kit_explanation.name: Mega Punch!
kit_explanation.explanation: Mega Punch! attacks all enemies with a listed four-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. Power-Up Star changes the number of additional Mega Punch! instances on her own turn: one at one star, two at two or three stars, with a further damage bonus at three. The initial Nova bonus does not spread to repeats.

kit_explanation.name: The Biggest and Coolest One!
kit_explanation.explanation: The Biggest and Coolest One! attacks one enemy, gives two-turn ATK Up and three Leap. It has a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6, making it both a damage action and ramp tool.

kit_explanation.name: Auto-Hunt System
kit_explanation.explanation: Auto-Hunt System grants Leap after another Star ally attacks with 70% to 100% chance by passive level. At Omega’s turn start, five Leap are consumed for one Power-Up Star unless that buff is already capped at three. Each star grants 5% SPD; converting stacks is automatic.

pros: Power-Up Star can turn one area skill into several attacks.
Ultimate supplies three Leap without needing several basic turns.
Star teammates directly accelerate her core mechanic.
Power-Up Star also supplies stacking personal speed.
cons: Ramp is gated by her turn starts, not just the number of ally attacks.
Few defensive or control tools if pressured early.
Repeat Nova Toughness damage is explicitly restricted.

teams.name: Star ramp core
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Two Star damage allies feed Leap while Frey sustains the group and cleanses a priority target.
teams.playstyle: Use attacks to prepare conversions, then spend Mega Punch! when enough stars exist for the current wave.

teams.name: Protected repeat carry
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Smile supplies marked-target follow-ups and Star attacks, with Carmen/Frey covering survival.
teams.playstyle: Keep Omega the intended highest-ATK oath recipient; attack Aqua Bomb targets when useful and avoid expecting support non-attacks to feed Leap.

alternatives.why: Voyager Luna offers more immediate area damage and Bind area vulnerability, with stronger published ratings in both modes.
alternatives.tradeoff: She trades Omega’s repeat scaling for Insight management and chance-based vulnerability.

alternatives.why: Ceres has far higher published PvP utility through dispel, turn denial and Stun.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not offer Omega’s Power-Up Star repeat engine, which can still suit longer wave fights.

starpiercer-omega.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

bunny-knight.summary:
Bunny Charlotte is a Sun single-target attacker who also buffs the party's ATK. Song of the Toast grants a DEF-penetrating Lucky Token and an extra turn; while the token lasts, her own-turn basic repeats once. Sun teammates help refill Ignition for Cornered Rabbit.

Use Charlotte (Heart of Monastir) with Sun teammates whose normal turns refill Ignition, then keep Lucky Token active through her setup skill. That skill also gives the whole party ATK Up and Charlotte an immediate extra turn. Her own-turn basic repeats automatically once during the token window. She trades area coverage for focused pressure, and the ultimate’s reset wording remains ambiguous; do not build a plan that assumes an unverified permanent loop.
bunny-knight.watch: Cornered Rabbit says it removes Ignition and then checks maximum stacks for a reset. That ordering is ambiguous, so do not promise infinite recasts. Three Ignition rolls from Song become certain only at skill level 10.
bunny-knight.dependency_note: Her core attacks work without a Sun party, but allied Sun turns directly generate Ignition. Choose Sun allies who also supply protection, healing or damage rather than four attackers merely for the attribute.

skill_order.name: Song of the Toast
skill_order.why: Prioritize the level-6 cooldown reduction, then level 10 if you need all three Ignition rolls to be certain.

skill_order.name: Cornered Rabbit
skill_order.why: Its level-6 cooldown reduction provides ordinary availability even if the conditional reset is uncertain.

skill_order.name: Bunny Step
skill_order.why: The token repeats this basic, so damage upgrades pay off across repeated hits.

rotation: Use Song of the Toast before an allied damage window to give everyone ATK Up and gain Lucky Token, then use its extra turn according to current Ignition.
With Lucky Token active, Bunny Step on her own turn repeats automatically once and helps refill Ignition; do not manually cast the repeat.
Use Cornered Rabbit at five Ignition when practical, or earlier to secure a necessary kill. Check the actual cooldown afterward rather than assuming the ambiguous reset works.
Let useful Sun teammates take turns to build the next stack window. Nova Cornered Rabbit adds lifesteal if Charlotte needs self-recovery; ordinary use does not.

best_partners.why: Every allied Sun Tyria turn supplies Ignition; Tyria also uses Charlotte's team ATK Up for her mark-based damage.
Hilde's Sun turns feed Ignition while opening ally barriers cover Charlotte's setup turn.
Serpang's Sun turns feed Ignition, and his party heal gives enhanced recovery to Sun allies.

bunny-knight.build_tip: Use ATK, CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG with sufficient SPD to renew Lucky Token. Stored 90 SPD is a genuine timing concern; allies feeding stacks cannot replace her own turn. DEF penetration comes from the token, not Effect Hit. A Clumsy Way to Relieve Desire supports Strength, while A Knight’s Oath supports Vitality. The former adds two Strength during training after 50 Bond.
bunny-knight.tier_reason: The stored S+ PvE / S PvP ratings fit sustained Sun-team damage, party ATK Up, repeated basics and Lucky Token DEF penetration. PvE gives her time to use allied turns and rebuild Ignition; short PvP pressure makes her 90-SPD starting profile and setup more relevant. The ambiguous reset wording does not justify assuming unlimited ultimate casts.
bunny-knight.investment: Song of the Toast increases each of its three stack rolls from 75% to 100%; that is a meaningful reliability purchase beyond its level-6 cooldown. Rabbit's Luck scales basic-triggered next-turn progress from 6% to 10%, plus ATK at higher passive levels. No potentials are recorded. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
bunny-knight.pve_note: Single sturdy targets give her time to use Lucky Token basics; A Sun healer and defender feed her stacks while doing needed jobs. She has no native area damage for clearing large waves. Belgras gains Action gauge after a single-target hit from a unit carrying Devouring Thorns; repeated basics can accelerate that boss.
bunny-knight.pvp_note: Use Song for a team attack window rather than greedily waiting for every stack. Do not rely on a reset chain to beat an enemy cleanse, burst team or turn disruption.

kit_explanation.name: Bunny Step
kit_explanation.explanation: Bunny Step hits one enemy and grants one Ignition. With Lucky Token on her own turn, Rabbit's Luck repeats it once; each use also provides passive next-turn progress. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Song of the Toast
kit_explanation.explanation: Song of the Toast is a non-attacking party buff on a listed five-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. It gives two-turn ATK Up, three-turn Lucky Token to Charlotte and three separate Ignition rolls, from 75% each at level 1 to 100% at level 10, then grants an extra turn. Lucky Token penetrates 20% DEF. Nova restores her Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: Cornered Rabbit
kit_explanation.explanation: Cornered Rabbit hits one enemy on a listed six-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. It gains 5% damage per Ignition up to five and consumes Ignition. It also lists a full-stack cooldown reset, but the post-consumption wording needs confirmation. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and converts 30% of damage into self-healing.

kit_explanation.name: Rabbit's Luck
kit_explanation.explanation: Rabbit's Luck automatically grants Ignition when another Sun ally starts a turn. It adds 6–10% action gauge, progress toward the next turn, after Bunny Step depending on passive level, and enables the token's once-per-turn own-turn basic repeat. Higher levels also add ATK.

pros: Team ATK buff and an extra setup turn combine offense with support.
Lucky Token grants undispellable DEF penetration.
Sun supports generate her resource without abandoning their normal jobs.
Her ultimate’s Nova Burst converts damage into personal healing.
cons: No area attack, cleanse or ordinary healing.
Sun turns and Lucky Token uptime heavily influence her output.
The reset text is internally awkward; lower-level Song has random stack generation.

teams.name: Sun single-target core
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Tyria adds mark-based pressure, Hilde supplies opening ally barriers, and Serpang heals with a Sun bonus. All three feed Charlotte's passive by taking turns.
teams.playstyle: Buff ATK before the attackers act; let protection and healing determine when to spend cooldowns.

teams.name: Sun utility attack line
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Petra contributes DEF Down, Hilde absorbs pressure and Serpang heals/debuffs. Every teammate is also a Sun-turn source.
teams.playstyle: Try to land Petra's DEF Down before Charlotte's focused damage; healing and debuff success remain conditional.

alternatives.why: The original Charlotte can give one ally CRIT Rate Up and ATK Up and applies ATK Down to an enemy.
alternatives.tradeoff: More targeted utility, but lacks Bunny Charlotte's Lucky Token repeat loop and partywide ATK buff.

alternatives.why: Bunny Claire brings a crit-driven single-target loop with explicit bonus damage against buffed enemies.
alternatives.tradeoff: Does not need Sun turns, but gives no team ATK Up and prefers a different resource plan.

bunny-knight.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

west-beamsword.summary:
Western Ceres is an offensive controller: she removes a buff from every enemy, slows them with Freeze, then pushes a dangerous target away from its next turn. Her biggest advantage is creating another opportunity to act before the opponent. She is not the healing Maid Ceres variant.

Use Ceres (Western Liberators) to disrupt several opponents, then concentrate on the enemy whose next action is most dangerous. At five Chill, Blade Gale attempts a 70% Action gauge reduction as well as Stun. Earthshaker returns gauge according to targets hit, making enemy count part of her tempo. Boss immunity can remove much of that advantage, so verify the encounter before replacing a sustained attacker with her.
west-beamsword.watch: Freeze is a small speed reduction plus damage over time, not a skipped turn; Stun is her actual turn-stopping effect. Bosses that resist control reduce her value sharply.
west-beamsword.dependency_note: Her control works without a required attribute partner. She still needs protection and enough speed to act before a dangerous enemy; Moon allies add useful interactions rather than unlocking her basic function.

skill_order.name: 7th Form: Earthshaker
skill_order.why: Prioritize its level-6 cooldown reduction and level-4/8 Freeze-chance upgrades when using her for group control.

skill_order.name: 21st Form: Blade Gale
skill_order.why: Its level-6 cooldown reduction and level-4/8 Stun-chance upgrades improve repeated single-target disruption.

skill_order.name: Order by Force
skill_order.why: Available passive upgrades increase the turn progress earned from Earthshaker. Do not assume the maximum passive belongs to a first copy.

skill_order.name: 1st Form: Crescent Moon
skill_order.why: Basic damage is useful between cooldowns, but its small damage steps matter less than securing the control tools.

rotation: Against several enemies with useful buffs, open with Earthshaker to remove one buff each and attempt Freeze and Isolation. Its passive turn-progress reward scales with the number hit, so it is stronger against a group than a lone boss.
Use Blade Gale on the enemy whose next turn matters most. More Chill increases its gauge reduction, but do not wait for five stacks if an immediate Stun or pushback could prevent a defeat.
Attack a Frozen target with Crescent Moon or Blade Gale to use the passive's 30% damage bonus. Preserve Earthshaker for the next important buff wave when an immediate cast would accomplish little.
If the encounter blocks Stun, Freeze or gauge reduction, reassess her slot. Her damage remains usable, but a dedicated damage dealer can contribute more to an immunity-heavy boss.

best_partners.why: Bunny Frey supplies party CRIT Rate and gains turn progress and High Roller stacks after other Moon allies attack, including Ceres.
Wedding Carmen supplies healing and cleansing that Ceres lacks, and her Wedding March gives additional Chill to Moon allies.
Bell removes all buffs from one priority enemy and applies Silence, complementing Ceres's one-buff removal across the entire group.
Summer Luna adds team defense and reactive disruption against critical attackers, buying time for Ceres's next control cycle.

west-beamsword.build_tip: Prioritize SPD and sufficient Effect Hit for the target, then ATK and critical damage if her control is reliable. Add HP/DEF if she cannot survive an opening attack. Her listed maximum SPD is 106; equipment and turn order still decide who acts first. An Unseen Place supports Focus for Effect Hit; pair it with Strength training for damage. Its unique adds one Focus during training after 50 Bond.
west-beamsword.tier_reason: Published PvE A+ and PvP S+ fit a specialist whose buff removal, Stun and turn-progress disruption matter most against enemy teams. High PvP utility does not make her the strongest damage choice against every boss.
west-beamsword.investment: Secure the control-chance and cooldown upgrades before spending on small basic-damage increases. The passive's Earthshaker reward rises from 25% per target at its first level to 35% at the highest stored level. The profile does not establish an exact copy requirement or list a unique potential; do not equate maximum skill descriptions with zero-star performance.
west-beamsword.pve_note: Useful against waves where buff removal and delay prevent incoming damage. Against a lone control-immune boss, the smaller passive turn-progress reward and lost disruption make dedicated boss attackers more attractive. Demoraigis lists Stun immunity, so Blade Gale cannot supply its usual hard control there.
west-beamsword.pvp_note: Strong when she acts in time to remove protection or interrupt a key enemy. Check resistance and immunity before relying on a printed 100% chance, and distinguish Freeze's slow from Blade Gale's Stun.

kit_explanation.name: 1st Form: Crescent Moon
kit_explanation.explanation: Her basic attack hits one enemy and adds one Chill stack. Chill gives a small damage bonus against Sun enemies and also fuels Blade Gale's stronger turn-progress reduction. A Nova version adds Toughness damage and attempts an extra 15% enemy gauge reduction.

kit_explanation.name: 7th Form: Earthshaker
kit_explanation.explanation: Earthshaker hits everyone, attempts to remove one buff from each enemy, and applies two Freeze stacks plus Isolation. Freeze reduces speed and causes minor damage at turn start; Isolation reduces the chance of Preemptive Guard. She gains one Chill. Its listed five-turn cooldown has a level-6 reduction, and the passive returns turn progress for every target hit.

kit_explanation.name: 21st Form: Blade Gale
kit_explanation.explanation: Blade Gale hits one enemy, gives Ceres three turns of Western Winds for 25% more speed, and attempts a one-turn Stun. It also pushes the enemy's next turn back by 20%, plus 10% per Chill stack, up to 70%, then spends all Chill. Its listed five-turn cooldown has a level-6 reduction; Stun chance improves through skill upgrades.

kit_explanation.name: Order by Force
kit_explanation.explanation: This passive starts the first battle with two Chill. After Earthshaker, it advances Ceres toward her next turn for every enemy hit: 35% each at maximum passive level, capped at 175%. That is gauge gain, not a guarantee of several immediate extra turns. Crescent Moon and Blade Gale deal 30% more damage to Frozen targets; later passive levels also add ATK.

pros: Area buff removal and single-target Stun cover different enemy threats.
Earthshaker's turn-progress refund improves with enemy count.
She generates her own Freeze condition for stronger basic and ultimate damage.
Western Winds grants 25% SPD for three turns.
cons: No healing, Barrier or damage sharing for teammates.
Control-resistant bosses can remove the main reason to use her.
Maximum control chance and passive gauge gain require upgrades; raw SPD does not guarantee an opening turn.

teams.name: Moon pressure and recovery
teams.why: Ceres disrupts the enemy, Bunny Frey supplies critical chance, Professor M adds dual attacks and follow-ups, and Wedding Carmen supplies healing and cleansing. Moon attacks also feed Bunny Frey's passive.
teams.playstyle: Use Ceres to open a vulnerable target, then concentrate allied attacks there. Set actual ATK values so Wedding Carmen's starting Oath protects the intended ally; the lineup has no conventional defender.

teams.name: Control with burst protection
teams.why: Bell strips a priority target and Silences it, Ceres handles group buffs and delay, Summer Luna adds defense against critical pressure, and Maid Ceres heals and cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use Bell's full removal for the most protected enemy and Ceres's area removal for the rest. Keep Maid Ceres ready for the enemy response; control attempts can fail, and this composition sacrifices damage for safety.

alternatives.why: Choose Bell when the main problem is one heavily buffed enemy whose skills you need to Silence; her maximum stored SPD is 112 versus Ceres's 106.
alternatives.tradeoff: Bell offers full single-target buff removal, but not Ceres's combination of area removal, Stun and Chill-scaled gauge pushback. Actual gear can reverse their speed order.

alternatives.why: Consider Witch Asherah for a breakable boss where added Toughness damage and broken-target follow-ups matter more than control.
alternatives.tradeoff: She has no verified mode tier here and needs break windows to show that potential. Replacing Ceres gives up her buff removal and disruption; this is a conditional kit comparison, not a tested upgrade.

west-beamsword.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

west-rod.summary:
Original Lydia is a durable debuffer who makes enemies act more slowly and become easier to debuff. Unknown Hex is the center of her kit: establish a debuff, then her basic can keep applying Hex while her passive builds ATK. Her listed maximum HP is 39,345, but that is personal bulk rather than protection for allies.

Build her around applying Hex before expecting reliable follow-up pressure. Speed and Effect Hit help her reach susceptible targets, while ATK adds damage after the utility is covered. The short special cooldown supports repeated group attempts. Resistance and immunity still matter, so a Hex-immune boss removes much of her reason to occupy a slot.
west-rod.watch: The special checks for an existing Hex when it attacks; do not assume it first applies Hex and then earns its conditional gauge reduction on that same cast. Her passive wording and effect summary disagree on which attacks build ATK, so a basic-focused plan is the safer assumption.
west-rod.dependency_note: A teammate who establishes a debuff before Lydia's basic makes her loop easier to start. She benefits from extra basic attacks and needs a healer or protector; a Chaos-only lineup is not required.

skill_order.name: Void Within the Tome
skill_order.why: Prioritize its level-6 cooldown reduction if you need a dependable Hex setup on one enemy; later upgrades improve SPD Down chance.

skill_order.name: Seeker of the Void
skill_order.why: Available passive levels improve the ATK growth and personal HP that support a longer basic-focused fight.

skill_order.name: Invitation Beyond the Stars
skill_order.why: Its level-6/10 Hex-chance upgrades matter for group debuffing, but even the stored maximum is 75% before resistance checks.

skill_order.name: Touch of the Void
skill_order.why: Improve basic damage after the key utility upgrades, especially if allies frequently call her into basic attacks.

rotation: Start by putting a debuff on the intended target, through a teammate or Lydia's ultimate. Void Within the Tome attempts Hex and SPD Down and gives Lydia 30% progress toward her next turn.

Use Touch of the Void on that debuffed enemy to refresh a one-turn Hex through the passive and build Agitation. A basic-focused approach is useful when maintaining the debuff matters more than immediate area damage.
Use Invitation Beyond the Stars against a group, particularly when important targets already have Hex so its 15% gauge reduction can apply. Do not treat its 75% maximum Hex chance as certainty.

Reapply control before the enemy catches up and heal Lydia when required. Against an enemy that ignores slowing or resists the debuffs, use a stronger damage specialist instead of waiting for a loop that cannot function.

best_partners.why: Rosaria's group DEF Down establishes debuffs and adds burst damage while Lydia works on slowing targets. Lydia's Hex can help later debuff attempts, but cannot retroactively help a debuff already checked.

Waltz Asherah supplies healing and cleansing, and her rising Dual Attack chance can create more opportunities for allied basic attacks rather than forcing Lydia to spend every turn on a cooldown skill.
Emily's targeted Barrier and ATK buff can protect a fragile damage slot while Lydia supplies the slowing effects that Emily lacks.

west-rod.build_tip: Use SPD and enough Effect Hit to establish the loop, then ATK for damage and HP/DEF for survival. Her passive adds Effect Hit with Agitation, but late-fight stacks do not guarantee that the opening debuff lands. Journey option: A Satisfying Bloom is Focus-tagged, supporting Effect Hit for her debuff role; its listed training effectiveness is +7% at Arcana level 1. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
west-rod.tier_reason: Published PvE A and PvP B+ are plausible for a useful slowing specialist who needs setup and lacks the immediate protection or extra-action damage of stronger general choices. Her utility is encounter-dependent, and the source's generic description does not resolve the passive wording conflict.
west-rod.investment: Improve control uptime and application chance before basic damage. Seeker of the Void's highest stored description gives 6% ATK per qualifying attack, up to five stacks, compared with 4% initially; its effect summary narrows this to basic attacks. This guide does not assume broader stacking works or invent a copy requirement from passive levels. No unique potential is listed. Touch of Void is linked to Halloween Lydia in savior_sources, despite the shared character_id; it is not assumed available to Western Liberators Lydia. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 2 at level 40, listing +4 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
west-rod.pve_note: Useful in longer encounters where Hex and SPD Down work and allies can capitalize on reduced resistance. Against immune bosses, control contributes much less; her lower raw ATK means she is not an automatic replacement for a main damage dealer.
west-rod.pvp_note: The listed maximum SPD of 107 can support an early debuff turn with suitable gear. However, setup can fail against immunity, cleansing or a faster burst team, and she does not provide a full enemy buff strip.

kit_explanation.name: Touch of the Void
kit_explanation.explanation: The basic hits one target and adds Agitation, a small stacking damage bonus against Order enemies. At the reviewed passive level, using it against an enemy that already has any debuff also attempts a one-turn Unknown Hex. Nova adds Toughness damage and attempts a 15% pushback to the enemy's next turn.

kit_explanation.name: Invitation Beyond the Stars
kit_explanation.explanation: This three-turn-cooldown area attack adds Agitation and attempts two-turn Unknown Hex on each enemy. Its printed chance improves from 50% to 75% with upgrades. Hex lowers Effect RES by 20% and speed by 10%. If a target already has Hex when attacked, this skill also attempts to remove 15% of its progress toward its next turn.

kit_explanation.name: Void Within the Tome
kit_explanation.explanation: Her ultimate hits one target, adds Agitation and gives Lydia 30% progress toward her next turn. It attempts a two-turn Hex and a separate two-turn SPD Down, whose chance improves through upgrades. Its listed six-turn cooldown has a level-6 reduction. This is the clearer setup button for a specific enemy before returning to basic attacks.

kit_explanation.name: Seeker of the Void
kit_explanation.explanation: Agitation improves Lydia's Effect Hit by 6% per stack, up to five stacks. Attacking a debuffed enemy builds an ATK bonus, and a basic against a debuffed target can apply Hex. The skill description says attacks build ATK, while the effect summary says basics; plan around basics until that difference is verified. Higher passive levels also add up to 15% HP.

pros: Hex combines a speed reduction with reduced Effect RES for follow-up debuffs.
Her basic can maintain Hex instead of relying entirely on long cooldowns.
Personal HP and self-turn progress help her stay active in a longer control fight.
Her special revisits area Hex on a three-turn listed cooldown.
cons: An established debuff is needed to start the basic's Hex interaction.
The area Hex chance remains 75% at maximum skill level, before resistance checks.
No party healing or damage sharing, and the ATK-stacking wording is ambiguous.

teams.name: Protected debuff progression
teams.why: Rosaria supplies damage and DEF Down, Lydia slows enemies, Emily protects a chosen ally, and Waltz Asherah heals and cleanses. The roles complement one another without requiring a mono-attribute bonus.
teams.playstyle: Use whichever debuff can land before Lydia's basic, then maintain Hex on the priority enemy. Spend Emily's targeted support according to actual danger, and avoid delaying emergency healing to preserve an ideal sequence.

teams.name: Disrupt and finish
teams.why: Bell removes key buffs and Silences, Lydia adds slowing, Amora supplies damage and ACC Down, and Wedding Carmen heals while sharing damage with the highest-ATK ally.
teams.playstyle: Strip protection before relying on debuffs, then focus Amora on a vulnerable target. Tune actual ATK for the intended Oath recipient; control is conditional, so this is not a guaranteed lockdown.

alternatives.why: Ceres is usually the stronger disruption choice when you need immediate area buff removal, Stun and a larger conditional single-target pushback.
alternatives.tradeoff: She trades away Lydia's resistance-reducing Hex and basic-maintenance loop. Boss immunity can limit either controller, so check the fight rather than only the higher PvP rating.

alternatives.why: Rosaria is a stronger general damage choice when you want a large area hit plus DEF Down without waiting for Lydia's ATK stacks.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not replace Hex's resistance reduction or Lydia's sustained slowing. Availability and your actual build can matter more than upgrading an already-functional specialist.

west-rod.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

detective-professor.summary:
Professor M is an attack enabler who repeatedly brings the highest-ATK ally into the fight. Her basic grants that ally Sample Behavior Analysis and forces a dual attack; other allies' attacks feed her Chill and next-turn progress. At full Chill, an allied attack automatically triggers Evil Begets Evil.

Build Professor M around a carry whose basic attack is useful, then make that ally win the highest-ATK check. Her basic calls that ally into a forced Dual Attack, while allied attacks build Chill and speed her next turn. At five Chill an allied attack triggers the special automatically; it cannot be selected as a normal opener. The ultimate adds Target Engrave, increasing special-skill damage received by 20%, so the team still needs to focus the marked opponent.
detective-professor.watch: Evil Begets Evil is a reaction, not a selectable cooldown skill. Sample Behavior Analysis follows the current highest-ATK other ally and only one instance exists; buffs or gear can redirect it away from the intended carry.
detective-professor.dependency_note: Choose a carry whose basic is useful and make that ally the intended highest ATK. The team also needs enough attacking actions to refill Chill and a defender/healer to survive the cycle.

skill_order.name: The Magic Bullet
skill_order.why: The Magic Bullet level 6 improves cooldown and level 8 improves Target Engrave application chance to its listed 100%.

skill_order.name: Black or White
skill_order.why: A frequently used basic that initiates the forced dual attack; damage upgrades have repeated value.

skill_order.name: Evil Begets Evil
skill_order.why: Upgrade the automatic reaction for damage and levels 4/8 next-turn progress once the team generates it often; do not plan to cast it manually.

rotation: Use Black or White when a forced basic from the highest-ATK ally is useful; inspect who actually has the highest ATK rather than assuming the selected team role decides.
Use The Magic Bullet on the enemy that will receive special-skill attacks. The 50% gauge gain advances Professor M's next turn, while three Chill help prepare the reaction.

At five Chill, let the next allied attack trigger Evil Begets Evil automatically. Focus her recent target to take advantage of its target preference and, when available, its broken-target damage bonus.
Keep using basics to renew Sample Behavior Analysis; applying a new instance removes the old one. Spend defensive cooldowns according to incoming danger, not a fixed attack chain.

best_partners.why: A forced Prelude basic can add Thorns and potentially trigger Tyria's marked-target Requiem; both have explicit basic/follow-up reasons to work together.
Gwen gains Electric Shock from allied attacks and an extra stack from special attacks while in Standby; Professor M supplies repeated attacking actions and marks special vulnerability.
Emily's targeted ATK Up/barrier can support the intended highest-ATK carry while party DEF Up helps preserve the attack engine.

detective-professor.build_tip: Favor SPD, ATK and crit for frequent attacks, with Effect Hit if Target Engrave must land. Tune relative ATK within the actual party so the intended basic attacker receives Sample Behavior Analysis; maximum database ATK alone does not decide that. A Hedonist’s Diversion supports Endurance, giving one additional Endurance during training after 40 Bond. Pair defensive training with Strength for her ATK attacks.
detective-professor.tier_reason: The stored S+ PvE / S+ PvP ratings fit a kit that adds allied attacks, damage support, special-skill vulnerability and repeated self turn progress. The rating depends on choosing a useful highest-ATK partner and keeping allies attacking; isolated or heavily controlled teams lose that engine.
detective-professor.investment: The Magic Bullet levels 4/8 improve mark chance and level 6 reduces cooldown. Evil Begets Evil levels 4/8 raise its turn progress from 5% to 10% to 15%. Research Subject's ordinary-ally Chill roll grows from 50% to 100% across passive levels; do not assume top-level resource consistency on first copy. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
detective-professor.pve_note: Excellent kit fit for a long focused fight where the carry's basic matters and special attacks can exploit Target Engrave. A boss immune to the mark still permits the dual-attack plan, but removes that specific team damage benefit.
detective-professor.pvp_note: Attack suppression and carry targeting matter more than thematic team names. A fast team can feed reactions, but enemy control can stall the loop; her reaction and gauge gains are not a guaranteed no-response turn chain.

kit_explanation.name: Black or White
kit_explanation.explanation: Black or White hits one enemy and gives Chill. Research Subject then buffs the highest-ATK other ally and forces that ally into a dual attack. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and 20% next-turn progress to Professor M.

kit_explanation.name: Evil Begets Evil
kit_explanation.explanation: Evil Begets Evil is an automatic reaction after an allied attack if Professor M has five Chill. It consumes Chill, attacks her preferred recent target, gains 30% damage against a broken enemy and advances her next turn by 5–15% through skill levels 1/4/8. No manual cast or normal cooldown sequence is established.

kit_explanation.name: The Magic Bullet
kit_explanation.explanation: The Magic Bullet hits one enemy on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It gives three Chill and 50% next-turn progress, and attempts two-turn Target Engrave with chance increasing from 75% to 100% through upgrades. Target Engrave makes special skills deal 20% more damage to that enemy; it is not a universal damage-taken mark. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Research Subject
kit_explanation.explanation: Research Subject automatically gives Sample Behavior Analysis after Black or White and forces a dual attack with the highest-ATK other ally. Other allies attacking give Professor M 4% next-turn progress and a 50–100% Chill chance by passive level. The analyzed ally additionally supplies 4% progress and one more Chill. Sample gives that ally 10% damage and lasts one turn; a new application replaces the existing one.

pros: Basic attack adds a second ally attack rather than only personal damage.
Special-skill vulnerability can amplify a focused team window.
Allied attacks feed both her reaction resource and next-turn progress.
The ultimate advances her next turn by 50% Action gauge.
cons: Highest-ATK targeting may select the wrong ally without tuning.
Reaction requires five Chill and an allied attack, not an on-demand button.
No native party heal, cleanse or barrier to keep the engine alive.

teams.name: Tyria basic engine
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Tyria's basic places Thorns, Emily protects/buffs the intended carry and Dress Asherah sustains while Professor M adds forced basics.
teams.playstyle: Make Tyria the highest-ATK other ally and keep attacks focused on the marked priority target.

teams.name: Special-skill stakeout
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Gwen converts allied attacks into shocks and special attacks add another stack; Hilde protects the opening and Dress Asherah heals.
teams.playstyle: Renew Gwen's Standby and aim attacks at one priority enemy; reactions occur only when their separate resource conditions are met.

alternatives.why: Gille is a specialized sidegrade for Shatter teams whose win condition is breaking a boss and amplifying that window.
alternatives.tradeoff: Professor M works without Shatter and supplies forced basics; Gille remains provisionally rated NEW and is not a proven upgrade.

alternatives.why: Charlotte is a sidegrade when the team needs immediate party ATK Up plus self-contained focused attacks rather than a highest-ATK targeting engine.
alternatives.tradeoff: Professor M keeps the special vulnerability mark and repeated forced allied basics, while Charlotte wants Sun turns for her own resources.

detective-professor.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

detective-sheriff.summary:
Gwen is a protected follow-up attacker who watches teammates build Electric Shock. While On-Site Standby is active, allied attacks add shocks and special attacks add an extra stack; reaching five lets her automatically use Light of Truth!. Her ultimate refreshes Standby and triggers that special immediately.

Choose Gwen when the other three slots can keep attacking rather than spending most turns on non-attacking support. While Standby is active, allied Special attacks feed Electric Shock faster, and five shocks turn into an automatic special. Her ultimate restores the protection window and triggers that attack immediately. She cannot redirect the whole party’s incoming damage, and area attacks still reach her, so place a real protector alongside this damage engine.
detective-sheriff.watch: Standby prevents direct attack selection only while another ally remains. It is not a barrier against area damage, and it does not disable Preemptive Guard like ordinary Stealth. Electric Shock is Gwen's resource, not an enemy stun or damage-over-time effect.
detective-sheriff.dependency_note: Use allies who attack often, especially with special skills, while keeping at least one other ally alive for Standby. A defender and healer protect against damage that targeting protection does not stop.

skill_order.name: The Culprit Is You!
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown on the skill that refreshes Standby and directly triggers her special.

skill_order.name: Light of Truth!
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves manual cadence; damage upgrades improve both manual and triggered copies.

skill_order.name: Truth Behind the Whip
skill_order.why: Basic damage is the final priority; Leap helps her out-of-Standby gauge mechanism but is not her shock resource.

rotation: Use The Culprit Is You! to establish three-turn Standby and gain shocks, then let its built-in Light of Truth! resolve automatically.
While Standby is active, use useful allied attacks and specials to feed Electric Shock. At five stacks after an allied attack, Stakeout consumes five and triggers Light of Truth! automatically.
Manual Light of Truth! remains an option when ready for focused pressure and 10% next-turn progress; do not count it as receiving the additional-trigger damage bonus.
Use Truth Behind the Whip between cooldowns for Leap. Outside Standby, other unit turns grant gauge per Leap; this is a fallback timing benefit rather than protection.

best_partners.why: Repeated attacking actions help build shocks; The Magic Bullet adds special-skill vulnerability for Gwen's manual and triggered special attacks.
Claire's manual and triggered Where Are You Looking? supply special-skill attacks while contributing focused damage, helping feed Gwen's Standby resource.
Bal Doré heals while attacking with a special skill, contributing shock generation while recovery and cleanse help preserve other allies.

detective-sheriff.build_tip: Build ATK and crit for repeated special attacks, then enough SPD to renew Standby. Add HP/DEF against area damage. She has no native offensive debuff to justify building Effect Hit merely because she carries a detective-themed resource. [A Self-Proclaimed Veteran Detective] Memory supports Strength and adds 9% Training Effectiveness after 40 Bond.
detective-sheriff.tier_reason: The stored S PvE / S+ PvP ratings fit protected focused pressure and repeated special attacks fed by teammates. PvP target-selection protection is a distinct benefit, but enemy area damage, buff removal and losing the other allies can still expose her.
detective-sheriff.investment: Prioritize ultimate and special level-6 cooldown milestones, followed by special damage. Stakeout's out-of-Standby gauge increases from 2% to 4% per Leap at higher passive levels, with ATK gains; its core shock triggers are already described at level 1. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
detective-sheriff.pve_note: Use a durable team that keeps attacking through boss phases; specials help build shocks faster. Do not assume Standby prevents area boss damage or that resource stacks stun the boss. Demoraigis: Beta reacts after five incoming attacks; count Gwen’s extra hits when planning the boss’s next response.
detective-sheriff.pvp_note: Her strongest role is sustained priority-target pressure while another ally keeps Standby functional. Team survival, enemy area coverage and the ability to renew the buff matter more than assuming she cannot be hit.

kit_explanation.name: Truth Behind the Whip
kit_explanation.explanation: Truth Behind the Whip attacks one enemy and grants Leap. Leap modestly boosts damage against Moon enemies and fuels Stakeout's gauge benefit outside Standby. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Light of Truth!
kit_explanation.explanation: Light of Truth! attacks one enemy on a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6 and grants 10% progress toward the next turn. Additionally triggered copies deal 10% more damage than the manual version. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and two Electric Shock stacks.

kit_explanation.name: The Culprit Is You!
kit_explanation.explanation: The Culprit Is You! hits one enemy on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It adds two Electric Shock stacks, grants three-turn On-Site Standby and automatically triggers Light of Truth! on the enemy. Standby prevents direct attack selection while another ally exists, but does not remove area damage. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Stakeout
kit_explanation.explanation: Stakeout grants one-turn Standby at the first battle start. During Standby, another ally's attack adds one Electric Shock and a special attack adds another. After an allied attack at five or more shocks, it consumes five and triggers Light of Truth!, favoring Gwen's recent target. Without Standby, other ally/enemy turn starts give 2–4% next-turn progress per Leap by passive level. Shocks cap at ten.

pros: Standby offers meaningful direct-target protection while allies remain.
Teammate special attacks accelerate her automatic special damage.
Ultimate refreshes protection and adds an immediate special without a second manual action.
A triggered Light of Truth! gains an additional 10% damage.
cons: Area damage still reaches her and she cannot keep Standby protection alone.
Follow-up frequency depends on other allies attacking while Standby is active.
No healing, cleanse, enemy control or teamwide protection.

teams.name: Special attacks under cover
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Professor M marks special vulnerability and adds allied attacking actions, Emily shields/buffs Gwen, and Dress Asherah heals while supplying an attacking special.
teams.playstyle: Renew Standby and focus the marked target; preserve the other allies so target protection remains active.

teams.name: Claire and Gwen pursuit
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Claire supplies focused specials, Hilde opening barriers and Dress Asherah sustained healing/cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Let Claire's Chill loop produce useful specials while Gwen accumulates shocks; maintain defenses against area attacks.

alternatives.why: Rosaria is a higher-rated PvE alternative when area damage and DEF Down matter more than focused teammate-fed follow-ups.
alternatives.tradeoff: Gwen retains Standby target protection and stronger focused follow-up identity rather than area coverage.

alternatives.why: Professor M is a sidegrade when the team benefits more from a forced carry basic and a special-skill mark.
alternatives.tradeoff: Gwen offers personal Standby protection and repeated special damage; Professor M needs careful highest-ATK targeting.

detective-sheriff.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

wild-hog.summary:
Harley is a tempo defender: she gives the team DEF Up, delays enemy turns and can speed allies up while healthy. Her special feeds Ignition to the highest-ATK Sun ally. She is better understood as a support for a Sun offense than as a defender who catches every attack for the team.

Treat Harley as a Sun tempo helper who also contributes defensive buffs. Speed improves his attack scaling and lets his pushes arrive earlier; HP and DEF keep him alive to repeat them. His ultimate changes behavior at the half-health threshold, so healing changes the next decision. He has no ordinary healing, and a Sun carry gains more from his special than a mixed team.
wild-hog.watch: She has no listed Taunt, ally Barrier or healing. The healthy and injured versions of Chicken Race give different benefits, and her advanced passive interactions are not present at passive level 1.
wild-hog.dependency_note: Use a Sun attacker if you want the special's three Ignition stacks to benefit a teammate. Bring recovery or stronger protection when incoming burst can kill allies before her tempo buffs matter.

skill_order.name: Chicken Race!
skill_order.why: Its level-6 cooldown reduction improves team DEF uptime, while level-4/8 upgrades improve the healthy team's speed-buff chance.

skill_order.name: You Wanna Go?
skill_order.why: The level-6/10 cooldown reductions improve access to enemy pushback, personal speed and the Sun ally's Ignition supply.

skill_order.name: You Bullying My Boys?
skill_order.why: Available higher passive levels add the ally-hit speed engine and stack conversion. These are meaningful upgrades, not merely more HP.

skill_order.name: Let's Go, Dave!
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a lower priority than her protection and speed-support tools.

rotation: Use Chicken Race before a dangerous enemy damage turn when party DEF Up is valuable. At half HP or above it can also speed other allies up; below half it instead gives Harley personal Berserk Mode.
Use You Wanna Go? on an enemy whose next turn you want to delay. Check which Sun ally actually has the highest ATK before expecting its three Ignition stacks to feed your preferred attacker.

Use the basic between cooldowns and let the upgraded passive build speed from allies being attacked. At maximum Ignition, her attack can spend those stacks for improved Effect Hit; that does not guarantee the opening pushback lands.
Keep her healthy when team speed is more useful than personal Berserk Mode. Do not deliberately risk losing her or a teammate just to activate the low-HP branch.

best_partners.why: Bunny Charlotte benefits from Harley's Sun turns and can use three supplied Ignition stacks if she is the highest-ATK Sun ally. Check actual stats rather than assuming she receives them.
Muriel gains Ignition when another Sun ally attacks and rewards an already-debuffed target, so Harley's attacks and tempo control fit her sustained Sun plan.
Maid Ceres heals Harley back toward the healthy Chicken Race branch and supplies cleansing absent from Harley's own kit.

wild-hog.build_tip: Build SPD, HP and DEF first for repeated support turns and survival, with enough Effect Hit for required pushback. The special and ultimate include SPD scaling, but that is a bonus to a useful support stat, not a reason to sacrifice survivability for damage.
