Journey option: Born to Be Wild is Endurance-tagged, supporting DEF for personal durability; its listed training effectiveness is +7% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
wild-hog.tier_reason: Published PvE B+ and PvP B+ fit a conditional support defender. Team DEF, speed and Sun-stack support are useful, but she lacks the direct carry protection and rescue tools offered by higher-rated defensive choices.
wild-hog.investment: Prioritize cooldown milestones and healthy-team buff chance over damage-only upgrades. Read the passive level carefully: level 1 supplies only 5% HP, while higher levels unlock the richer speed and Ignition interactions described here. The profile does not map those levels to a reliable copy threshold and lists no unique potential. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
wild-hog.pve_note: A reasonable Sun support where the team can survive with DEF Up and separate healing. Her special feeds one Sun ally, so it is less valuable if the selected ally wastes or cannot exploit Ignition; gauge-immune bosses also remove part of her utility.
wild-hog.pvp_note: Useful if her defense and turn disruption arrive before enemy burst. She cannot be treated as a substitute for damage sharing, barriers or a dependable Taunt, and dropping below half HP changes the ultimate's team-speed benefit into personal speed.

kit_explanation.name: Let's Go, Dave!
kit_explanation.explanation: Her basic hits one enemy and adds one Ignition stack. Ignition gives a small damage bonus against Star enemies and can later be spent by the upgraded passive. A Nova basic adds Toughness damage and attempts a 15% reduction to the enemy's progress toward its next turn.

kit_explanation.name: You Wanna Go?
kit_explanation.explanation: This single-target attack gives Harley two turns of SPD Up, gives three Ignition stacks to the highest-ATK Sun ally, and attempts to push the enemy's next turn back by 25%. Its damage uses both ATK and SPD. The listed five-turn cooldown can be reduced at levels 6 and 10; the ally-stack target is determined by stats, not by a manual choice.

kit_explanation.name: Chicken Race!
kit_explanation.explanation: Her area attack gives everyone two turns of DEF Up and attempts to remove 15% of each enemy's turn progress. If Harley is at least half HP, it can also grant other allies one turn of SPD Up; that chance reaches 100% through upgrades. Below half HP, she instead gains three turns of undispellable Berserk Mode for personal speed. The listed five-turn cooldown has a level-6 reduction.

kit_explanation.name: You Bullying My Boys?
kit_explanation.explanation: The passive begins as a small HP increase, so do not expect all of its advanced effects at level 1. At the highest stored level it gives 15% HP and raises Harley's speed by 3% when another ally is attacked, up to five stacks. Attacking while already at maximum Ignition spends those stacks for two turns of Effect Hit Up, helping later debuff attempts.

pros: Team DEF Up and enemy pushback can reduce pressure together.
Supplies three Ignition stacks to a qualifying Sun attacker.
SPD investment supports both her turn frequency and parts of her damage scaling.
Being hit can accumulate a personal speed increase.
cons: No Taunt, party healing or ally Barrier to directly rescue a carry.
Team SPD Up requires the healthy ultimate branch and improves with skill upgrades.
The richer passive requires higher passive levels, and the special's ally target depends on actual ATK.

teams.name: Sun offense with recovery
teams.why: Harley supplies defense and tempo, Bunny Charlotte gains Ignition from Sun ally turns, Tyria adds marked-target damage, and Maid Ceres heals and cleanses. All four are Sun, but the specific skills are the reason for the lineup.
teams.playstyle: Decide whether Charlotte or Tyria should receive Harley's three stacks and tune actual ATK accordingly. Keep Harley healthy for party speed; avoid treating overlapping ATK buffs from Charlotte and Maid Ceres as separate permanent damage bonuses.

teams.name: Sun debuff attrition
teams.why: Original Charlotte supplies targeted critical support and ATK Down, Muriel extends debuffs and gains Ignition from Sun attacks, and Maid Ceres sustains the group while Harley contributes DEF and delay.
teams.playstyle: Apply the useful debuff before Muriel's extension, use Charlotte's targeted buff on the intended damage dealer, and heal Harley before the healthy speed branch is lost. Add stronger direct protection instead if enemy burst overwhelms this defensive-buff plan.

alternatives.why: Emily is a stronger general defensive choice when a carry needs a targeted Barrier and you want incoming attacks to recycle the team-defense ultimate.
alternatives.tradeoff: She gives up Harley's Sun Ignition supply and healthy-team SPD support. A well-built Harley can remain useful when those specific tools solve the encounter.

alternatives.why: Summer Luna is a stronger specialist against critical attackers, with protective team effects, Taunt and reactive DEF Down.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her response relies on incoming allied critical hits, and she does not provide Harley's direct three-stack Sun supply or team speed branch.

wild-hog.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

construct-bomb.summary:
Petra is a straightforward Sun single-target attacker who brings DEF Down for the rest of the team. Breaking Ground accelerates her and builds Ignition; Construction Negotiations spends those stacks for extra damage while attempting a two-turn defense reduction.

Petra is easiest to justify beside a teammate who already breaks the enemy’s Toughness bar. Those breaks feed her resource and action progress, allowing more opportunities to apply DEF Down. Prioritize speed and adequate Effect Hit before chasing damage alone. The listed activation chance is not a promise that DEF Down will bypass resistance.
construct-bomb.watch: Her response to an ally breaking Toughness is absent at passive level 1. Construction Negotiations starts with a 75% DEF Down application chance and reaches its listed 100% only at skill level 8; resistance or Immunity can still prevent the debuff.
construct-bomb.dependency_note: Petra builds her own Ignition; a separate breaker becomes useful once her upgraded passive rewards allied breaks. She needs defensive support rather than three other attackers just to fill stacks.

skill_order.name: Construction Negotiations
skill_order.why: Reach level 6 for cooldown and level 8 for listed 100% DEF Down application chance before pure damage luxury upgrades.

skill_order.name: Breaking Ground
skill_order.why: The speed buff and two Ignition help her cycle; Nova adds two fixed Toughness damage for a needed break.

skill_order.name: Improvised Blueprints
skill_order.why: Lowest priority unless a long fight keeps her basic attacking often.

rotation: If the team needs DEF Down now, use Construction Negotiations before their damage even without five Ignition; its team benefit can outweigh the stack bonus.
Otherwise use Breaking Ground to gain SPD Up and two Ignition, then spend stacks with Construction Negotiations during the team's planned damage window.
With the upgraded passive, let another ally finish a break when practical to grant Petra Ignition and next-turn progress. Her own break does not satisfy that trigger.
Use Improvised Blueprints between cooldowns; reserve Nova Breaking Ground for Toughness pressure that actually changes a break window.

best_partners.why: Charlotte gives party ATK Up and uses Petra's DEF Down; Petra's Sun turns also build Charlotte's Ignition.
Tanya can finish a break to activate Petra's upgraded passive and provides team CRIT Rate Up before damage.
Serpang heals Petra with the Sun bonus, lowers enemy ATK and Effect RES, and helps sustain a slower boss plan.

construct-bomb.build_tip: Use SPD/Effect Hit for DEF Down timing, then ATK and crit for her damage. Do not spend everything on Effect Hit against an immune enemy; her stored 116 value is not an immunity bypass. Journey option: Made by Petra♡ is Focus-tagged, supporting Effect Hit for her debuff role; its listed training effectiveness is +8% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
construct-bomb.tier_reason: The stored A PvE / A PvP rating fits accessible focused damage plus DEF Down, with speed and conditional turn progress. She contributes useful setup but offers no unique guaranteed control or area damage.
construct-bomb.investment: Construction Negotiations levels 4 and 8 increase DEF Down chance, while level 6 reduces cooldown. Pre-Construction Review starts as only 5% ATK; passive level 2 introduces the allied-break reaction, scaling to 20% turn progress at level 4. No potentials are recorded. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 2 at level 40, listing +4 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
construct-bomb.pve_note: Put DEF Down before the main damage dealer against a debuffable boss. Stack-building is secondary when an early defense reduction enables the team; an unbreakable encounter removes her passive reaction value.
construct-bomb.pvp_note: Focused DEF Down can expose one target, but she has no turn denial and cannot remove protective buffs. Bring a remover when a barrier or immunity blocks the intended kill.

kit_explanation.name: Improvised Blueprints
kit_explanation.explanation: Improvised Blueprints attacks one enemy and adds one Ignition, which modestly improves damage against Star enemies. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Breaking Ground
kit_explanation.explanation: Breaking Ground hits one enemy on a three-turn cooldown and grants two-turn SPD Up plus two Ignition. Nova temporarily adds two fixed Toughness damage, distinct from an ordinary cast.

kit_explanation.name: Construction Negotiations
kit_explanation.explanation: Construction Negotiations is a single-target attack on a listed five-turn cooldown, shortened at level 6. It gains 4% damage per Ignition up to five, then consumes the stacks and attempts two-turn DEF Down. Application chance rises from 75% to 85% at level 4 and 100% at level 8; DEF Down reduces DEF by 30%. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Pre-Construction Review
kit_explanation.explanation: Pre-Construction Review is only an ATK increase at level 1. From passive level 2, another ally breaking an enemy's Toughness gives Petra one Ignition and 10% next-turn progress, once per turn; later levels raise this to 15% then 20% and improve ATK.

pros: DEF Down helps the whole team focus one enemy.
Three-turn special supplies both speed and two resource stacks.
Nova special offers a concrete extra Toughness-damage option.
Another ally’s Break can feed her Ignition and action progress.
cons: No area damage, healing, cleanse or protection.
DEF Down is not fully reliable at early skill levels or against resistance/immunity.
Ally-break acceleration requires a later passive level and another unit to secure the break.

teams.name: Sun defense-reduction support
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Petra debuffs DEF for Charlotte, Hilde supplies opening barriers, and Serpang heals Sun allies and can lower resistance.
teams.playstyle: Apply DEF Down before Charlotte's focused attack; retain Serpang's heal for incoming damage.

teams.name: Break-fed Petra
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Tanya brings crit support and can secure breaks that feed Petra; Emily and Dress Asherah keep the pair alive.
teams.playstyle: When safe, let Tanya finish a break, then use Petra's resulting turn progress to place DEF Down for the next window.

alternatives.why: Rosaria supplies area DEF Down, large area damage and 50% self next-turn progress, a higher-utility option for multi-enemy fights.
alternatives.tradeoff: Petra retains a short special cycle and Nova special with two extra fixed Toughness damage on one target.

alternatives.why: Professor M is a higher-rated attack enabler through dual attacks and a special-skill vulnerability mark.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her mark only amplifies special skills rather than Petra's more general DEF Down, and she needs allied attacks to drive her loop.

construct-bomb.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

bunny-scissors.summary:
Bunny Scarlet disrupts healing and removes one enemy buff while contributing area damage. Her turn-start pinball rolls determine whether Anyway, I Won! gets a shorter cooldown or a full reset; she is a reactive utility attacker rather than a predictable burst rotation.

Pick her for healing reduction and a timely buff removal, then let the damage rolls be a bonus. Her special removes one buff and grants an extra turn, making it the more dependable tactical tool. Speed and Effect Hit serve that job before critical damage. Check the fresh balls every turn; yesterday’s favorable roll is not a fixed rotation.
bunny-scissors.watch: Pinball Time! is random, and its temporary balls are removed after an attack. Inspect the roll before choosing your attack; three Seven Balls are not a normal guaranteed state. Recovery Down and SPD Down remain subject to enemy defenses.
bunny-scissors.dependency_note: She supplies her own random balls and Ignition. External buffs improve Ready and Willing! if that potential is available, and a healer/defender covers her lack of sustain.

skill_order.name: Anyway, I Won!
skill_order.why: Area Recovery Down is her broadest utility; damage upgrades help, but none remove the Seven Ball randomness.

skill_order.name: This Doesn't Count!
skill_order.why: Improve the targeted strip/anti-heal attack used to expose a key enemy; it also grants an extra turn.

skill_order.name: Here I Come!
skill_order.why: Basic upgrades come last because the utility attacks matter more than its Ignition-building hit.

rotation: At the start of each turn, check Normal Ball and Seven Ball before attacking. If three Seven Balls are present and the ultimate is ready, Anyway, I Won! can use that reset condition.
Use This Doesn't Count! to remove one important enemy buff and attempt Recovery Down, then take the extra turn according to the new state rather than assuming the previous balls persist.
Use Anyway, I Won! when partywide healing reduction or a possible one-turn SPD Down matters. Do not delay a necessary anti-heal solely to fish for three Seven Balls.
Use Here I Come! between cooldowns. Maintain useful external buffs for Ready and Willing! if owned, but do not sacrifice healing merely to maximize its five-buff condition.

best_partners.why: Song of the Toast supplies party ATK Up, one useful buff for Ready and Willing!; Scarlet's Sun turns also feed Charlotte's Ignition.
Cleaning Service provides both a targeted barrier and ATK Up; Turn-Down Service adds party DEF Up, helping Scarlet survive and furnishing distinct buffs.
Serpang heals with a Sun bonus and can lower one enemy's Effect RES, supporting Scarlet's debuff attempts without promising a bypass.

bunny-scissors.build_tip: Favor SPD and Effect Hit for timely utility, then ATK and crit for damage. Stored 112 Effect Hit and 20 CRIT Rate are maxima; do not treat them as free starting values or a guarantee to land debuffs. Journey option: The Great and Amazing Bunny Girl is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
bunny-scissors.tier_reason: The stored B+ PvE / B+ PvP rating fits useful anti-heal/strip utility with random cooldown acceleration. Healing enemies raise her value; fights without recovery or removable buffs leave mostly damage and unreliable slow utility.
bunny-scissors.investment: Prioritize the utility attack used in the encounter before maximizing every damage node. High Score! adds CRIT Rate and a higher accumulated SPD cap at later passive levels. Ready and Willing! is a listed unique potential that rewards having buffs with Effect Hit and damage; its wording does not clearly separate the fixed versus per-buff portions, so do not plan an exact bonus without checking the active effect. The buff-count benefit caps at five. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 10 at level 200, listing +12 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
bunny-scissors.pve_note: Use against healing elites or wave groups that can receive Recovery Down. Against a non-healing, debuff-immune boss her distinctive utility fades; the occasional ultimate reset is a bonus rather than a damage plan.
bunny-scissors.pvp_note: Target a removable defensive buff with This Doesn't Count! and follow with team pressure before healing recovers the target. One buff removed is not a complete strip, and anti-heal does not prevent cleansing or resurrection.

kit_explanation.name: Here I Come!
kit_explanation.explanation: Here I Come! attacks one enemy and adds one Ignition. Ignition also gives Scarlet extra damage through High Score!, up to five stacks; Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: This Doesn't Count!
kit_explanation.explanation: This Doesn't Count! is a single-target four-turn-cooldown attack that attempts two-turn Recovery Down, removes one buff, adds Ignition and grants Scarlet an extra turn. Recovery Down halves incoming healing if it lands. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Anyway, I Won!
kit_explanation.explanation: Anyway, I Won! attacks all enemies on a listed five-turn cooldown, attempts one-turn SPD Down at 75% and two-turn Recovery Down at 100%, and adds Ignition. Each Seven Ball reduces its cooldown by one; three Seven Balls specify a reset. Nova adds damage and fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: High Score!
kit_explanation.explanation: High Score! automatically rolls Pinball Time! three times at turn start: Normal Ball adds 1% damage and Seven Ball adds 7%. Attacking removes these rolled effects. Ignition adds 7% damage per stack, and turn-start Seven Balls accumulate flat SPD, with the cap rising from six to ten through passive levels. Later levels also grant CRIT Rate.

pros: Targeted buff removal comes with an extra turn.
Area anti-heal can pressure multiple recovery-dependent enemies.
A favorable pinball roll can accelerate her area attack substantially.
Ignition adds a separate damage bonus without requiring Seven Balls.
cons: Random ball results prevent a dependable ultimate-reset schedule.
Only one buff is removed by the targeted attack.
No native healing or protection, and debuff immunity sharply reduces utility.

teams.name: Sun anti-heal pressure
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Charlotte buffs ATK, Hilde provides opening ally barriers, and Serpang heals Sun allies and lowers enemy resistance. Scarlet contributes healing reduction that these allies do not supply.
teams.playstyle: Pick Scarlet's attack from the current balls and enemy buffs; keep Serpang ready for retaliation.

teams.name: Buff-supported utility
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Emily supplies barrier/ATK/DEF buffs, Dress Asherah heals and cleanses, and Gwen converts allied attacks into Electric Shock while protected by Standby.
teams.playstyle: Strip or anti-heal a priority target before Gwen's damage; extra turns do not guarantee Gwen follow-ups without enough shocks.

alternatives.why: Bell offers removal of all buffs plus Silence on one target, a higher-utility option against heavily buffed PvP threats.
alternatives.tradeoff: Scarlet retains area anti-heal and her extra-turn strip; Bell does not replace those effects.

alternatives.why: Rosaria provides a large area hit, area DEF Down and 50% self turn progress for more direct wave pressure.
alternatives.tradeoff: Scarlet is still the relevant choice when recovery reduction, rather than raw area pressure, is required.

bunny-scissors.research_note: Community build coverage checked. Detailed paid recommendations were unavailable; the build and rotation here follow the local kit.

bunny-spear.summary:
Bunny Claire is a focused Moon attacker whose crits generate resources and faster turns. Bunny Jackpot starts a three-turn crit buff, Where Are You Looking? adds three Chill on a crit, and a basic used at full Chill can trigger that special automatically.

Use Claire (Flawless Blue Rose) against one durable opponent. Her special returns 30% Action gauge and supplies three Chill only on a critical hit, so opening crit consistency matters before her passive has fully ramped. At five Chill, a basic triggers that special automatically. The ultimate gains damage from enemy buffs, up to five, but leaving a lethal buff active just to increase its multiplier is a poor trade. Bring protection and remove dangerous buffs when necessary.
bunny-spear.watch: Jackpot Bloom and passive crit growth overlap external CRIT Rate buffs. Plan around the ramp instead of assuming full crit chance on the opening hit. Enemy buffs strengthen Bunny Jackpot but can also be dangerous enough to require removal.
bunny-spear.dependency_note: She supplies ATK Up, critical buffs and her own Chill loop. External early crit support makes the special's three-Chill condition more reliable; survival support remains necessary.

skill_order.name: Bunny Jackpot
skill_order.why: Establishes Jackpot Bloom and is the principal focused attack; upgrades are damage increases, not hidden cooldown unlocks.

skill_order.name: Where Are You Looking?
skill_order.why: Improves the special used manually and through the basic-triggered loop; its 30% next-turn progress is already present.

skill_order.name: Faster Than Sight
skill_order.why: Basic damage matters once full Chill lets it trigger the special; improve after the two cooldown attacks.

rotation: Use Bunny Jackpot early when its crit buff is needed, especially against a safely manageable buffed enemy; the extra 20% on this attack is separate from the buff granted afterward.
Use Where Are You Looking? with adequate CRIT Rate to gain three Chill and 30% progress toward the next turn. Its ATK Up is applied after the attack.
At or near five Chill, use Faster Than Sight and let Conviction Toward Victory trigger Where Are You Looking? after the basic if the full-stack condition is met.
Do not spend several turns waiting for an ideal buff count if you can kill a priority enemy now. Nova Bunny Jackpot adds 20% turn progress as well as fixed Toughness damage.

best_partners.why: All In gives early CRIT Rate Up for Claire's special; Claire's Moon attacks feed Frey's Cash In resource and next-turn progress.
The Magic Bullet adds special-skill vulnerability, useful for Where Are You Looking?; a highest-ATK Claire can also be called into basics.
Emily protects Claire with Cleaning Service and provides ATK Up, allowing Claire to prioritize crit consistency over trying to tank.

bunny-spear.build_tip: Balance early CRIT Rate with her later passive stacks and Jackpot Bloom; then add ATK, CRIT DMG and SPD. Stored 104 SPD gives a better starting timing profile than 90-SPD attackers but does not establish turn order after gear. The Perfect Bunny Girl supports Vitality and Support Quest income. For her ATK damage, include Strength training rather than treating that matching card as a complete build.
bunny-spear.tier_reason: The stored S PvE / A+ PvP rating fits sustained single-target damage with a crit/Chill loop. Bosses and buffed durable enemies suit her; she lacks the area control or universal team protection that would make every PvP matchup favorable.
bunny-spear.investment: Prioritize Bunny Jackpot and Where Are You Looking? damage, plus the passive upgrades raising turn-start CRIT Rate from 6% to 10% per stack, capped at three. Claire's Unique Potential gives opening Immunity; its effect row says one turn while the prose leaves duration unspecified. Treat it as conditional access, not permanent protection. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
bunny-spear.pve_note: Build a repeatable crit loop against a durable target. Bunny Jackpot gains up to five enemy-buff bonuses, but a buff-free boss is still attackable; that bonus is not a requirement to use the skill.
bunny-spear.pvp_note: Buff-heavy enemies offer extra damage but may retaliate strongly. Opening Immunity, if available, can be dispelled and does not make her safe for an entire fight. Bring cleanse or protection where needed.

kit_explanation.name: Faster Than Sight
kit_explanation.explanation: Faster Than Sight is a single-target basic adding Chill. At five Chill after this basic, the passive consumes the stacks and triggers Where Are You Looking? automatically. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Where Are You Looking?
kit_explanation.explanation: Where Are You Looking? hits one target on a three-turn cooldown. It grants two-turn ATK Up and 30% next-turn progress; a critical hit grants three Chill. It can be selected normally or triggered by the passive. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Bunny Jackpot
kit_explanation.explanation: Bunny Jackpot is a single-target four-turn-cooldown attack with +20% CRIT Rate for the hit. Afterward it grants three-turn Jackpot Bloom, adding 20% CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG. The hit gains 10% damage per enemy buff, up to five buffs. Nova also advances her next turn by 20%.

kit_explanation.name: Conviction Toward Victory
kit_explanation.explanation: Conviction Toward Victory automatically adds CRIT Rate at own-turn start, stacking three times: 6% per stack at passive level 1, 10% at level 4. Later levels add ATK. It also converts full Chill after Faster Than Sight into the automatic special; that is not an extra manually selected cast.

pros: Can maintain focused pressure with crit-driven Chill and a triggered special.
Own critical buffs reduce long-fight dependence on a permanent external crit supporter.
Bunny Jackpot specifically rewards attacking buffed enemies.
The ultimate gains up to five separate enemy-buff damage bonuses.
cons: No area attack for broad wave clear.
Failure to crit the special slows resource generation.
Full passive crit, Jackpot Bloom and external crit buffs can overlap wastefully.

teams.name: Moon focused damage
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Bunny Frey helps early crits and receives resources from Claire's attacks; Emily shields and buffs Claire, and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use early crit support to establish the loop, then avoid treating every basic as a guaranteed special until Chill is full.

teams.name: Special-mark pursuit
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Professor M marks special-skill vulnerability and can force Claire basics if her ATK is highest; Hilde barriers and Dress Asherah recovery protect the engine.
teams.playstyle: Aim Claire and Professor M at the same target; the mark must land for its damage benefit.

alternatives.why: Lyn is a higher-rated PvE alternative when one slot must handle both waves and a focused critical form.
alternatives.tradeoff: Claire keeps simpler single-target setup and a specific damage bonus against buffed enemies; Lyn needs stance-aware sequencing.

alternatives.why: Tyria offers higher-rated PvP pressure into marked Defenders with conditional DEF penetration.
alternatives.tradeoff: Claire retains her own crit ramp and turn-progress loop without depending on enemy Thorns marks.

bunny-spear.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

summer-oracle.summary:
Summer Luna protects allies from critical damage at the start of battle and reacts when another ally takes a critical hit. She combines HP-based attacks, personal Barriers, team DEF Up and single-target ATK Down/Taunt, with stronger reaction damage at full Ignition.

Use Luna (White Pearl Trap) to soften the opening against critical attackers. Waterproof Sunscreen gives other allies 50% CRIT DMG RES for three turns, while maximum HP improves her own damage and Barriers. Her automatic special waits for another ally to suffer a critical hit; it is not a manually scheduled rescue. The ultimate gives everyone DEF Up and attempts targeted disruption, but Taunt immunity and buff removal can limit her protection. Keep a healer for lasting recovery.
summer-oracle.watch: Summer Temptation is automatic and needs a critical hit on another ally. Waterproof Sunscreen increases critical-damage resistance; it neither stops critical hits nor grants immunity, and it excludes Luna herself.
summer-oracle.dependency_note: Her reactive value depends on enemy critical hits against teammates. Add real healing and carry damage; her own shields do not recover the whole party.

skill_order.name: Welcome to Paradise!
skill_order.why: Level 6 shortens Welcome to Paradise!’s cooldown, supporting team DEF Up and targeted disruption.

skill_order.name: Summer Temptation
skill_order.why: Levels 4/8 improve full-Ignition Taunt chance; improve damage for reaction pressure.

skill_order.name: Midsummer Essential
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels add HP and improve Ignition generation from allies being critically hit.

skill_order.name: Bubble Swing!
skill_order.why: Basic Nova adds a personal Barrier and extra Ignition; ordinary basic damage is secondary.

rotation: Use Welcome to Paradise! before a dangerous attacker acts when ATK Down/Taunt can help, while giving the team two-turn DEF Up.
Use Bubble Swing! between ultimates. Spend its Nova Burst when the personal Barrier and extra Ignition justify the resource, rather than treating those effects as baseline.
Let Summer Temptation trigger after another ally is critically hit. It provides personal Barrier and DEF Down; at five Ignition it gains extra damage and a Taunt attempt, then consumes stacks.
Do not hold critical healing or weaken ally defenses to force the reaction; survival is more valuable than manufacturing a proc.

best_partners.why: Luna’s Sun attacks feed upgraded Triumphant, while Muriel can extend Luna’s DEF Down or ATK Down.
Party healing and two-debuff cleanse cover sustain and cleansing missing from Luna’s kit.
Harley supplies additional turn pressure and team speed; avoid overvaluing duplicate DEF Up.

summer-oracle.build_tip: HP is the first damage-and-survival stat because her attacks and Barriers scale with it. Add SPD, DEF and sufficient Effect Hit for the debuffs you rely on; critical offense is secondary to doing the protection job. A Midsummer Night’s Sky is a Vitality fit for this HP-scaling variant; it adds 8% Training Effectiveness after 30 Bond. Follow the Light! instead trains Strength.
summer-oracle.tier_reason: The higher PvP rating fits anti-critical support and retaliation against aggressive carries. PvE value is more encounter-specific because ally-critical triggers and Taunt may be absent or blocked; this does not imply every boss is controllable.
summer-oracle.investment: Prioritize the ultimate’s level-6 cooldown, then reaction Taunt chance/damage and passive HP/stack consistency. The opening five Ignition exist at passive level 1; higher passive levels improve later replenishment. No unique potential is listed. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here.
summer-oracle.pve_note: Use team DEF Up against damaging phases and check whether the boss can be Taunted or debuffed. Low-critical enemies give fewer Summer Temptation triggers. Demoraigis: Alpha can remove a party buff through Collapse Wave, so do not assume every opening protection lasts its full duration.
summer-oracle.pvp_note: Fits into teams facing critical attackers; initial Sunscreen softens their damage while ally-critical triggers can punish them. It does not cover every damage type or protect Luna with Sunscreen herself.

kit_explanation.name: Bubble Swing!
kit_explanation.explanation: Bubble Swing! attacks one target, adds one Ignition and scales partly with Luna’s maximum HP. Its Nova Burst adds a one-turn personal Barrier and another Ignition, plus Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Summer Temptation
kit_explanation.explanation: Summer Temptation is a reaction with a listed one-turn cooldown: when another ally is critically hit, Luna attacks that attacker, gains a two-turn HP-based Barrier and attempts DEF Down. At full Ignition it adds damage and a Taunt attempt with 75% to 100% skill-level chance, then consumes Ignition.

kit_explanation.name: Welcome to Paradise!
kit_explanation.explanation: Welcome to Paradise! attacks one enemy, gives all allies two-turn DEF Up, adds three Ignition and attempts two-turn ATK Down plus one-turn Taunt. The listed five-turn cooldown has a level-6 reduction, and damage scales partly with maximum HP.

kit_explanation.name: Midsummer Essential
kit_explanation.explanation: Midsummer Essential grants five opening Ignition and three-turn Waterproof Sunscreen to other allies; Sunscreen adds 50% CRIT DMG RES. Incoming critical hits replenish Ignition, with ally-hit generation improving from 60% to 100% by passive level. Higher levels also add maximum HP.

pros: Opening anti-critical support helps allies before Luna’s first action.
Maximum HP contributes to both offense and personal Barriers.
Ultimate provides team DEF Up while weakening and redirecting one attacker.
She starts the first battle with five Ignition for an early empowered reaction.
cons: Reaction requires another ally to suffer a critical hit.
Sunscreen excludes Luna and is a timed opening buff.
No direct party recovery or cleanse.

teams.name: Sun debuff retaliation
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Muriel extends landed debuffs, Harley advances tempo and dress Asherah supplies party sustain/cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Apply Luna’s protection before pressure, then extend the useful landed debuff rather than assuming a guaranteed Taunt lock.

teams.name: Protected area pressure
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Amora supplies immediate damage, Voyager Luna supplies area vulnerability and Frey restores/cleanses allies.
teams.playstyle: Let Summer Luna reduce incoming damage while the two area attackers capitalize on Bind if it lands.

alternatives.why: Carmen has a higher published PvE rating and provides more direct highest-ATK carry protection, recovery and targeted cleanse.
alternatives.tradeoff: Summer Luna retains anti-critical opening support, Taunt and enemy DEF/ATK debuffs.

alternatives.why: Emily is a higher-PvE-rated defender that can buff a carry’s ATK, shield it and contribute area damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: Emily does not reproduce Sunscreen or Summer Luna’s Taunt and critical-hit retaliation.

summer-oracle.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

summer-smile.summary:
Summer Smile marks one enemy with Aqua Bomb and follows allies’ attacks on that survivor with Heat Control when she has enough Leap. Those reactions build Sparkler, which her ultimate spends on additional Heat Control instances.

Use Smile (Sunshine Cat) in a party that can focus the marked enemy without instantly killing it. Heat Control needs that target to survive an ally’s hit and costs two Leap, so every ally attack is not a free reaction. Her opening Aqua Bomb chooses the fastest enemy and explicitly bypasses several defenses only for that opening application. ATK and critical stats improve the attacks; Leap supply and target coordination decide whether those attacks happen often enough to justify her slot.
summer-smile.watch: Heat Control is not selectable, needs at least two Leap for its ally-attack trigger and does not fire if the ally kills the marked target. The opening mark’s explicit resistance/immunity/accuracy bypass is limited to the start-of-battle effect.
summer-smile.dependency_note: Other allies must attack the marked target while it survives. Her unique potential helps Leap supply but is an acquired effect, not part of the ordinary passive.

skill_order.name: Heat Control
skill_order.why: Heat Control is the repeated-damage engine, especially with Laughter Protocol.

skill_order.name: Summer Night Fireworks
skill_order.why: Level 6 shortens the ultimate cooldown; Sparkler makes its follow-up package more valuable.

skill_order.name: Underwater Experiment
skill_order.why: Passive levels improve ATK and critical damage against the marked target.

skill_order.name: Hydration
skill_order.why: Basic damage comes later, but its Nova is a useful Leap refill.

rotation: Identify the opening Aqua Bomb on the fastest enemy. Use Hydration to move the mark to a priority target if attacking the fastest one is unsafe or wasteful.
Build at least two Leap before allies attack the marked survivor. Hydration Nova adds two extra Leap and 10% turn progress; Laughter Protocol adds one Leap each turn if acquired.
Let allies attack Aqua Bomb to trigger Heat Control automatically, consuming Leap and building Sparkler. Do not order a manual Heat Control cast.

Use Summer Night Fireworks with Sparkler for its additional follow-up package, or sooner for necessary damage/three Leap. The text says it triggers Heat Control but also restricts Heat Control to its trigger conditions; do not assume every extra instance bypasses those conditions.

best_partners.why: Frequent single-target attacks and eligible reactions can pressure the Aqua Bomb target while Smile has Leap.
Dispel and turn disruption can expose the marked enemy for Smile and allies to focus.
Star-enhanced healing and cleanse help Smile remain active; support non-attacks do not trigger Heat Control.

summer-smile.build_tip: ATK and critical stats with enough SPD to maintain stacks/mark timing. Add Effect Hit if relying on later mark applications; only the opening application explicitly bypasses resistance, immunity and accuracy. Vacation Prep: Time to Shop! supports Strength and improves Sensory Training chance after 50 Bond; the other Smile cards train Focus.
summer-smile.tier_reason: The better PvE than PvP rating fits sustained marked-target coordination, especially against a durable priority enemy. PvP target access, cleanse, Leap starvation or early kills can interrupt the engine; opening mark bypass is not a guarantee of follow-up success.
summer-smile.investment: Invest Heat Control and the ultimate’s level-6 cooldown before basic damage if using the follow-up engine. Laughter Protocol adds 20% special-skill damage and a turn-start Leap; obtain it only if this is a planned role, rather than treating it as free innate power. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here.
summer-smile.pve_note: Sustained single-target encounters give allies repeated chances to trigger follow-ups. Very weak waves may die before Heat Control fires, reducing the value of the marked-target plan. Demoraigis: Beta triggers Fractured Radiance after five incoming attacks, so additional reactions also advance that enemy mechanic.
summer-smile.pvp_note: The opening mark targets highest SPD rather than your chosen enemy. Decide whether to focus that target or move Aqua Bomb; an immunity bypass on opening mark does not bypass every later defense.

kit_explanation.name: Hydration
kit_explanation.explanation: Hydration attacks one enemy and adds one Leap. With Nova Burst it adds two more Leap and 10% progress toward Smile’s next turn, in addition to Toughness damage. Her passive then attempts to place Aqua Bomb on that target.

kit_explanation.name: Heat Control
kit_explanation.explanation: Heat Control reacts when another ally attacks a surviving Aqua Bomb enemy while Smile has at least two Leap. It spends two Leap, adds one Sparkler up to three and grants 15% turn progress. The effect record lists Leap generically, but the description explicitly says the reaction consumes two.

kit_explanation.name: Summer Night Fireworks
kit_explanation.explanation: Summer Night Fireworks attacks one enemy on a listed five-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6, and adds three Leap. It consumes Sparkler to request extra Heat Control instances prioritizing marked enemies. Because Heat Control also states trigger restrictions, the exact extra-instance interaction should be checked in play rather than promised as an unconditional chain.

kit_explanation.name: Underwater Experiment
kit_explanation.explanation: Underwater Experiment marks the highest-SPD enemy for three turns at battle start, explicitly ignoring Effect RES, Immunity and ACC for that opening effect. Hydration and the ultimate attempt to relocate the single active mark afterward; those applications do not state the same bypass. Attacks against the mark gain CRIT DMG by passive level.

pros: Ally focus fire can create damage between Smile’s own turns.
Opening mark explicitly bypasses several defenses for that application.
Unique potential improves both special damage and Leap supply.
Heat Control grants 15% Action gauge when its conditions are met.
cons: Trigger fails if the ally kills the marked enemy.
Leap is consumed quickly and the normal basic only supplies one.
Ultimate-follow-up wording and reaction restrictions need live verification.

teams.name: Star focus engine
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Roberta and Voyager Smile attack priority targets while Frey provides Star-friendly sustain and cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Keep attacks on the surviving mark, watch Leap before ally actions and spend Sparkler when the fight warrants it.

teams.name: Protected mark carry
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Carmen protects Smile if she is highest ATK, Ceres strips protection and dress Asherah sustains/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Set the intended oath recipient, expose the marked enemy and avoid treating non-attack healing turns as reaction triggers.

alternatives.why: Roberta is higher-rated in both modes and offers simpler single-target pressure with personal cleanse against area attackers.
alternatives.tradeoff: Smile can instead add follow-ups to ally attacks without requiring the enemy to hit Roberta with an area skill.

alternatives.why: Amora offers higher-rated immediate area pressure and an explicit extra turn with less marked-target setup.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not bring Smile’s Aqua Bomb-driven off-turn damage pattern.

summer-smile.research_note: Public character build reviewed; gear details were image-only or gated, so no unseen set or slot recommendation is claimed.

independent-dragon.summary:
Lacy combines fast single-target attacks with a team-wide Entangled Dream debuff. That mark weakens enemy ATK and makes attacks into Lacy feed her healing and next-turn progress. She has substantial personal tools, but the response loop only works when marked enemies actually attack her.

Build around a priority enemy while keeping Entangled Dream on opponents that are likely to attack Lacy. Her ultimate damages one enemy even though its mark reaches the whole opposing party. Marked incoming hits restore her HP from ATK and advance her next turn; a tank that draws every hit away can reduce that loop. She brings speed and self-sustain, but no party heal and no rescue for a defeated ally.
independent-dragon.watch: Entangled Dream is listed as a 10% ATK reduction, not sleep or a lost turn. Song of Water and Fire damages one target even though it attempts the debuff on everyone. Her self-heal is conditional and is not party healing.
independent-dragon.dependency_note: Her ATK buff, SPD buff and conditional self-heal are self-contained. A healer still covers burst, and a taunting ally can reduce the number of marked attacks she personally receives.

skill_order.name: Song of Water and Fire
skill_order.why: Get level 6 for cooldown and levels 4/8 for more reliable mark application before marginal damage upgrades.

skill_order.name: Upstream Water Prison
skill_order.why: Improve her repeatable marked-target attack and SPD buff's damage.

skill_order.name: Wish-Bearing Script
skill_order.why: Raise ATK and the turn-progress response as passive levels become available.

skill_order.name: Ascending Fire Dragon
skill_order.why: Basic damage is the last priority unless cooldown downtime dominates.

rotation: Usually establish Entangled Dream with Song of Water and Fire when the enemy can receive it; choose the single damage target deliberately.
Use Upstream Water Prison against a marked priority target for its bonus and SPD Up. If an urgent finish is available, do not wait just to apply a mark first.
Use Ascending Fire Dragon in gaps and let Wish-Bearing Script react automatically. Keep a healer ready when Lacy is attacked before marking or receives too much burst.

best_partners.why: Frey adds Barriers and a full one-target cleanse, covering damage that Lacy's conditional self-heal cannot handle.
Ceres heals and cleanses while leaving Lacy free to take marked attacks; overlapping ATK Up is not an extra stack to assume.
Dana can give ATK Up to the highest-ATK other ally, supporting Lacy's damage and ATK-based self-heal if she receives it.
Bell strips buffs and Silences a dangerous enemy while Lacy focuses a marked target.

independent-dragon.build_tip: Her listed maximum SPD is 115 and Toughness is 5, useful starting traits rather than proof she outspeeds a built opponent. Prioritize ATK and critical damage consistency, then SPD, survival and enough Effect Hit for a mark-dependent plan. No Pain, No Gain is a Strength fit for both attacks and ATK-based recovery. Its unique improves Old Coin gain, not direct damage.
independent-dragon.tier_reason: The higher PvE placement fits sustained single-target damage, self-buffs and marked-hit recovery. In PvP, resistance, control and lethal burst can deny the mark-response loop before it pays off. Her broad mark is an ATK reduction, not a team-wide turn skip.
independent-dragon.investment: Song of Water and Fire's cooldown and mark-chance upgrades are the practical first milestones, then Upstream Water Prison and passive ATK. Her potentials arrays are empty; do not budget around an unlisted unique effect. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
independent-dragon.pve_note: Good for a marked priority enemy and sustained incoming attacks. Against mark immunity, retain her direct damage and self-buffs but discount both the special's conditional damage and the marked-hit recovery loop.
independent-dragon.pvp_note: She can apply team-wide ATK pressure while focusing one target. A listed 100% mark chance is still subject to applicable resistance/immunity, and her self-heal only helps if she survives the attack.

kit_explanation.name: Ascending Fire Dragon
kit_explanation.explanation: Ascending Fire Dragon is a single-target basic that adds one Agitation. Agitation's ordinary attribute bonus is against Order enemies, not all enemies. Nova adds one Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Upstream Water Prison
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 3 turns. Upstream Water Prison hits one target, adds Agitation and gives two turns of SPD Up. It deals 20% more damage when that target has Entangled Dream. Nova adds Toughness damage and a further listed damage bonus.

kit_explanation.name: Song of Water and Fire
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Song of Water and Fire hits a single enemy, adds three Agitation and gives Lacy ATK Up for three turns. It then attempts three turns of Entangled Dream on all enemies. The application chance rises from 75% to 85% at level 4 and 100% at level 8; the mark lowers ATK by 10%.

kit_explanation.name: Wish-Bearing Script
kit_explanation.explanation: Wish-Bearing Script starts the first battle with two Agitation. When an enemy with Entangled Dream attacks Lacy, she gains Agitation, heals based on ATK and advances her next turn, from 6% to 10% across levels. After an unmarked enemy attacks her while Agitation is full, she consumes all stacks to attempt a two-turn mark on that attacker. Higher levels add ATK. These are reactions to being attacked, not manual actions.

pros: High listed maximum SPD and five Toughness support an active personal kit.
Ultimate applies a broad ATK-reducing mark while damaging a chosen enemy.
Marked attacks into Lacy feed healing, resource and next-turn progress together.
Her special supplies two turns of SPD Up without external support.
cons: No party heal or direct ally protection.
Mark immunity removes multiple connected benefits.
An ally's Taunt can divert attacks away from her self-recovery engine.

teams.name: Marked duelist (theorycraft)
teams.why: Frey supplies emergency defense, Bell removes buffs, and Dana supports another attacker while Lacy handles one marked enemy.
teams.playstyle: Apply marks, then use Lacy's special on the priority target; use Frey's direct cleanse when control stops her from acting.

teams.name: Recovery and disruption (theorycraft)
teams.why: Ceres covers healing, Bell removes buffs and supplies Silence, and Kyra can exploit that Silence while Lacy pressures a marked target.
teams.playstyle: Focus one enemy while keeping Ceres's recovery ready. Treat ATK Up overlap as coverage, not multiplied bonuses.

alternatives.why: Fei is a useful duelist alternative when evasion and reactive attacks fit the enemy better.
alternatives.tradeoff: Fei depends on evasion rather than Entangled Dream and lacks Lacy's listed team-wide ATK reduction and self-heal.

alternatives.why: Carnelia has a higher published PvP rating and supplies area damage, Buff Block and enemy turn delay when those tools matter more than a duelist.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her PvE rating is lower, and her once-per-battle lethal-damage response does not replace Lacy's repeatable marked-hit healing. Changing roles requires an available separate character and build.

independent-dragon.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

construct-gadget.summary:
Tanya is a Star focused attacker who can turn her own breaks into ally turn progress. Buzz-Buzz Chainsaw offers brief team crit support; after enough Leap, her upgraded passive enters Demolition Mode and Bang-Bang Bunker gains additional Toughness damage.

Her job is to help create the damage window by breaking Toughness, then keep attacking inside Demolition. Coordinate her single-target burst with the remaining enemy bar instead of spending it into an unfavorable matchup. Speed, ATK and critical stats support that plan. Her small party progress boost follows her own Break, so it is a reward rather than an unconditional opener.
construct-gadget.watch: Demolition Mode and the team turn-progress reward do not appear in passive level 1. Tanya must personally break the target for that reward; another ally breaking it is not enough. Her team CRIT Rate buff lasts only one turn.
construct-gadget.dependency_note: She can attack alone, but her reason to occupy a team slot is break timing plus brief crit support. Let teammates lower Toughness without stealing a planned Tanya break when the upgraded passive is available.

skill_order.name: Buzz-Buzz Chainsaw
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown; levels 4 and 8 raise self next-turn progress from 15% to 20% to 30%.

skill_order.name: Bang-Bang Bunker
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown and level 10 extends ATK Up to two turns; invest if she is the break finisher.

skill_order.name: Boom-Boom Tool
skill_order.why: Basic damage is secondary, but it supplies Leap when no break is available.

rotation: Use Buzz-Buzz Chainsaw before allied attacks that need its one-turn CRIT Rate Up, while considering whether the hit will accidentally finish a break.
Use Bang-Bang Bunker to finish Toughness when its two base break points and conditional extra point matter. With the upgraded passive, her own break gives three Leap and advances other allies.
At five Leap, the next own-turn start consumes them for three-turn Demolition Mode. Check the state before counting the extra Toughness damage.
Use Boom-Boom Tool for Leap between cooldowns. If Fried Food Party is available, keep Tanya at 50% HP or above so using skills also gives 20% turn progress.

best_partners.why: Tanya's own break triggers Petra's upgraded ally-break passive, while Petra applies DEF Down for Tanya's attacks.
Lyn's Clear Wind branch distributes three Leap to Star allies, helping Tanya reach Demolition Mode, and can buff Star allies' crit damage.
Team healing helps maintain Fried Food Party's HP condition, and Lumière Sonnet cleanses and advances Tanya's next turn.

construct-gadget.build_tip: Use enough SPD to place the brief crit buff before allies, then ATK and crit. HP/DEF and healing help preserve Fried Food Party, but the potential should not be treated as an always-on free extra turn. Journey option: The Indomitable Masterpiece is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
construct-gadget.tier_reason: The stored A PvE / B+ PvP rating fits a useful break/crit hybrid whose payoff depends on securing breaks and planning one-turn buffs. Breakable bosses favor her more than short PvP rounds with disrupted turn order.
construct-gadget.investment: Buy Chainsaw's cooldown/turn-progress milestones and Bunker's level-6 cooldown before maximizing basics. Demolition Work level 2 introduces the actual break engine; level 1 is ATK only. Fried Food Party is a listed unique potential granting 20% turn progress after skills at HP 50% or above; no unlock requirement is supplied. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. Resonance progression adds stats separately from skill levels; do not read the maximum stat endpoint as first-copy performance.
construct-gadget.pve_note: Aim to secure the break herself when the team needs her 6–10% allied next-turn boost. Against targets that cannot break, evaluate her as a brief crit supporter and single-target attacker, not a complete turn engine.
construct-gadget.pvp_note: Short CRIT Rate Up needs speed tuning. Do not sacrifice a kill or survival just to grant a small allied gauge boost, and do not count on a non-attacking cleanse from Tanya.

kit_explanation.name: Boom-Boom Tool
kit_explanation.explanation: Boom-Boom Tool attacks one enemy and grants one Leap. Leap slightly boosts damage against Moon enemies and fuels the passive conversion. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Buzz-Buzz Chainsaw
kit_explanation.explanation: Buzz-Buzz Chainsaw attacks one enemy on a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. All allies gain one-turn CRIT Rate Up, while Tanya gains 15% next-turn progress at level 1, 20% at level 4 and 30% at level 8. Nova adds damage and fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Bang-Bang Bunker
kit_explanation.explanation: Bang-Bang Bunker is a single-target five-turn-cooldown attack reduced at level 6. It grants ATK Up afterward for one turn, extended to two at level 10, and deals one extra Toughness damage if Demolition Mode is already active on attack. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Demolition Work
kit_explanation.explanation: Demolition Work begins as only an ATK increase. From passive level 2, Tanya personally breaking Toughness grants three Leap and 6–10% next-turn progress to other allies, depending on passive level. At five Leap at own-turn start, she consumes them for three-turn Demolition Mode, adding 10% damage.

pros: Can combine a break finisher with allied next-turn progress.
Team crit support arrives on an attacking skill.
Fried Food Party adds a clear HP-conditioned cycling option if obtained.
Her own Break advances the other allies’ action gauges.
cons: Main break engine is absent at passive level 1.
One-turn team crit buff is sensitive to turn order.
No sustain and a personal-break requirement can conflict with another breaker.

teams.name: Leap and break support
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Lyn can distribute Leap to Tanya in the Clear Wind branch; Emily protects Tanya and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use Lyn's team branch when distributed Leap matters; leave an appropriate Toughness remainder for Tanya.

teams.name: Reciprocal break setup
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Petra places DEF Down and benefits when Tanya breaks; Emily shields Tanya while Serpang heals and lowers resistance.
teams.playstyle: Time Chainsaw before Petra's attack; maintain HP for Fried Food Party if available.

alternatives.why: Lyn is a higher-rated PvE damage/Star-support option, with area or focused forms and Star-team Leap distribution.
alternatives.tradeoff: Tanya keeps the distinct personal-break reward that advances other allies and her HP-conditioned potential.

alternatives.why: Professor M offers higher-rated repeated attack support through forced dual attacks and a special-skill mark without needing to personally break.
alternatives.tradeoff: Tanya retains straightforward Toughness pressure and party CRIT Rate Up rather than relying on a highest-ATK partner.

construct-gadget.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

detective-watson.summary:
Lily is a Moon area attacker with a supportive barrier skill. Lily's Precious Moment shields the other allies and gives her a personal crit/speed state; Mr. Rabbit's Instant Verdict then gains damage while that state is active and can lower enemy ATK.

Use her as an area attacker who contributes protection to the other three slots. The special’s 50% action progress helps setup but does not shield Lily herself or guarantee the next turn. Build ATK for attacks and barriers, then speed and enough durability to survive the gap. Emily is a useful partner because her targeted Barrier covers Lily’s own exclusion.
detective-watson.watch: Her party barrier excludes Lily, and her skill grants 50% progress toward another turn rather than an immediate extra turn. The Moon-hit resource loop is absent at passive level 1; she cannot be assumed to cycle it on first copy.
detective-watson.dependency_note: Use other Moon allies who can survive being attacked if you want the upgraded passive's Chill generation. She needs actual healing and personal protection because the barrier skill protects everyone except her.

skill_order.name: Lily's Precious Moment
skill_order.why: Levels 6 and 10 reduce barrier-skill cooldown; barrier upgrade nodes support her distinctive team contribution.

skill_order.name: Mr. Rabbit's Instant Verdict
skill_order.why: Levels 6 and 10 reduce ultimate cooldown; its damage improves when Consulting is active.

skill_order.name: Strike Amidst the Chaos
skill_order.why: Basic damage is last; it builds Chill but does not solve her need for protection.

rotation: Use Lily's Precious Moment before incoming damage to shield other allies and establish ATK Up plus Detective Consulting on Lily.
Use Mr. Rabbit's Instant Verdict while Consulting is active when possible for its 30% damage bonus; do not delay needed ATK Down through a lethal enemy turn.
At upgraded passive levels, attacks into other Moon allies build Lily's Chill. Five Chill at her turn start converts into Consulting automatically; it is not a separate cast.
Use Strike Amidst the Chaos between cooldowns and protect Lily herself. Nova Verdict changes the ATK Down application chance, not the enemy's ability to resist or ignore debuffs.

best_partners.why: Emily is a Moon defender who can give Lily a targeted barrier, covering the self-exclusion of Precious Moment; attacks into Emily can feed Lily's upgraded passive.
Frey gives team crit support and benefits from Lily's Moon attacks through Cash In; Frey still does not replace a healer.
Party healing/cleanse keeps Lily alive while she prepares Consulting, and turn progress helps recover from her low stored SPD.

detective-watson.build_tip: ATK improves attacks and the ally barriers; add SPD so she can shield before damage and crit for her personal attacks. Use enough HP/DEF to survive despite her own barrier exclusion, with Effect Hit only if ATK Down is a key job. Journey option: Rabbit with Two Faces is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +5% at Arcana level 1. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
detective-watson.tier_reason: The stored B PvE / D+ PvP ratings fit conditional area damage and useful ally barriers with slow setup and little immediate denial. PvE can allow her Consulting window; PvP exposes her 90-SPD starting profile, self-excluded barrier and delayed payoff.
detective-watson.investment: Buy Precious Moment cooldown reductions at levels 6/10 if barriers are why she is selected, then Verdict cooldowns at 6/10. Mystery Duo level 1 is only ATK; level 2 introduces Moon-ally-hit Chill and ultimate gauge gain, which reaches 20% at passive level 4. No potentials are listed. Barrier effect rows show a maximum value and do not establish the starting shield strength. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 2 at level 40, listing +4 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
detective-watson.pve_note: Useful for a deliberate wave plan: shield allies, establish Consulting, then use the boosted area ultimate. Bosses immune to ATK Down remove part of the defensive utility, and barriers cannot restore damage already taken.
detective-watson.pvp_note: Prefer faster or more complete utility if the team cannot afford a setup action. Enemy area damage can both feed a later passive and hurt Lily, so taking damage is not automatically a favorable trade.

kit_explanation.name: Strike Amidst the Chaos
kit_explanation.explanation: Strike Amidst the Chaos is a single-target basic granting one Chill. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage. Chill can later be converted by Mystery Duo, but that conversion is not in passive level 1.

kit_explanation.name: Lily's Precious Moment
kit_explanation.explanation: Lily's Precious Moment is a non-attacking skill on a listed five-turn cooldown, reduced at levels 6 and 10. It grants two-turn ATK-scaled barriers to all other allies, while Lily gets ATK Up, two-turn Consulting and 50% next-turn progress. Consulting adds 20% CRIT Rate and 15% SPD. Nova restores her Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: Mr. Rabbit's Instant Verdict
kit_explanation.explanation: Mr. Rabbit's Instant Verdict attacks all enemies on a listed six-turn cooldown reduced at levels 6 and 10, grants Chill and attempts two-turn ATK Down at 75%. With Consulting already active, it deals 30% more damage. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and lists 100% ATK Down application chance; it still does not promise success against Immunity.

kit_explanation.name: Mystery Duo
kit_explanation.explanation: Mystery Duo is ATK only at passive level 1. From level 2, Verdict also advances Lily's next turn by 10–20%, attacks on another Moon ally grant Chill, and five Chill at her turn start are consumed to grant two-turn Consulting. Higher passive levels also improve ATK.

pros: ATK investment supports both party barriers and personal damage.
Consulting grants crit/speed and explicitly improves ultimate damage.
Upgraded passive can turn attacks on other Moon allies into her next setup state.
Her area ultimate attempts ATK Down as a defensive contribution.
cons: The barrier skill excludes Lily herself.
No healing or cleanse despite occupying a supportive slot.
Slow setup and passive-level requirements limit early or fast-PvP value.

teams.name: Shielded Moon area setup
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Frey supplies crit support, Emily supplies Lily's missing personal barrier and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses. Moon allies can feed Mystery Duo when attacked.
teams.playstyle: Establish Consulting before Verdict when safe; do not overlap every defensive action if a later enemy attack is the real danger.

teams.name: Moon focused and area mix
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Claire handles a priority target, Emily protects Lily, and Serpang heals while attempting enemy ATK/Effect RES Down.
teams.playstyle: Use Lily's barrier before area damage, then Consulting Verdict for waves; Claire handles the surviving durable target.

alternatives.why: Rosaria is a higher-rated area attacker with DEF Down and 50% next-turn progress in the damage action itself.
alternatives.tradeoff: Lily retains barriers for other allies and ATK Down; Rosaria does not replace that support coverage.

alternatives.why: Emily is a higher-utility PvE protective slot when the carry needs a targeted barrier/ATK Up and party DEF Up.
alternatives.tradeoff: Lily retains a barrier for every other ally from one skill and Consulting-boosted area damage, but still needs healing.

detective-watson.research_note: Community build checked against the stored skills; advice is kit-based, and paid details were unavailable.

mutant-mask.summary:
Kyra is a single-target disruptor who uses Stealth to gain damage and delay an enemy's next turn. Distorted Attention gives her Stealth and attempts Silence plus ATK Down; Price of Silence then rewards both her own Stealth and a Silenced target. Allies can also supply Silence so the payoff is not limited to her short window.

Choose Kyra for focused disruption with a team that can keep her Stealth useful. Her ultimate attempts one turn of Silence and two turns of ATK Down, while Stealth lets the special reduce enemy Action gauge by 30%. The Silence damage bonus needs the debuff still active when the hit lands. Her stored 90 SPD makes that timing a build concern. Area attacks still reach her, and losing the other allies removes Stealth’s protection against direct targeting.
mutant-mask.watch: Stealth prevents direct targeting only while other allies are present; it is not protection from all area damage. Her Silence lasts one turn and can be resisted or removed, so a fixed ultimate-then-special sequence may miss the bonus if the enemy acts between them.
mutant-mask.dependency_note: She can establish Stealth and Silence herself, but an allied Silence provider improves timing. A healer and actual protection cover area damage; a team that simply leaves her last alive removes Stealth's targeting protection.

skill_order.name: Distorted Attention
skill_order.why: Get cooldown reductions at levels 6/10 for Stealth and control access.

skill_order.name: Price of Silence
skill_order.why: Then level 6 for cooldown and level 10 for stronger conditional turn delay.

skill_order.name: Flesh-Cutting Kotodama
skill_order.why: Passive upgrades improve damage from Stealth, not immunity or untargetability against every attack.

skill_order.name: Unusual Greeting
skill_order.why: Basic damage follows the two utility attacks; its resource trigger exists independently of damage upgrades.

rotation: Use Distorted Attention to establish Stealth and attempt control on a dangerous target.

Use Price of Silence while Stealth is active; seek a still-Silenced target for the damage bonus, including Silence supplied by Bell. Check remaining duration rather than assuming Kyra's own Silence lasts until her next turn.

Use Unusual Greeting when its resource gain can renew Stealth or cooldown skills are unavailable. Nova can supply Stealth after the basic when worthwhile; automatic Stealth refresh is not another cast.

best_partners.why: Bell's two-turn Silence can supply a longer window for Price of Silence's damage bonus and removes enemy buffs.
Kyra's Sun attacking cooldown skills feed Cristelle's Ignition; ATK Down and Silence add debuffs for chain damage.
Ceres heals area damage and cleanses Kyra without relying on Stealth to prevent every hit.
Emily's Barrier protects Kyra against damage Stealth does not avoid and supplies an ATK buff when needed.

mutant-mask.build_tip: SPD and suitable Effect Hit for timing control, then ATK and critical stats. Add survival for area attacks. Her listed maximum SPD is 90, so a fast control plan needs real build support rather than the Assassin label. As Cute as Kyra! supports Strength and improves Condition Effect after 70 Bond. Girl of Kotodama supports Focus for the debuff plan.
mutant-mask.tier_reason: The A PvE / A+ PvP ratings fit a conditional single-target control attacker. Stealth, Silence and turn delay have practical opponent-facing value, while boss immunity and area damage reduce the benefits that distinguish her.
mutant-mask.investment: Prioritize Distorted Attention's two cooldown milestones, then Price of Silence's cooldown and turn-delay upgrade. No potentials are listed. Do not infer a star-based Stealth or Silence unlock from the final stored passive. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
mutant-mask.pve_note: Useful alongside Cristelle against debuff-susceptible targets. Against Silence immunity she keeps ATK Down attempts and Stealth-based utility, but loses Price of Silence's conditional damage unless another valid source can apply Silence.
mutant-mask.pvp_note: Time control and Stealth around actual enemy turns. A listed 100% debuff chance is not guaranteed against resistance/immunity, and a short Silence does not prove a repeatable control lock.

kit_explanation.name: Unusual Greeting
kit_explanation.explanation: Unusual Greeting attacks one target and adds Ignition. Nova gives Stealth after the attack and adds Toughness damage. With the passive, reaching maximum Ignition after this basic spends the stacks for one turn of Stealth.

kit_explanation.name: Price of Silence
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 4 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Price of Silence hits one target, grants two turns of ATK Up and two Ignition. While Kyra is in Stealth it reduces the target's progress toward its next turn by 20%, rising to 30% at level 10. A target already under Silence takes 30% more damage from the skill. It does not apply Silence itself.

kit_explanation.name: Distorted Attention
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Distorted Attention hits one enemy, grants two turns of Stealth and two Ignition, and attempts two turns of ATK Down plus one turn of Silence at listed 100% chances. Levels 6 and 10 shorten cooldown. The Silence can expire before Kyra's next action if the target gets a turn.

kit_explanation.name: Flesh-Cutting Kotodama
kit_explanation.explanation: Flesh-Cutting Kotodama increases Kyra's damage while she attacks from Stealth, from 6% to 10% across levels, and later adds ATK. After Unusual Greeting reaches maximum Ignition it spends all Ignition to grant Stealth. This resource trigger belongs to the basic, not every attack.

pros: Can create her own Stealth and Silence setup.
Special combines conditional damage and enemy turn delay.
Sun attacks and multiple debuffs have explicit Cristelle synergy.
The basic’s Nova provides another one-turn Stealth route.
cons: Silence window can expire before her next turn.
Stealth does not prevent all area damage or work alone.
No self-heal and low listed maximum SPD.

teams.name: Shared Silence (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell supplies a longer Silence and buff removal; Emily protects Kyra and Ceres heals.
teams.playstyle: Have Kyra use Price of Silence before the target's Silence expires, while preserving Stealth and checking actual turn order.

teams.name: Sun debuff chain (theorycraft)
teams.why: Scarlet supplies Burn, Kyra supplies Silence/ATK Down and Cristelle rewards the debuff count while Ceres sustains.
teams.playstyle: Use Sun attacking skills to feed Cristelle, then focus a debuffed target; do not sacrifice urgent control just to add one more chain instance.

alternatives.why: Bell is higher-rated in PvP and brings two-turn Silence, all-buff removal and broad ACC Down.
alternatives.tradeoff: She lacks Kyra's Stealth and conditional ordinary-special turn delay; building a different character may be unnecessary if Kyra's specific role already works.

alternatives.why: Carnelia is higher-rated in both modes and adds area pressure, Buff Block and ordinary-special turn delay.
alternatives.tradeoff: She prevents new buffs rather than applying Silence or hiding in Stealth, so replacing Kyra changes the control plan.

mutant-mask.research_note: Public character build reviewed; gear details were image-only or gated, so no unseen set or slot recommendation is claimed.

dress-stranis.summary:
Dress Asherah is an HP-scaling healer and cleanser, not the damage-focused Voyager or Dark variants. Bal Doré heals while attacking; Lumière Sonnet heals the party, removes two debuffs and helps other allies reach their next turns. Her upgraded passive makes basic attacks contribute targeted recovery.

Choose her to stabilize a whole party rather than rescue one marked carry. Maximum HP improves her recovery and her attacking skills, while speed helps her reach cleansing windows sooner. Insight increases the upgraded passive’s Dual Attack Chance, letting ordinary attacks add recovery between cooldowns. Those automatic opportunities are useful background sustain, but she still needs to act in time: neither healing nor a delayed cleanse can reverse a teammate’s defeat.
dress-stranis.watch: She has no native revive or barrier. Her basic's targeted heal and Insight-based dual-attack chance are higher-passive mechanics, while the basic cleanse requires Nova. The source's high-rating investment assumption should not be confused with a locally verified unlock breakpoint.
dress-stranis.dependency_note: She supports almost any team that needs recovery, cleanse and turn progress. Choose teammates whose offense benefits from staying active; do not select her as a substitute for a specialized damage dealer.

skill_order.name: Lumière Sonnet
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown on party recovery, two-debuff cleanse and allied turn progress; prioritize this for debuff-heavy fights.

skill_order.name: Bal Doré
skill_order.why: Recovery nodes at levels 2/3/6/8/10 improve the repeatable attacking heal; prioritize earlier if ordinary damage is the main threat.

skill_order.name: Belle Lame
skill_order.why: Damage upgrades are last; Nova utility and higher-passive basic healing matter more than the basic hit itself.

rotation: Use Lumière Sonnet when two-debuff party cleanse, recovery or allied turn progress changes the fight; do not spend it only because it is available if a dangerous debuff wave is imminent.
Use Bal Doré for routine party healing while attacking, gaining Starlight Wish and Insight; its SPD/Effect RES buff helps Asherah herself, not the entire team.
Between cooldowns, use Belle Lame. At the relevant passive level it also heals the lowest-HP-ratio ally; with Nova it removes one debuff from all allies.
Let Insight build the upgraded passive's dual-attack chance naturally, but do not treat a chance-based dual attack as a manually scheduled emergency heal.

best_partners.why: Emily's barriers and DEF Up reduce incoming damage, while Asherah restores HP and removes debuffs that Emily's kit does not explicitly cleanse.
Bal Doré is an attacking special that contributes to Gwen's Electric Shock during Standby, while healing keeps Gwen's other allies alive.
Healing and cleanse keep the break carry active; Lumière Sonnet's allied turn progress helps reach Shatter/break windows without requiring shared damage roles.

dress-stranis.build_tip: Prioritize Max HP for both heals and HP-scaled attacks, then SPD, DEF and appropriate resistance. Her own Starlight Wish adds resistance, but it is not Immunity; avoid diverting healing investment into crit unless survival and recovery are already sufficient. Young Lady of Stranis is a Vitality fit for her HP scaling; its unique adds one Vitality during training after 30 Bond.
dress-stranis.tier_reason: The stored S+ PvE / S PvP ratings fit broad recovery, party cleanse and allied turn progress. The source explicitly ties its high assessment to a three-star investment assumption; local data does not verify that as a particular passive unlock. Long PvE fights favor repeated recovery, while PvP still requires surviving until she acts.
dress-stranis.investment: Prioritize Lumière Sonnet level 6 and Bal Doré recovery upgrades, plus HP. L'unisson level 1 is only HP; level 2 adds basic-triggered healing and Insight-based dual-attack chance, scaling from 10% to 20% per stack by passive level 4. The community rating source states the high-rating build assumes three stars; this is a source investment claim, not a verified local star-to-passive breakpoint. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
dress-stranis.pve_note: Use Bal Doré to cover routine damage and save Sonnet for a dangerous debuff or broad recovery window. HP scaling makes defensive investment productive, but cleanse removes two debuffs rather than every possible debuff.
dress-stranis.pvp_note: Her cleanse and turn progress can recover a team from disruption if she gets an action. Two removals may leave harmful effects behind, and she cannot revive an ally already defeated or guarantee immunity against the next control effect.

kit_explanation.name: Belle Lame
kit_explanation.explanation: Belle Lame is a single-target basic with ATK and Max HP damage scaling, granting one Insight. With an upgraded L'unisson it also heals the lowest-HP-ratio ally. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and removes one debuff from all allies; ordinary basics do not include that cleanse.
