kit_explanation.name: Bal Doré
kit_explanation.explanation: Bal Doré attacks one enemy on a three-turn cooldown and heals every ally, with both damage and healing scaling partly or fully from Asherah's Max HP. It grants Insight and two-turn Starlight Wish, which gives Asherah 10% SPD and 30% Effect RES. Recovery improves at the listed recovery nodes. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Lumière Sonnet
kit_explanation.explanation: Lumière Sonnet is a non-attacking party heal on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It removes two debuffs from each ally, grants one Insight and gives every other ally 15% progress toward their next turn. Healing scales with her Max HP. Nova restores her Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: L'unisson
kit_explanation.explanation: L'unisson begins as a 5% Max HP bonus. From passive level 2, Belle Lame also heals the lowest-HP-ratio ally and each Insight adds 10–20% dual-attack chance depending on passive level, capped at five stacks. Higher levels also raise the HP bonus. These later mechanics should not be assumed from the first passive level.

pros: Party healing and two-debuff cleanse share one skill.
Can heal while attacking with Bal Doré and, at upgraded passive levels, her basic.
HP investment improves recovery and durability together; Sonnet also advances other allies.
Sonnet advances every other ally by 15% Action gauge.
cons: No revive, barrier or complete prevention of incoming debuffs.
Basic recovery and high dual-attack chance require later passive mechanics.
Healing cannot save a teammate defeated before she acts, and two removals may not clear a full debuff stack.

teams.name: Sustained break carry
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Emily supplies barrier/DEF coverage, Dark Asherah supplies Shatter and boss breaks, and Gille amplifies those windows. Dress Asherah keeps the setup team healthy and cleansed.
teams.playstyle: Use routine attacking heals while preserving Sonnet for a dangerous debuff phase; do not spend every support action before the boss responds.

teams.name: Protected special engine
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Professor M and Gwen generate repeated attacks, Hilde gives opening protection, and Bal Doré contributes an attacking special while healing.
teams.playstyle: Keep allies alive for Gwen's Standby, cleanse disruption when it threatens the engine, and select targets according to the real mark/shock state.

alternatives.why: Kingdom Frey can fully cleanse one ally with Rapid Resupply and provide party barriers, useful when one carry has many debuffs.
alternatives.tradeoff: Dress Asherah retains broader repeated party healing, two-debuff party cleanse and allied turn progress; Frey is a situational tool rather than a universal upgrade.

alternatives.why: Serpang is a sidegrade when Sun recovery bonuses, enemy ATK/Effect RES Down or skill-damage nullification are specifically needed.
alternatives.tradeoff: Dress Asherah provides party cleanse and direct allied turn progress; Serpang does not replace those and needs separate debuff handling.

alternatives.why: Maid Ceres is a strong alternative when you want a party ATK buff and extra group heals fed by allied turns, rather than Waltz Asherah's dual-attack-based recovery.
alternatives.tradeoff: Maid Ceres removes fewer debuffs per ordinary cleanse and needs her cleaning counters for extra healing. Waltz Asherah retains party turn-progress support and her own established recovery loop; compare actual upgrades, not only the shared high PvE tier.

dress-stranis.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

wedding-shielder.summary:
Wedding Carmen protects the highest-ATK ally selected at the first battle’s start. Damage sharing, automatic rescue and party recovery on her basic create a sustained carry-protection kit, while Wedding March provides a targeted cleanse/heal and feeds Chill to Moon allies.

Choose her when keeping one attacker alive matters more than adding another damage dealer. Set the intended carry’s ATK highest before battle so Oath reaches the right ally, then keep Carmen healthy enough to absorb redirected damage. Guardian Knight is an automatic response with a cooldown, not an extra button to cast whenever someone is hurt. Her basic attacks provide group recovery, while her targeted ultimate handles an urgent cleanse.
wedding-shielder.watch: The oath target is selected by ATK at the first battle’s start, not freely chosen each turn. Only the highest damage-sharing effect applies; the description ties its protection to single-target attacks. Wedding March’s prose says “allies,” but its Single Ally target and cleanse effect point to one target: do not promise a party-wide cleanse.
wedding-shielder.dependency_note: Build ATK ordering around the intended oath carry and keep Carmen alive through redirected damage. She protects a damage plan rather than replacing a damage dealer.

skill_order.name: Guardian Knight
skill_order.why: Guardian Knight’s level-6 cooldown and level-4/8 turn-progress improvements make repeated automatic rescue more useful.

skill_order.name: Wedding March
skill_order.why: Wedding March’s level-6 cooldown supports more targeted cleanse/heal access.

skill_order.name: Oath
skill_order.why: Higher passive levels add HP and increase Carmen’s progress after the oath ally takes single-target attacks.

skill_order.name: Do Not Disturb
skill_order.why: Basic damage is last; using it remains important because Oath triggers party recovery afterward.

rotation: Before battle, check who actually has the highest ATK and will receive Oath of Devotion; do not assume the portrait you prefer is selected.
Use Wedding March when the important ally needs debuffs removed and HP restored. A Moon recipient also gains three Chill, but do not waste an urgently needed cleanse merely for stacks.
Use Do Not Disturb between support uses: Oath heals the whole party afterward, with greater recovery when full Chill is consumed. Nova adds a separate lowest-HP ally heal.

Guardian Knight triggers automatically when the oath ally is attacked and the reaction is ready. Watch Carmen’s HP as redirected damage and rescue cycles accumulate; do not schedule a manual Guardian Knight cast.

best_partners.why: A Moon carry can receive three Chill from Wedding March, directly strengthening Blade Gale’s Chill-based turn reduction.
Wedding March is a non-attack that can feed Lugh’s Snow Blossom before Swift Decree, while oath protection helps the slash setup.
Carmen can protect Amora as the highest-ATK ally and remove debuffs that would suppress Amora’s clean-state damage bonus.

wedding-shielder.build_tip: HP first for recovery, Barrier and redirected-damage survival; add SPD and DEF so she can keep supporting. Resistance helps avoid support interruption but is not immunity. Set ally ATK ordering deliberately rather than maximizing everyone’s displayed power. A Drowsy Afternoon Interlude fits HP training: its unique adds one Vitality during training after 50 Bond. Night View Beyond the Window instead supports Protection.
wedding-shielder.tier_reason: The top published rating in both modes fits a broad protection package: damage sharing, automatic rescue, basic-based party healing and targeted full cleanse. Its conditions still matter: protect the right oath ally and keep Carmen alive; the published rating is not proof of universal survival.
wedding-shielder.investment: Guardian Knight level 6 lowers reaction cooldown and levels 4/8 raise its gauge support. Wedding March level 6 improves access to cleanse/heal. The unique potential also named Wedding March adds one maximum Toughness and two Nova Force after special/ultimate use if acquired; distinguish it from the active skill of the same name. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here.
wedding-shielder.pve_note: Strong fit for a focused carry with repeated incoming damage. Party recovery on basics supports longer stages, but heavy area debuffs may still require an actual party cleanser because her targeted ultimate should not be treated as one.
wedding-shielder.pvp_note: Protects a chosen-by-stats carry and rewards attacks on it with rescue and turn progress. The opponent can pressure Carmen or another ally, and reaction cooldowns plus redirected damage prevent assuming every hit is fully covered.

kit_explanation.name: Do Not Disturb
kit_explanation.explanation: Do Not Disturb is a single-target basic that adds one Chill and scales partly with Carmen’s maximum HP. Her passive heals all allies after this basic; the basic Nova additionally heals the lowest-HP ally. The party heal is passive behavior, not a separate cast.

kit_explanation.name: Guardian Knight
kit_explanation.explanation: Guardian Knight is a reaction with a listed three-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. An attack on the oath ally triggers healing, a two-turn HP-based Barrier and progress toward both allies’ next turns, rising from 15% to 30%. It also gives Carmen two Chill and cannot be manually selected.

kit_explanation.name: Wedding March
kit_explanation.explanation: Wedding March has a listed five-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. It grants Carmen three Chill, removes debuffs and heals its target; a Moon target also gains three Chill. Although the description uses a plural, the stored target and cleanse entry are single-target, so plan this as targeted support until confirmed otherwise.

kit_explanation.name: Oath
kit_explanation.explanation: Oath selects the highest-ATK ally at the first battle’s start for Oath of Devotion, which adds Effect RES and persists through revival. Its description links 40% damage sharing and Carmen’s turn progress to single-target attacks on that ally; only the strongest sharing effect applies. Do not assume this covers all area damage. After her basic Carmen heals all allies, consuming full Chill for stronger recovery. Higher passive levels add HP and turn progress.

pros: Combines damage sharing with automatic heal/Barrier rescue for the oath carry.
Party recovery on basics gives useful actions between cooldowns.
Targeted full cleanse and Moon Chill feed support several different carries.
Unique potential can add maximum Toughness and Nova resource generation.
cons: ATK ordering can assign the oath to the wrong ally.
Redirected damage creates a real survival burden for Carmen.
Reaction cooldown prevents every incoming hit from receiving a fresh rescue.
Stored target data does not support advertising Wedding March as a party-wide cleanse.

teams.name: Moon control carry
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Ceres can use Moon Chill feed, Voyager Luna adds area vulnerability and dress Asherah supplies true party cleanse/recovery.
teams.playstyle: Set Ceres as highest ATK if she is the oath plan, use Wedding March for needed cleanse/Chill and let Guardian Knight react automatically.

teams.name: Protected slash engine
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Carmen and Elisa offer non-attack support for Lugh’s flowers, Lydia slows enemies and Elisa adds revival insurance.
teams.playstyle: Make Lugh the intended oath target, prepare flowers without wasting heals and keep Carmen healthy enough to bear redirected damage.

alternatives.why: A same-PvE-tier sidegrade when the carry needs targeted ATK Up and Barrier plus more area damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: Carmen retains damage sharing, targeted full cleanse and party recovery after basics; Emily does not reproduce that package.

alternatives.why: A same-PvE-tier sidegrade for repeated party healing and two-debuff party cleanse when area debuffs are the main problem.
alternatives.tradeoff: Carmen keeps oath-based protection, reactive Barriers and Moon Chill feed, which dress Asherah does not replace.

wedding-shielder.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

wedding-dualsword.summary:
Wedding Epindel specializes in attacking Barriers: Bouquet Toss gains extra damage against a shielded target and can advance the highest-ATK teammate if it breaks that Barrier. Sun allies and allied critical hits feed Ignition for her conditional extra turn.

Her useful job is punishing shields, rather than leading every damage team. Build enough speed to reach the shield window, then ATK and critical stats. Sun teammates accelerate Ignition, but her extra turn still requires the full-stack condition. Against enemies without barriers, much of the special attack’s identity disappears.
wedding-dualsword.watch: Breaking a Barrier is not the same as merely hitting one, and Bouquet Toss does not automatically dispel it. The extra turn requires full Ignition after attacking on her own turn; the ally gauge reward requires an actual Barrier break.
wedding-dualsword.dependency_note: She wants enemies that use Barriers and allies that feed Ignition or capitalize on the highest-ATK ally’s turn progress. Without those conditions she loses much of her special utility.

skill_order.name: Bouquet Toss
skill_order.why: Bouquet Toss is the anti-Barrier payoff and level 6 reduces its cooldown.

skill_order.name: Bride's Entrance
skill_order.why: Bride’s Entrance has a level-6 cooldown upgrade and stronger shielded-target gauge reduction at levels 4/8.

skill_order.name: Purewhite Resolve
skill_order.why: Passive levels improve Sun-ally stack generation consistency and add ATK.

skill_order.name: Falconet Strike
skill_order.why: Basic damage is secondary to the anti-Barrier tools and stack engine.

rotation: When an enemy has a Barrier, consider Bouquet Toss before another ally removes it so Epindel can use the extra damage and possibly earn the Barrier-break ally gauge reward.
If five Ignition is reachable safely before Bouquet Toss, its own-turn full-stack check can grant an extra turn. Do not delay a necessary attack solely to force that bonus.
Use Bride's Entrance for area pressure and SPD Up, especially when several relevant enemy Barriers are present; its turn reduction is conditional on shielded targets.
Fill with Falconet Strike and let allied critical hits/Sun turns feed the passive. Bouquet Toss clears Ignition after its effects, so rebuild rather than assuming permanent five stacks.

best_partners.why: Harley can grant three Ignition to the highest-ATK Sun ally; set Epindel as that recipient if feeding her is the plan.
Sun turns help upgraded Purewhite Resolve, while Luna supplies defensive support and debuffs to expose the priority target.
Her on-attack CRIT Rate bonus supports Epindel’s allied-critical stack trigger; she can also benefit from Bouquet Toss’s highest-ATK ally gauge reward if geared for it.

wedding-dualsword.build_tip: ATK and critical stats to actually break Barriers, then SPD for timely pressure. Highest-ATK targeting matters: Epindel should be the top Sun ATK for Harley’s feed, while Bouquet Toss’s reward explicitly excludes Epindel. Journey option: Till Death Do Us Part is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
wedding-dualsword.tier_reason: The higher PvP than PvE rating fits an enemy-Barrier counterpick rather than universal damage superiority. PvE enemies without Barriers remove both the special’s matchup damage and its ally reward; PvP still requires enough damage to break the shield.
wedding-dualsword.investment: Prioritize Bouquet Toss’s level-6 cooldown and damage, then Bride’s Entrance’s level-6 cooldown and level-4/8 gauge gains. Higher passive levels improve Sun-turn Ignition rolls from 60% to 100%. No unique potential is listed. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +3 CRIT Rate; it is not part of the starting stat line.
wedding-dualsword.pve_note: Use when a stage actually presents durable Barriers or when the Sun stack engine fits the roster. Against unshielded bosses, compare a less conditional damage dealer before investing heavily.
wedding-dualsword.pvp_note: A targeted answer to shielded opponents when Epindel can access and break the Barrier. Preemptive Guard, resistance and mitigation can still interfere; her anti-Barrier damage is not an unconditional kill.

kit_explanation.name: Falconet Strike
kit_explanation.explanation: Falconet Strike is a single-target basic adding one Ignition. It fills gaps between anti-Barrier skills; its Nova Burst adds one Toughness damage, without adding an automatic extra turn.

kit_explanation.name: Bouquet Toss
kit_explanation.explanation: Bouquet Toss attacks one target on a listed four-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6. It attempts 20% enemy turn-progress reduction and deals extra damage against Barrier. Breaking the Barrier grants 30% progress to the highest-ATK other ally. Full Ignition after an own-turn attack grants an extra turn; it then gives ATK Up and clears Ignition.

kit_explanation.name: Bride's Entrance
kit_explanation.explanation: Bride's Entrance attacks all enemies on a listed five-turn cooldown, reduced at level 6, and gives two-turn SPD Up. Shielded targets suffer turn-progress reduction that rises from 10% to 20%; damage gains 15% per enemy Barrier counted, capped at three. The wording does not establish that every Barrier on every unit is always counted identically.

kit_explanation.name: Purewhite Resolve
kit_explanation.explanation: Purewhite Resolve grants Ignition when an ally critically hits. At a Sun ally’s turn start it attempts two Ignition stacks, each with a chance rising from 60% to 100% by passive level. Higher levels also add ATK. These stacks are automatic and are consumed by Bouquet Toss, not by a separate command.

pros: Has a clear matchup advantage against Barriers rather than generic damage only.
A successful Barrier break can advance another attacker’s next turn.
Sun turns and allied critical hits provide two passive stack sources.
A full Ignition attack can earn an extra turn.
cons: Anti-Barrier payoff shrinks against teams without shields.
Ally turn gain requires breaking the shield, not just damaging it.
No innate healing, Barrier or cleanse to survive a failed burst.

teams.name: Sun shield breaker
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Harley feeds Ignition, Summer Luna supplies protection and dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Make Epindel highest Sun ATK for Harley; target an existing enemy Barrier before it disappears.

teams.name: Two-carry Barrier punish
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Roberta supplies critical-hit opportunities and can receive the Barrier-break gauge reward; Carmen/Frey cover sustain.
teams.playstyle: Choose ATK ordering deliberately: Bouquet Toss excludes Epindel when selecting its ally reward, while Carmen selects the highest-ATK ally for her oath.

alternatives.why: Amora is higher-rated in both modes and gives less matchup-dependent area pressure, an extra turn and conditional cleanse.
alternatives.tradeoff: Epindel keeps her specific Barrier damage and ally turn reward when shield-breaking is the actual job.

alternatives.why: Ceres is a higher-rated option when removing an enemy buff and disrupting its turn is more useful than dealing shield damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: Epindel rewards actually breaking a Barrier and can feed another carry’s turn; a dispel is a different way of solving protection.

wedding-dualsword.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

bunny-pray.summary:
Bunny Frey is a Moon damage dealer and CRIT Rate supporter, not the healing Kingdom Frey. She builds High Roller through Bullseye, Chill conversion and Moon allies attacking, then her basic changes into Forced Negotiation at five High Roller on her own turn.

Use Frey (Noble Princess) when several attackers can use a three-turn 30% CRIT Rate buff. All In gives her an extra turn, while Moon allies’ attacks feed High Roller and advance her next turn by 8%. At five High Roller, her own-turn basic becomes the stronger Forced Negotiation and returns another 30% gauge. Gear around that team’s actual crit needs: her main buff has little value on already capped attackers. A separate healer remains necessary.
bunny-pray.watch: High Roller has five stacks, while Bullseye only attempts three applications; one ultimate does not guarantee the empowered basic. The CRIT buff is for the party, but the ATK buff and turn acceleration are for Frey herself.
bunny-pray.dependency_note: Moon allies attacking grant her turn progress and High Roller chances through Cash In. Pick attackers that benefit from CRIT Rate Up; she still needs a healer or protective teammate.

skill_order.name: Bullseye
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown and level 8 raises all three High Roller rolls to 100%, directly improving the empowered-basic setup.

skill_order.name: All In
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves party-buff access; level 10 makes the three Chill rolls certain.

skill_order.name: Bet Refusal
skill_order.why: Invest in the basic because Forced Negotiation is its empowered form and a main resource payoff.

rotation: Use All In when teammates need CRIT Rate Up; take the extra turn to use Bullseye if available or a basic if its five-High-Roller condition is already met.
Bullseye creates up to three High Roller stacks. Check the visible count before expecting Forced Negotiation; Moon ally attacks and start-of-turn Chill conversion can fill the gap.
At five High Roller, select Bet Refusal on her own turn: it becomes Forced Negotiation automatically, hits harder, advances her next turn and consumes High Roller.
Between empowered basics, preserve useful CRIT buff uptime and let Moon attacks feed Cash In. Do not wait for five Chill if an immediate area hit or team buff solves the encounter.

best_partners.why: Claire's Moon attacks feed Cash In; Frey's CRIT Rate Up helps Where Are You Looking? crit for three Chill.
Professor M is Moon and attacks repeatedly through her own basic and reactive skill; eligible attacks feed Frey while her dual-attack support adds pressure.
Emily is Moon, grants a targeted barrier/ATK Up and attacks while protecting the group; these attacks also feed Cash In.

bunny-pray.build_tip: Build ATK and enough CRIT Rate after accounting for her 30% party buff, then CRIT DMG and SPD. Do not build her as a healer because of her character name; she has none of Kingdom Frey's recovery skills. The Indomitable Masterpiece supports Strength and improves Sensory Training chance after 40 Bond; The Princess Ascends the Throne instead supports Vitality.
bunny-pray.tier_reason: The stored S PvE / A PvP ratings fit a useful crit-support attacker whose own damage needs High Roller cycling. Moon attack-heavy PvE teams can feed both her resources and next-turn progress. Short PvP rounds, disrupted setup and already crit-capped teammates reduce her contribution; she is not a healer.
bunny-pray.investment: Bullseye level 8 is a concrete stack-reliability milestone; All In level 6/10 improves cadence/reliability. Cash In's High Roller chance after Moon attacks grows from 50% to 100% across passive levels, while its 8% turn progress remains constant. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
bunny-pray.pve_note: Use her in longer encounters where five High Roller can be reached and crit support helps multiple allies. Pair area Bullseye with an actual defensive support; she cannot recover the team's HP.
bunny-pray.pvp_note: All In offers immediate crit support and an extra turn, but 90 stored SPD makes a first-action setup uncertain. Do not model Forced Negotiation as available from the start without checking High Roller.

kit_explanation.name: Bet Refusal
kit_explanation.explanation: Bet Refusal hits one enemy and adds Chill. At five High Roller on her own turn it automatically becomes Forced Negotiation, which deals 100% increased damage, adds 30% next-turn progress and Chill, then removes High Roller. Nova adds damage and fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: All In
kit_explanation.explanation: All In is a party CRIT Rate buff lasting three turns, on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It tries to give Frey Chill three times, with each roll rising from 75% to 100% through upgrades, and grants an extra turn. Nova restores her Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: Bullseye
kit_explanation.explanation: Bullseye attacks all enemies on a listed six-turn cooldown reduced at level 6, then gives Frey two-turn ATK Up and three High Roller rolls. Those rolls rise from 75% to 85% at level 4 and 100% at level 8. High Roller caps at five and slightly strengthens basic damage. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Cash In
kit_explanation.explanation: Cash In is automatic: at the start of her turn, five Chill are exchanged for one High Roller unless High Roller is already full. Another Moon ally attacking gives 8% progress toward Frey's next turn and a 50–100% chance, depending on passive level, of one High Roller. Later passive levels also add ATK.

pros: Three-turn party CRIT Rate Up helps several damage dealers at once.
Moon ally attacks create both resources and next-turn progress.
Empowered basic gives a focused payoff alongside her area ultimate.
All In grants Frey an extra turn after the party buff.
cons: No healing despite sharing a name with a healer variant.
High Roller setup takes more than three successful stacks from one ultimate.
Already crit-capped allies receive little value from her main team buff.

teams.name: Moon crit engine
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Claire uses the crit buff to help her special generate Chill; Emily protects her and supplies Moon attacks, while Dress Asherah handles healing/cleanse.
teams.playstyle: Keep All In up for Claire's special and check Frey's High Roller count before using an empowered basic.

teams.name: Moon follow-up engine
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Professor M's Moon attacks help Cash In while her forced dual attack adds another offensive action. Emily and Dress Asherah provide survival.
teams.playstyle: Choose the intended highest-ATK ally for Professor M; do not assume every trigger or High Roller roll succeeds at low passive levels.

alternatives.why: Tanya also gives party CRIT Rate Up while attacking and can help break Toughness.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her crit buff lasts only one turn, but she has a direct break-support route rather than High Roller setup.

alternatives.why: Dress Asherah is the more relevant slot when the team needs healing, cleanse and allied turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: Provides survival instead of Frey's party crit buff and empowered-basic damage.

bunny-pray.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

stranisearl-roseblade.summary:
Amora combines an area execution with an explicit extra turn, then uses Nocturnal Bloom to act faster and penetrate DEF. Her passive rewards attacking without debuffs and can convert full Insight into a turn-start cleanse and offensive buffs.

Use her when a damage slot must pressure both a wave and its last survivor. The clean-state damage bonus reaches 30%, so pairing her with Waltz Asherah gives more than extra safety: it keeps that bonus available. Her own cleanse waits for a full Insight check at the start of her turn. Build the ATK and critical stats that scale both attacks, then add enough speed to reach her opening before enemy disruption.
stranisearl-roseblade.watch: ACC Down reduces accuracy rather than guaranteeing misses. Her cleanse needs five Insight at turn start, so she is not immediately immune to control and should not deliberately absorb dangerous debuffs.
stranisearl-roseblade.dependency_note: Her ultimate creates its own extra turn and Bloom window. Support improves safety and removes debuffs before her damage check, but no specific teammate is required to enable her basic kit.

skill_order.name: Light-Forged Execution
skill_order.why: Primary area damage and immediate extra turn; levels 4/8 improve area ACC Down chance.

skill_order.name: Piercing Star
skill_order.why: Levels 4/8 improve turn progress and Bloom shortens its cooldown after attacking.

skill_order.name: Master of Stranis
skill_order.why: Upgrades raise ATK and the damage bonus for being debuff-free.

skill_order.name: The Ever-Sober Spear
skill_order.why: Basic investment follows the main damage/turn engine.

rotation: Use Light-Forged Execution when area damage and the extra turn matter; it establishes Nocturnal Bloom rather than requiring several basic attacks first.
On the extra turn, use Piercing Star on the priority enemy when available; Bloom enables its one-turn cooldown reduction after attacking.
Have a cleanser act before Amora’s attack if feasible: Master of Stranis rewards having no debuffs on attack. Her own full-Insight cleanse happens at turn start only.
Use The Ever-Sober Spear to fill cooldown gaps and gain Insight. Watch the next turn-start conversion; do not treat accumulated stacks as an immediate manual cleanse.

best_partners.why: Lumière Sonnet removes two debuffs per ally and advances other allies, helping Amora reach attacks without debuffs.
Protects the highest-ATK ally and provides a targeted full cleanse if Amora receives the oath.
Bind increases all-target damage taken, supporting Light-Forged Execution where the debuff lands.

stranisearl-roseblade.build_tip: ATK and critical stats with SPD for opening pressure. Defensive stats help survive before the Insight cleanse. Effect Hit improves ACC Down where relevant, but it should not consume the entire damage budget. For Journey, pair a Strength card such as Customized Training to Cover Weaknesses with Journey of No Return for Vitality; the latter gives two extra Vitality during training after 30 Bond.
stranisearl-roseblade.tier_reason: The strong PvP rating fits immediate area pressure, extra-turn access and conditional self-cleanse; the PvE rating fits mixed wave and priority-target damage. Boss immunity lowers ACC Down’s value without deleting her damage engine.
stranisearl-roseblade.investment: Upgrade Light-Forged Execution for damage/application and Piercing Star’s level-4/8 gauge gains. Passive levels increase the debuff-free damage bonus from 10% to 30% as well as ATK. No unique potential is listed. Upper effects require the relevant skill/passive level; database maximum stats are not equal-investment outcomes or a zero-star promise. No exact combat star threshold is established here.
stranisearl-roseblade.pve_note: Use the ultimate to clear or soften waves, then focus a survivor with Piercing Star. Cleanse before attacking when possible; not every boss permits accuracy debuffs. Against Despair of Night, extra hits also advance its ten-hit retaliation counter; time the burst around that response.
stranisearl-roseblade.pvp_note: Her immediate extra turn can keep pressure on an exposed target, but turn order still decides whether she survives and whether the opener is disrupted. Self-cleanse is conditional insurance, not permanent immunity.

kit_explanation.name: The Ever-Sober Spear
kit_explanation.explanation: The Ever-Sober Spear is a single-target basic that adds one Insight. Insight normally adds a small stacking damage bonus against Chaos, and also fuels her passive conversion.

kit_explanation.name: Piercing Star
kit_explanation.explanation: Piercing Star attacks one enemy on a listed three-turn cooldown, attempts one-turn ACC Down, adds Insight and grants 15% to 30% progress toward her next turn. With Nocturnal Bloom after attacking it reduces its own cooldown by one.

kit_explanation.name: Light-Forged Execution
kit_explanation.explanation: Light-Forged Execution attacks all enemies on a listed six-turn cooldown, grants three-turn Nocturnal Bloom and an explicit extra turn. It also attempts two-turn ACC Down, improving from 75% to 100% chance. Bloom adds SPD and 20% DEF penetration.

kit_explanation.name: Master of Stranis
kit_explanation.explanation: Master of Stranis boosts damage when Amora has no debuffs. Being attacked while debuffed grants three Insight. At turn start, full Insight is consumed to remove all her debuffs and give two-turn ATK Up plus Bloom. Passive upgrades strengthen the ATK and clean-state damage bonuses.

pros: Ultimate immediately supplies both Bloom and an extra turn.
Bloom improves speed and DEF penetration while supporting special cooldown recycling.
Full Insight can clear all personal debuffs and restore offensive buffs.
Her special supplies 30% Action gauge before any external support.
cons: Clean-state damage bonus is weakened until debuffs are removed.
Self-cleanse waits for a full-stack turn-start check.
No innate team healing or shielding.

teams.name: Clean execution
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Dress Asherah clears debuffs, Carmen protects the intended carry and Ceres dispels/pressures enemy protection.
teams.playstyle: Arrange support before Amora where possible, then use ultimate into a focused special.

teams.name: Area vulnerability pressure
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Voyager Luna provides Bind vulnerability, Summer Luna reduces pressure and Frey supplies cleanse and recovery.
teams.playstyle: Attempt Bind before Amora’s area attack; retain a plan for damage if the debuff fails.

alternatives.why: A same-PvP-tier sidegrade when buff removal and single-target Stun matter more than raw area pressure.
alternatives.tradeoff: Amora retains an explicit ultimate extra turn, Bloom penetration and her own full-debuff cleanse.

alternatives.why: A higher-PvE-rated utility alternative for a team already rich in damage but missing carry protection.
alternatives.tradeoff: Replacing Amora removes a damage slot; Carmen provides recovery and damage sharing rather than execution pressure.

alternatives.why: Carnelia supplies immediate area damage and self-contained tempo through Echo, with Buff Block instead of ACC Down.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her follow-up target is random and her lethal-hit safeguard is once per battle; she lacks Amora’s explicit extra turn and full self-cleanse.

stranisearl-roseblade.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

halloween-beamsword.summary:
Ceres in the Sharp & Sweet variant is a team healer whose cleaning counter turns ordinary actions into extra healing. Ally turns build Dust Detection; five stacks let her own action trigger Pre-Arrival Cleanup. Her larger heal also cleanses and supplies team ATK Up, so she contributes to damage without building as an attacker.

This is Ceres (Sharp & Sweet), the healing variant, and her party ATK buff helps a carry without demanding damage gear on Ceres herself. Other allies’ turns build Dust Detection; she spends five stacks through one of her own actions for an automatic extra Cleanup. Prioritize HP and speed so she can turn that resource into recovery. The catch is timing: no Barrier or damage sharing protects a teammate before her healing arrives.
halloween-beamsword.watch: Her automatic cleanse is conditional on the extra Cleanup occurring during her turn. A normal Pre-Arrival Cleanup is not the same cleanse. Repeated healing does not prevent a lethal opening hit, and her listed 101 maximum SPD needs help if she must act early.
halloween-beamsword.dependency_note: Ally turns accelerate Dust Detection, while enemy area attacks advance her next turn. She does not need a specific attribute partner; she needs allies who survive long enough to take turns.

skill_order.name: Maid's Special
skill_order.why: Prioritize the level-6 cooldown reduction on the party heal, cleanse and ATK buff.

skill_order.name: Pre-Arrival Cleanup
skill_order.why: Then take its level-6 cooldown reduction and healing upgrades; it is also the skill used by the automatic extra activation.

skill_order.name: Service with Heart
skill_order.why: Improve HP and the response to area damage when the passive upgrade is available.

skill_order.name: Dust Buster
skill_order.why: Damage-only upgrades are a late expense on an HP healer.

rotation: Use Maid's Special before allied damage turns when healing or cleansing is useful; save it if an imminent enemy debuff wave matters more than the ATK buff.
Use Pre-Arrival Cleanup for ongoing group damage. Check Dust Detection before Ceres acts: at five stacks, even Dust Buster can be followed automatically by the extra Cleanup.
When the extra Cleanup is ready, check Ignition for the stronger heal; do not delay an emergency heal merely to reach maximum stacks.

best_partners.why: Emily's targeted Barrier buys time for healing, while her own extra turn provides another ally-turn opportunity for Dust Detection.
Carnelia supplies damage and turn denial; Ceres can heal her after Spoke's once-per-battle lethal-damage survival.
Dana buffs herself and another attacker, while Ceres supplies healing and cleansing that Dana lacks.
Bell's defeat-triggered turn progress helps her keep acting; Ceres protects that damage-and-control slot rather than competing with it.

halloween-beamsword.build_tip: HP improves both active heals; add SPD so her own actions can cash in Dust Detection, then DEF and resistance for survival. Damage stats do little for her core job. Maid for Hardship is the Vitality fit for this healer. An Unseen Place boosts Focus, useful to the control variant but not a substitute for HP training here.
halloween-beamsword.tier_reason: Her healing, team ATK buff and conditional repeatable cleanses fit strong support value in both modes. Longer fights and survivable area damage support her cleaning engine; a lethal opening or heavy stacked debuffs still demand protection or another cleanser.
halloween-beamsword.investment: Start with the two level-6 healing-skill cooldown upgrades, then healing strength and passive HP. The potentials arrays are empty; no unique-potential unlock can be recommended from these files. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
halloween-beamsword.pve_note: Best suited to repeated damage and debuff waves. She cleanses one debuff at a time on the direct party heal and on qualifying extra Cleanup activations, so stacked dangerous debuffs can still require another answer.
halloween-beamsword.pvp_note: Area attacks can accelerate her next heal, but only after she survives the hit. Build enough bulk and speed to act; neither her cleansing nor Refreshing Mood grants debuff immunity.

kit_explanation.name: Dust Buster
kit_explanation.explanation: Dust Buster is the no-cooldown single-target attack and adds one Ignition stack. Its ordinary upgrades improve damage, not healing. Nova adds one Toughness damage; use it only when breaking matters more than spending Nova on support.

kit_explanation.name: Pre-Arrival Cleanup
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 4 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Pre-Arrival Cleanup heals everyone from Ceres's maximum HP and gives Refreshing Mood, a stacking start-of-turn heal. It adds Ignition when cast normally. An additional activation during her turn also removes one debuff per ally; at maximum Ignition that extra activation gets stronger healing and spends Ignition. Do not assume a manual cast includes those conditional benefits.

kit_explanation.name: Maid's Special
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Maid's Special heals the whole party, removes one debuff from each ally, and gives two turns of ATK Up. It also adds Dust Detection and Ignition. This is the direct response to widespread injury or debuffs; its Nova extends ATK Up and restores Ceres's Toughness.

kit_explanation.name: Service with Heart
kit_explanation.explanation: Service with Heart automatically adds Dust Detection after her own skills and at other allies' turn starts. Debuffed ally turn starts add Ignition; being hit by an area attack adds Ignition and advances her next turn by 18%, rising to 30% at the highest listed level. At five Dust Detection stacks her own skill triggers an extra Cleanup and spends five stacks; that extra activation does not itself generate the usual two resources. Higher passive levels add up to 15% HP.

pros: Combines group healing, a direct cleanse and a party ATK buff in one slot.
Ally turn starts build the resource for extra healing without requiring their attacks.
Area damage advances her next turn, supporting recovery after a wave.
Refreshing Mood adds healing at the recipient’s next turn start.
cons: The extra Cleanup needs five Dust Detection stacks and one of her own actions.
The stronger extra heal spends maximum Ignition rather than staying permanently empowered.
No Barrier or party damage-sharing effect is listed to stop initial burst.

teams.name: Sustained cleanup (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily protects a chosen attacker, Dana shares ATK Up, and Carnelia handles damage and Buff Block while Ceres handles recovery.
teams.playstyle: Let Emily shield the vulnerable damage dealer; use Ceres's heals around incoming damage and avoid spending both ATK buffs only to refresh one another.

teams.name: Control with recovery (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell strips buffs and Silences, Kyra exploits Silence, and Haydee shares damage through Guard while Ceres restores the group.
teams.playstyle: Protect Haydee's HP after shared damage and use Ceres's direct cleanse when debuffs threaten the two damage dealers.

alternatives.why: Wedding Carmen is a higher-utility alternative for protecting one high-ATK carry: Oath shares damage and Guardian Knight reacts with healing, Barrier and next-turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not replace Ceres's team ATK buff or Dust Detection loop. Wedding March's ally wording conflicts with its Single Ally target field, so do not assume a party-wide full cleanse. The separate variant must be available and built; both have S+/S+ mode ratings.

alternatives.why: Waltz Asherah offers a stronger direct answer when every ally needs two debuffs removed in one action, plus healing and next-turn progress for other allies.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her published PvE S+ / PvP S ratings do not make her a universal upgrade over Ceres. She lacks Maid's Special's team ATK Up and the extra-Cleanup engine, and switching requires another build.

halloween-beamsword.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

halloween-rod.summary:
Lydia in the Moon maid variant is a linked damage dealer. She marks the highest-ATK other ally; that ally's turns and attacks build Clocking Out, which turns Lydia's single-target cooldown attacks into stronger area versions. Her strength depends on how reliably the marked ally feeds that five-stack window.

Choose Lydia (Ready-Made Puppy) alongside an area attacker who can reliably hold the highest-ATK mark. That ally generates Clocking Out during its own turns; five stacks let Lydia use a stronger area version of her special or ultimate. A basic can spend the same resource, so check cooldowns before attacking. Mounting Embarrassment gradually adds critical damage, but it cannot replace the marked ally’s actions. Control or defeat of that partner can leave Lydia waiting on an engine she cannot feed alone.
halloween-rod.watch: Passing the Buck chooses a teammate automatically, so check the actual highest-ATK ally. Her next attack spends five Clocking Out stacks once the threshold is met; a basic can consume the resource that you wanted for an area attack. The effect record for resource removal names an enemy target despite the passive describing self-consumption.
halloween-rod.dependency_note: Choose an attacking partner with high ATK and area attacks, and arrange for that partner to act before Lydia when possible. Do not assume every teammate is marked or that off-turn attacks qualify: the passive specifies the marked ally's own turn.

skill_order.name: Not My Fault!
skill_order.why: Take cooldown reductions at levels 4 and 8 so the stronger transformed ultimate is available more often.

skill_order.name: All This Work?!
skill_order.why: Improve the shorter-cooldown transformed area attack's damage next.

skill_order.name: Down to Business
skill_order.why: Raise the passive's ATK and turn-progress bonus as available.

skill_order.name: Shoo!
skill_order.why: Basic damage is filler; Nova's Embarrassment gain can help but does not replace the marked ally.

rotation: Before battle, make the intended area attacker the highest-ATK other ally; verify rather than assuming the mark follows a preferred slot.
After that ally has acted, check Clocking Out. At five stacks, choose Not My Fault! or All This Work?! on Lydia's turn for the area transformation.
Use Shoo! if the cooldown attacks are unavailable or a single-target finish is more urgent. Do not describe My Bad! or I've Had Enough! as separately selectable skills.

best_partners.why: Carnelia's Dissonance Break hits every enemy and can feed Clocking Out if she receives the highest-ATK mark.
Bell's Condolence hits all enemies and her SPD Up and defeat-triggered turn progress can produce more marked-ally turns.
Emily's targeted Barrier protects Lydia or the marked carry; Turn-Down Service is also an area attack if Emily happens to receive the mark.
Frey provides Barriers and a full single-target cleanse to keep the marked attacker functioning.

halloween-rod.build_tip: ATK and reliable CRIT Rate before extra CRIT DMG, since Embarrassment already builds CRIT DMG. Add SPD in relation to the marked ally's turn order and enough HP to survive area damage. You Call This an Outfit?! supports Strength and improves Sensory Training chance after 50 Bond. A Satisfying Bloom trains Focus rather than her main attack stat.
halloween-rod.tier_reason: The stronger PvP placement fits linked burst and transformed area attacks when the marked carry can act. PvE waves also feed Clocking Out efficiently, while lone bosses give fewer stacks per marked attack. Both ratings assume a functional marked-ally plan, not a self-sufficient solo attacker.
halloween-rod.investment: Prioritize Not My Fault!'s two cooldown upgrades, then area damage and passive levels. Touch of the Void, if actually obtained, supplies 20% CRIT Rate and stacking ATK from targets critically hit; account for it before buying excess CRIT Rate. Its unlock threshold is not established here. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement.
halloween-rod.pve_note: Multiple enemies let the marked ally build the transformation resource faster. Against one boss, value repeated marked turns and keep an eye on whether Lydia must attack before the five-stack window.
halloween-rod.pvp_note: An ally turn into an empowered area hit is a plausible pressure sequence, not a proven opener. Control on the marked ally or Lydia can interrupt it; she brings no listed cleanse or protection herself.

kit_explanation.name: Shoo!
kit_explanation.explanation: Shoo! attacks one enemy and adds Chill. Nova adds Toughness damage, a damage bonus and two Mounting Embarrassment stacks. At five Clocking Out it can also consume the passive resource, so inspect her cooldown attacks first.

kit_explanation.name: All This Work?!
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 3 turns. All This Work?! normally attacks one enemy and adds two Mounting Embarrassment stacks. During her own turn with at least five Clocking Out stacks, it becomes I've Had Enough!, an area attack with a 100% damage-dealt increase and four Embarrassment stacks. Those stacks increase CRIT DMG; the special's upgrade track is damage-only.

kit_explanation.name: Not My Fault!
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Not My Fault! normally hits one target and adds three Mounting Embarrassment stacks. With five Clocking Out on her own turn, it becomes My Bad!, a boosted area attack that grants six Embarrassment stacks. Levels 4 and 8 shorten its long cooldown, improving access to the transformed attack.

kit_explanation.name: Down to Business
kit_explanation.explanation: Down to Business marks the highest-ATK other ally at the first battle start with Passing the Buck, whose effect lists ATK and CRIT DMG bonuses. That ally gains Lydia two Clocking Out stacks on turn start and one per target attacked during its own turn, capped at five per attack. At five stacks its attack also advances Lydia's next turn once per turn, from 20% to 30% across passive levels. Lydia gets damage bonuses from Chill and from having five Clocking Out, then spends five Clocking Out after attacking. Higher levels add ATK; Mounting Embarrassment separately accumulates CRIT DMG up to 30 stacks.

pros: An appropriately marked area attacker can quickly enable the stronger area forms.
Embarrassment adds lasting damage growth through stacking CRIT DMG.
Passing the Buck also improves the chosen ally's offensive stats.
The marked ally reaching five Clocking Out advances Lydia by 30% Action gauge.
cons: Highest-ATK targeting can mark the wrong teammate after build changes.
Empowered attacks depend on five resource stacks and available cooldowns.
Single-target encounters and control on the marked ally slow the linked engine.

teams.name: Marked area carry (theorycraft)
teams.why: Carnelia is the intended marked attacker; Emily and Frey supply protection and recovery for the linked pair.
teams.playstyle: Verify Carnelia wins the other-ally ATK check, then follow her area attack with Lydia's available transformed skill.

teams.name: Defeat momentum (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell offers area attacks and defeat-based turn progress; Ceres heals while Emily protects the selected carry.
teams.playstyle: Make Bell the marked ally if using this plan. Treat defeat-based acceleration as a bonus rather than assuming an early kill.

alternatives.why: Carnelia has higher published ratings in both modes and supplies immediate area damage, Buff Block and enemy turn delay without needing a marked teammate.
alternatives.tradeoff: She lacks Lydia's ally ATK/CRIT DMG mark and transformed-skill loop. A separate build costs resources, so this is a role comparison rather than a requirement to replace an invested Lydia.

alternatives.why: Dana offers straightforward area damage and a targeted-by-ATK ally buff.
alternatives.tradeoff: Dana uses a different Star-ally resource engine and does not replicate Lydia's transformed attacks.

halloween-rod.research_note: Public character build reviewed; some slot details require paid access; these priorities follow the verified kit.

dark-unknown.summary:
Dark Asherah is a break-focused Order attacker, distinct from her Voyager damage and Dress healing variants. Lucula Noctis supplies Shatter; Phantom Sever then gains substantial Toughness pressure, especially against bosses. Attacking already broken targets resets Phantom Sever and builds Witch's Stigma.

Build the team around an actual breakable boss, then establish Shatter before the special’s Toughness burst. The own-turn break can award an extra turn only once every two turns, so this is a timed window rather than a permanent loop. ATK strengthens both normal attacks and fixed chain damage; critical stats affect the ordinary attacks. Gille amplifies the same Shatter plan, while sustain keeps it running.
dark-unknown.watch: The boss chain-damage bonus requires a target in Toughness Break, and the extra turn requires her own break on her own turn with a two-turn limit. Neither benefit is unconditional damage or an endless turn loop.
dark-unknown.dependency_note: She supplies her own Shatter, but the team must create and exploit break windows while keeping her alive. Gille directly supports her Shatter state; a defender/healer covers periods without Insight protection.

skill_order.name: Lucula Noctis
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves Shatter access; levels 4 and 8 increase next-turn progress from 5% to 10% to 15%.

skill_order.name: Phantom Sever
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves ordinary cooldown and levels 4/8 improve turn progress; the attack is central to Shatter boss breaking.

skill_order.name: Fatal Blow
skill_order.why: Basic damage is later; its Insight and Nova Toughness pressure can still be tactically useful.

rotation: Use Lucula Noctis to establish three-turn Shatter before spending Phantom Sever when its boss Toughness bonus matters.
Under Shatter, choose Phantom Sever to remove a meaningful amount of boss Toughness. If her own-turn hit secures the break and the passive limit allows it, she gains an extra turn automatically.
Attack the broken target on her own turn to reset Phantom Sever, gain Witch's Stigma and apply conditional chain damage. Recheck the break state before expecting another reset.
Use Fatal Blow for Insight and Nova break pressure when appropriate. Incoming attacks consume Insight for damage reduction, so the stack count can change before her next action.

best_partners.why: Gille's ultimate gives Overture and turn progress to Shatter holders; Dark Asherah supplies that state herself, then creates breaks for Gille's follow-up.
Emily's barrier/ATK Up protects a break carry and boosts ATK-based chain damage without needing Dark Asherah to sacrifice offense.
Dress Asherah heals, cleanses and advances allies, preserving Dark Asherah through repeated boss attacks; they are different slugs with different roles.

dark-unknown.build_tip: Build ATK for direct and fixed chain damage, then CRIT Rate/CRIT DMG for attacks and SPD for break windows. Add durability if she runs out of Insight under focused damage; fixed chain damage should not be assumed to scale like a normal critical hit. Journey option: Faded Dream is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
dark-unknown.tier_reason: The stored PvE NEW / PvP NEW status is provisional. Her explicit boss break bonuses suggest a strong conditional PvE role; short PvP fights, unbreakable targets or disrupted setup do not establish the same value. No settled tier is inferred from maximum multipliers.
dark-unknown.investment: Prioritize the level-6 cooldown milestones and level-8 turn-progress improvements on the two area attacks. Ruthless Favoritism's broken-target chain scales from 20% to 30% ATK, or 120% to 180% against a boss, across passive levels; these are conditional upgraded descriptions. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +2 SPD; it is not part of the starting stat line.
dark-unknown.pve_note: Check whether the boss can break before committing the slot. Under Shatter, Phantom Sever explicitly adds two Toughness damage plus three more against bosses, and broken-boss hits have a larger chain coefficient; those conditions explain the specialization.
dark-unknown.pvp_note: She brings area damage and conditional extra turns but no native hard control or team recovery. Do not treat Insight's 30% damage reduction as permanent: each qualifying incoming attack spends a stack.

kit_explanation.name: Fatal Blow
kit_explanation.explanation: Fatal Blow hits one enemy and gives one Insight. Insight modestly improves damage against Chaos enemies and also serves as her defensive resource. Nova adds two fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Phantom Sever
kit_explanation.explanation: Phantom Sever attacks all enemies on a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It grants ATK Up, Insight and 5–15% next-turn progress by skill level. With Shatter already active, it deals two additional Toughness damage and three more against a boss. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Lucula Noctis
kit_explanation.explanation: Lucula Noctis attacks all enemies on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It grants three-turn Shatter, two Insight and 5–15% next-turn progress through levels 1/4/8. Shatter raises ATK and adds fixed Toughness damage to later attacks; Nova adds fixed Toughness damage to this attack.

kit_explanation.name: Ruthless Favoritism
kit_explanation.explanation: Ruthless Favoritism automatically rewards own-turn attacks into broken targets with a Phantom Sever reset, Witch's Stigma and fixed chain damage. Stigma adds ATK and SPD, capped at five stacks. The chain coefficient is much higher against broken bosses and rises with passive level. Incoming attacks consume Insight to reduce damage by 30%. Her own-turn break grants an extra turn at most once every two turns.

pros: Explicit extra boss Toughness pressure under her own Shatter.
Broken-target attacks can reset the main special rather than waiting its full cooldown.
Insight offers conditional damage reduction while Stigma rewards successful break windows.
Her basic Nova adds two fixed Toughness damage.
cons: Much of her damage engine disappears if the target cannot break.
The extra turn has an own-turn break requirement and a two-turn limit.
Insight is consumed by attacks and she has no healing or cleanse.

teams.name: Orchestrated boss break
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Dark Asherah supplies Shatter for Gille's Overture, Emily protects the carry and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Establish Shatter before Gille's ultimate, then use Phantom Sever to create a broken-target window.

teams.name: Break and focused pursuit
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Hilde gives opening protection, Professor M adds forced basics and a special-skill vulnerability mark, and Dress Asherah sustains.
teams.playstyle: Set Dark Asherah as highest ATK if she should receive dual attacks; do not assume the mark can land on every boss.

alternatives.why: Lyn is an established rated PvE alternative for mixed wave/focused damage without needing a boss to be broken for her central stance payoff.
alternatives.tradeoff: Dark Asherah retains explicit broken-boss chain damage, special resets and Shatter-based boss Toughness pressure.

alternatives.why: Rosaria supplies immediate area DEF Down and 50% next-turn progress, useful when rapid broad pressure matters more than break specialization.
alternatives.tradeoff: Dark Asherah offers more explicit boss-break mechanics; her provisional rating is not evidence that Rosaria universally outdamages her.

dark-unknown.research_note: community’s new November 11 build was reviewed. Its settled rating differs from the local provisional snapshot; no equal-investment combat test validates the ranking here.

west-lancer.summary:
Besta is a straightforward HP-based defender. Her ordinary kit weakens one enemy's ATK and increases her own DEF, so she is easier to keep alive than her allies. Blossom changes her role substantially by adding ally barriers, team DEF Up and a conditional response to area attacks.

Base Besta is a temporary durability pick, not a complete party protector. Time her one-turn ATK Down before the threatening attack, and let a real healer cover allies. HP and DEF suit her role; offensive investment does not add missing redirection. Evaluate the separately stored Blossom kit on its own merits before spending, because its barriers and reactions change the recommendation substantially.
west-lancer.watch: The base kit has no Taunt, ally healing or damage sharing. A defender label alone does not force enemies to attack her, and Blossom benefits must not be treated as ordinary SR abilities.
west-lancer.dependency_note: Bring an actual healer and damage dealers. A Star healer such as original Frey can support her, but simply stacking Star allies does not create protection that her base kit lacks.

skill_order.name: Repel
skill_order.why: Its level-4/8 cooldown reductions improve access to ATK Down; with Blossom it also becomes an ally-protection tool.

skill_order.name: Unstoppable Charge
skill_order.why: Take the cooldown reductions before small damage upgrades. Base DEF Up is personal; Blossom changes it to a team buff.

skill_order.name: Faint Emotions
skill_order.why: HP helps every version survive. Blossom's reactive Repel chance also improves with available passive levels.

skill_order.name: Steadfast Lance
skill_order.why: Basic damage is the last priority when resources are limited; it is not the missing source of team protection.

rotation: Use Repel on the dangerous attacker before its damage turn if ATK Down can affect it. The base version lasts only one turn, so timing matters more than using it immediately whenever available.

Use Unstoppable Charge before Besta takes heavy damage for her personal DEF Up. With Blossom it protects the whole party and adds a personal Barrier; do not wait below half HP merely to enlarge that shield.
Use Steadfast Lance between cooldowns. In the Blossom version, watch Leap: taking a hit at maximum stacks creates a Barrier automatically, while incoming area attacks can trigger Repel once per turn.

If teammates are dying while Besta survives, change the protection slot rather than building more personal HP. A healer can cover damage already taken; a better protector can stop more of it reaching the carry.

best_partners.why: Original Frey heals and cleanses allies Besta cannot heal, and her recovery skills have extra benefit for Star targets.
Tanya supplies actual Toughness pressure and team critical support while Besta handles limited defensive duties.

Against area attackers, Roberta's automatic response supplies damage while a Blossom Besta can also respond with Repel. Neither trigger should be assumed to activate on ordinary single-target attacks.

west-lancer.build_tip: Build HP, DEF and enough SPD to place ATK Down before the threat acts; add Effect Hit if landing that debuff is essential. Her damage scales partly with HP, but that does not make offensive investment a substitute for team protection. Journey option: Forbidden Archive Vol. 1 is Vitality-tagged, supporting HP for recovery or HP scaling; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
west-lancer.tier_reason: Published base ratings of PvE C+ and PvP C are reasonable for a defender whose main support is a short single-target ATK reduction. Blossom adds important protection, but that is a separate upgrade and has no independently verified rating in this guide.
west-lancer.investment: Prioritize functional cooldown reductions over damage-only steps. Compare the cost of Blossom with building an available stronger defender; the upgrade is meaningful, but not a proven best investment. Base Faint Emotions rises from 3% to 12% HP. No exact copy requirement or unique potential is established by this profile. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 6 at level 120, listing +8 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
west-lancer.pve_note: A workable early defensive slot when one attacker can be weakened and the party has separate healing. Her limited base protection becomes more noticeable against widespread damage; Blossom's barriers and team defense improve that job.
west-lancer.pvp_note: Do not expect the base kit to intercept damage aimed at a carry. Blossom can answer area pressure, but its extra Repel remains a chance-based response, and she still lacks a listed Taunt.

kit_explanation.name: Steadfast Lance
kit_explanation.explanation: A single-target basic attack adds one Leap stack and deals damage using both ATK and maximum HP. Leap adds a small damage bonus against Moon enemies. Blossom keeps the ordinary attack similar, while its Nova version also attempts a one-turn ATK Down.

kit_explanation.name: Repel
kit_explanation.explanation: The base skill hits one enemy and attempts to lower its ATK by 30% for one turn. Its listed five-turn cooldown can be reduced at levels 4 and 8. Blossom extends ATK Down to two turns, advances Besta's next turn by 30%, shields the ally with the lowest HP percentage, and adds Leap. The ally shield is a Blossom benefit.

kit_explanation.name: Unstoppable Charge
kit_explanation.explanation: The base ultimate is a single-target hit that gives Besta two turns of DEF Up; damage uses her maximum HP as well as ATK. Its listed six-turn cooldown has two upgrade reductions. Blossom grants DEF Up to everyone and also shields Besta, making her personal Barrier larger below half HP. The ordinary skill does not give the whole team that buff.

kit_explanation.name: Faint Emotions
kit_explanation.explanation: The ordinary passive only increases maximum HP, up to 12% at its highest stored level. Blossom replaces that simple passive: a hit received at maximum Leap spends the stacks for a Barrier, and an incoming area attack can trigger Repel on a random enemy once per turn. The chance reaches 40% at the highest stored Blossom passive level, so it is never a guaranteed response.

pros: HP investment supports both survival and her damage scaling.
Repel can weaken one dangerous attacker without a critical-hit requirement.
Blossom adds real ally protection and a response to area pressure.
The base ultimate can extend personal DEF Up through Nova.
cons: The ordinary kit mostly protects Besta herself.
Base ATK Down lasts only one turn and does not bypass resistance or immunity.
No listed Taunt or ally healing; Blossom reactions also depend on stacks or chance.

teams.name: Early progression with separate healing
teams.why: Frey covers party healing and cleanse, Luna handles groups, and Tanya adds Toughness pressure. Besta weakens the main attacker rather than pretending to supply a full defensive kit.
teams.playstyle: Aim Repel at the biggest incoming threat, use Frey's healing for the party, and focus Tanya on a target she can break. Replace Besta if teammates keep falling despite her own survival.

teams.name: Blossom response to area attacks
teams.why: This version assumes Blossom Besta. Her barriers and team DEF help Roberta and Bell stay active, Roberta answers incoming area attacks, and Waltz Asherah heals and cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use the team DEF buff before expected damage. Let Roberta's response and Besta's chance-based extra Repel occur automatically; do not spend turns trying to cast those triggered attacks.

alternatives.why: Emily is a stronger general protection choice when your carry needs an ally Barrier and you want damage taken to recycle a team-defense ultimate.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not replace Besta's targeted ATK Down, and the better result still depends on the available upgrades and incoming attack pattern.

alternatives.why: Summer Luna is more directly suited to critical-hit pressure, with team defense, Taunt and a reactive attack that can apply DEF Down.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her response depends on allies receiving critical hits. She is a different specialist rather than a reason to discard an already-built Besta in every encounter.

west-lancer.research_note: No ordinary-version build was published in the reviewed build index. Blossom or Bunnygirl recommendations are different kits; this ordinary-version advice is kit-based. The community page reviewed covers Stellar Sigil Blooming, so its Arcana list does not establish ordinary-version combat performance.

officer-police.summary:
Annah is a self-sustaining defender who weakens one attacker rather than forcing enemies to hit her. Her base kit heals only herself; Blossom adds team DEF support, a personal shield and conditional counterattacks.

Base Annah is useful only if her own survival and one enemy’s ATK Down are what the lineup needs. Her two self-heals cannot rescue an exposed attacker, so retain party recovery and protection elsewhere. Build HP, DEF and timely speed before damage. Blossom adds a different defensive package, but a counter window still needs setup and does not force the opponent to attack her.
officer-police.watch: Do not read the Blossom team buffs into her base kit. Neither version lists a taunt, and the Blossom basic pushes a random teammate rather than your chosen carry.
officer-police.dependency_note: She needs an actual damage dealer and someone who heals or protects the other three allies; her personal recovery cannot cover them.

skill_order.name: Quick Bite Before We Start!
skill_order.why: Prioritize the level-4 and level-8 cooldown reductions so her self-heal is available more often.

skill_order.name: Arrest Them All!
skill_order.why: Improve conditional recovery and damage after securing the heal cycle; Blossom also makes this a team DEF button.

skill_order.name: Something Smells Delicious!
skill_order.why: HP growth supports survival; the Blossom passive is a different, conditional support/counter kit.

skill_order.name: Please Stop Resisting!
skill_order.why: Basic damage is secondary to surviving and reducing enemy pressure.

rotation: Use Arrest Them All! on the dangerous attacker before its next damaging turn when ATK Down can land; do not hold it solely for the below-half-HP heal.
Use Quick Bite Before We Start! when injured or needing its SPD buff; the base Nova Burst restores Toughness and advances her next turn, while Blossom Nova grants an extra turn.

Fill with Please Stop Resisting!. With Blossom, watch Ignition before attacking: reaching five stacks after attacking consumes them for a one-turn counter window; this is automatic, not a skill to cast.

best_partners.why: Rapid Resupply cleanses and heals a teammate Annah cannot heal.
Annah can reduce the main attacker’s ATK while Luna supplies the area damage missing from her kit.
Lydia slows enemy turns and applies Unknown Hex; Annah supplies personal staying power while Lydia sets up.

officer-police.build_tip: HP and DEF first, then enough SPD to refresh recovery. Effect Hit is useful only if ATK Down matters in the encounter; ATK is a low priority for this role. Journey option: Undercover Cop is Endurance-tagged, supporting DEF for personal durability; its listed training effectiveness is +8% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
officer-police.tier_reason: The low base-kit ratings fit a narrow self-sustaining role: keeping Annah alive does not protect the rest of the team. PvE can give her time to use recovery, whereas PvP enemies can attack around her because she has no listed taunt. The separately stored Blossom kit adds utility, but these published ratings do not establish a separate Blossom rating.
officer-police.investment: Raise Quick Bite Before We Start! to its documented cooldown upgrades before spending on basic damage. Compare the separate Blossom kit before committing its resources. Her potential arrays are empty, so no unique-potential spike is supported. All quoted upper effects require the corresponding skill/passive level; stored maximum stats are not equal-investment combat results or a zero-star promise. The local star rows do not establish a combat unlock threshold. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 6 at level 120, listing +8 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
officer-police.pve_note: Useful as a temporary durable slot against a single ATK-based threat. She does not solve area damage, party healing or boss mechanics on her own.
officer-police.pvp_note: ATK Down can soften one damage dealer if it lands. Focus fire can simply bypass her; random Blossom gauge support cannot be planned as a fixed opener.

kit_explanation.name: Please Stop Resisting!
kit_explanation.explanation: Please Stop Resisting! is a single-target basic that adds one Ignition stack. Ignition is a small damage bonus against Star enemies, capped at five, not a general damage multiplier against everyone.

kit_explanation.name: Quick Bite Before We Start!
kit_explanation.explanation: Quick Bite Before We Start! heals Annah using her own maximum HP and grants SPD Up for two turns. Its listed five-turn cooldown has reductions at levels 4 and 8. Blossom changes the buff to three turns and adds a personal HP-based Barrier.

kit_explanation.name: Arrest Them All!
kit_explanation.explanation: Arrest Them All! is a single-target attack with a listed five-turn cooldown, two Toughness damage and a two-turn ATK Down application. It also heals Annah if she is at or below half HP after attacking. Blossom adds two-turn team DEF Up and three Ignition stacks.

kit_explanation.name: Something Smells Delicious!
kit_explanation.explanation: Something Smells Delicious! is passive: base levels raise maximum HP from 3% to 12%. Blossom instead adds a random other ally’s progress toward its next turn after her basic, Ignition from incoming single-target hits, and a five-stack conversion into Enhanced Counterattack after attacking. These effects are not manual actions.

pros: Two separate self-recovery tools reduce her dependence on emergency healing.
ATK Down can reduce one attacker’s pressure for two turns.
Blossom adds meaningful team DEF Up instead of only personal durability.
Her base special adds two-turn personal SPD Up alongside recovery.
cons: No listed taunt or base damage-sharing effect directs attacks away from teammates.
Base recovery does not heal allies.
Blossom gauge gain is random and its counter window requires stack setup.

teams.name: Early defensive shell
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Frey handles party sustain, Lydia slows the threat and Luna clears groups while Annah uses ATK Down.
teams.playstyle: Debuff the dangerous attacker, use Luna’s area attacks, and reserve Frey’s cleanse for actual debuffs.

teams.name: Blossom attrition option
teams.why: Theorycraft, not a tested lineup: Elisa supplies rescue and revival, Ceres disrupts turns, and Asherah supplies area damage while Blossom Annah adds DEF Up.
teams.playstyle: Use the Blossom team buff before incoming damage; do not expect Annah to hold enemy targeting.

alternatives.why: Summer Luna is higher-rated in both modes and protects more directly through team DEF Up, Taunt and opening anti-critical support.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her reactive DEF Down depends on allies taking critical hits and she lacks Annah’s direct self-heal button.

alternatives.why: Blossom Besta supplies an ally Barrier and team DEF Up if those are the missing tools.
alternatives.tradeoff: Base Besta is also narrow; her improved ally protection requires the separate Blossom kit.

officer-police.research_note: The reviewed community index has no published ordinary-version build. Blossom and Bunnygirl builds must not be applied to this ordinary kit. The community page reviewed covers Stellar Sigil Blooming, so its Arcana list does not establish ordinary-version combat performance.

construct-wrench.summary:
Marcille is a single-target Sun attacker with Burn, a self ATK buff and healing reduction. Her ordinary kit is simple and crit-dependent; her separate Blossom kit adds a much more involved Fractured Nut/Hex Nut cycle. Do not judge the ordinary version as if those Blossom effects are already active.

For the ordinary kit, prioritize reliable critical hits before expecting speed or anti-heal. Nail Drive’s Burn lasts one turn, so apply it where the enemy’s next action makes that duration meaningful. ATK serves both attacks and Burn, while protection covers her fragility. The separate Blossom resource loop is a different investment decision; its stronger cycling does not describe an unupgraded copy.
construct-wrench.watch: Ordinary Nail Drive only burns for one turn and requires a crit for SPD Up; ordinary Screw Breaker requires a crit for one-turn Recovery Down. Blossom improves both and adds turn progress, but those are separate upgrades, not ordinary skill-level benefits.
construct-wrench.dependency_note: The ordinary version supplies her own basic buffs but benefits from early crit support and healing. Blossom additionally wants regular cooldown attacks and safe access to broken targets for Hex Nut damage.

skill_order.name: Nail Drive
skill_order.why: Reach ordinary levels 4 and 8 for cooldown reductions on Burn access; Blossom uses the same milestones but has a stronger crit/turn-progress payoff.

skill_order.name: Screw Breaker
skill_order.why: Levels 4 and 8 reduce the long cooldown; ordinary use offers ATK Up and crit-conditioned anti-heal.

skill_order.name: Nut Twist
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later purchase; it adds Ignition but does not independently produce the Blossom resource.

rotation: For ordinary Marcille, use Screw Breaker to establish ATK Up, then Nail Drive to apply Burn and attempt the crit-based SPD buff when ready.
If enemy healing is imminent, use Screw Breaker for Recovery Down only with a realistic crit chance; ordinary Nova Nail Drive is a separate anti-heal option.
Use Nut Twist between cooldowns. The ordinary passive is a crit-rate stat increase, not a hidden follow-up or turn-progress engine.

For Blossom only: use cooldown attacks to build Fractured Nut, check the three-stack start-of-turn conversion into Hex Nut, and spend Hex Nut on a useful hit, ideally into Toughness Break. Blossom Nova Nail Drive additionally shortens its cooldown by two turns.

best_partners.why: Song of the Toast raises Marcille's ATK; Marcille's Sun turns feed Charlotte's Ignition, giving a reciprocal reason to pair them.
All In supplies CRIT Rate Up to help ordinary Marcille meet her speed/anti-heal crit conditions; Frey is a damage supporter here, not the healer.
Marcille's Burn can feed Serpang's upgraded Burn-enemy-turn passive; he heals Sun allies and lowers enemy Effect RES for debuffs.

construct-wrench.build_tip: Prioritize reliable CRIT Rate and ATK, then SPD and CRIT DMG. Add enough Effect Hit if Burn/anti-heal are the job. Her ordinary stored ATK/HP are lower than several SSR attackers, but these maxima are not equal-investment damage comparisons. Journey option: The Indomitable Masterpiece is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
