construct-wrench.tier_reason: The stored PvE C+ / PvP C ratings fit an ordinary kit with narrow single-target utility, crit conditions and long initial cooldowns. Blossom improves cycling and break payoff, but should be evaluated separately rather than silently raising ordinary-tier expectations.
construct-wrench.investment: Ordinary Nail Drive and Screw Breaker each have cooldown reductions at levels 4 and 8. Ordinary Hammer and Anvil describes CRIT Rate increasing from 3% to 12%, despite upgrade labels saying CRIT DMG; use the description cautiously. No potentials are listed. Blossom is a distinct skill set with its own level progression and resource costs; no exact star requirement is established. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 2 at level 40, listing +3 CRIT Rate; it is not part of the starting stat line.
construct-wrench.pve_note: Ordinary Marcille can supply Burn and limited anti-heal to a focused fight. Blossom rewards crits and broken targets more substantially, but do not deliberately let an ally break merely to generate nuts if that endangers the run.
construct-wrench.pvp_note: One-turn ordinary anti-heal and crit-gated speed are fragile under turn disruption. Bunny Scarlet offers broader anti-heal/strip utility, while stronger focused damage options may use the slot more efficiently unless Marcille's Burn is specifically useful.

kit_explanation.name: Nut Twist
kit_explanation.explanation: Nut Twist is a single-target basic that grants one Ignition; Nova adds fixed Toughness damage. This core behavior is also present in Blossom and is not a Hex Nut generator by itself.

kit_explanation.name: Nail Drive
kit_explanation.explanation: Ordinary Nail Drive has a listed five-turn cooldown, reduced at levels 4 and 8. It attempts one-turn Burn and grants one-turn SPD Up on a crit; its Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and one-turn Recovery Down. Blossom Nail Drive instead supplies two-turn Burn and SPD Up, adds 30% next-turn progress on a crit and builds Fractured Nut. Blossom Nova shortens Nail Drive's cooldown by two, rather than promising the ordinary Nova anti-heal.

kit_explanation.name: Screw Breaker
kit_explanation.explanation: Ordinary Screw Breaker is a single-target six-turn-cooldown attack, reduced at levels 4 and 8. It grants two-turn ATK Up and attempts one-turn Recovery Down on a crit. Blossom instead attempts two-turn Recovery Down without the ordinary crit condition; its description adds 30% next-turn progress on a crit and a Fractured Nut stack. Both Nova versions add fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Hammer and Anvil
kit_explanation.explanation: Ordinary Hammer and Anvil increases CRIT Rate from 3% to 12% through four passive levels; it does not grant nuts. Blossom grants two Fractured Nuts at the first battle start or when an ally's Toughness breaks, and converts three nuts at own-turn start into Hex Nut. Hex Nut adds 30% CRIT DMG and 15% damage against broken targets, then disappears after an attack. Blossom also adds 1–3% CRIT DMG per Ignition stack, with later passive CRIT Rate increases.

pros: Ordinary Burn and Recovery Down give some utility beyond direct damage.
Two cooldown-reduction milestones improve both main attacks.
Blossom adds a distinct crit/turn-progress loop and a broken-target payoff.
The ordinary ultimate supplies two-turn ATK Up for subsequent damage.
cons: Ordinary speed and anti-heal effects depend on crits and last only one turn.
No team heal, cleanse, barrier or area damage.
Blossom benefits require separate investment and cannot justify ordinary first-copy expectations.

teams.name: Sun Burn support
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Charlotte buffs ATK, Hilde provides opening barriers and Serpang heals. Marcille's Burn can also feed Serpang's upgraded passive.
teams.playstyle: Apply Burn to a target that will take turns; use anti-heal near enemy healing rather than wasting its brief ordinary duration.

teams.name: Crit-assisted Marcille
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Frey helps early crit conditions, Emily shields/buffs Marcille and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use Frey's crit buff before cooldown attacks; in Blossom, watch nuts and reserve Hex Nut for a meaningful damage window.

alternatives.why: Charlotte is a higher-rated Sun focused attacker with party ATK Up, DEF penetration and repeated basics.
alternatives.tradeoff: Marcille still supplies Burn and Recovery Down, which Charlotte does not.

alternatives.why: Bunny Scarlet adds area Recovery Down, a one-buff strip and an extra turn, providing broader healing disruption.
alternatives.tradeoff: Marcille keeps Burn and her separate Blossom crit/resource loop; Scarlet's pinball-based cooldown value is random.

construct-wrench.research_note: The reviewed community index has no published ordinary-version build. Blossom and Bunnygirl builds must not be applied to this ordinary kit. The community page reviewed covers Stellar Sigil Blooming, so its Arcana list does not establish ordinary-version combat performance.

lpu-post.summary:
Vera is a straightforward HP-scaling healer: one skill heals and removes one debuff from one ally, and her ultimate heals the party. Express Delivery adds random utility, but its recipient is inconsistent between the ultimate description and effect record, so it should not be the reason a team depends on her.

Keep her spending focused on reliable healing rather than the random package. The single-target skill removes one debuff, which can rescue a teammate without guaranteeing a clean status bar. HP supports both heals and speed helps them arrive before another enemy hit. Use a deliberate buffing ally such as Emily for offensive support, and treat Express Delivery as incidental until its conflicting recipient data is resolved.
lpu-post.watch: One Step Toward My Dream says Vera gains Express Delivery when the target has a buff; the effect record instead targets already-buffed allies. The random outcome is ATK Up, DEF Up, SPD Up or Continuous Recovery, not a selectable buff. Her passive only adds HP.
lpu-post.dependency_note: She benefits from a partner who already supplies buffs, but the Express Delivery recipient needs confirmation. Use her for healing if already invested, with protection and offensive support from teammates.

skill_order.name: Swift and Safe Delivery
skill_order.why: Take cooldown reductions at levels 4/8 if repeated single-target cleansing is why you use Vera.

skill_order.name: One Step Toward My Dream
skill_order.why: Use its levels 4/8 cooldown upgrades first instead if party damage is the main problem.

skill_order.name: Veteran Courier
skill_order.why: HP supports both heals, but there are no hidden utility effects to unlock in the listed passive.

skill_order.name: Proper Response
skill_order.why: Basic damage is the last use of resources for this healer.

rotation: Use Swift and Safe Delivery on the injured or debuffed ally whose next action matters most.
Use One Step Toward My Dream when multiple allies need healing. Existing allied buffs may qualify for Express Delivery, but do not delay an emergency heal chasing a random bonus.
Use Proper Response when recovery is unnecessary. Do not wait for maximum Chill expecting an unlisted team-heal trigger.

best_partners.why: Emily gives a targeted ATK buff and Barrier plus party DEF Up, covering Vera's lack of direct protection and providing existing buffs.
Dana buffs herself and the highest-ATK other ally and supplies area damage, giving useful buffs independently of Express Delivery.
Carnelia supplies area pressure and Buff Block, while Vera handles recovery after nonlethal damage.
Charlotte supplies deliberate CRIT Rate support and extra-turn offense, so the team need not rely on Vera rolling ATK Up.

lpu-post.build_tip: HP for both heals, then SPD to answer damage/debuffs and enough DEF/resistance to stay functional. Her listed maximum 37,187 HP should not be read as a measured heal comparison at equal investment. Journey option: More Than Professional is Vitality-tagged, supporting HP for recovery or HP scaling; its listed training effectiveness is +8% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
lpu-post.tier_reason: The C+ PvE / C PvP ratings fit a low-complexity healer with narrow cleansing and uncertain random support. She can cover basic sustain, but deterministic cleanse, protection and turn support make stronger healers more flexible.
lpu-post.investment: Invest only far enough to meet the healing requirement if a replacement is planned. Cooldown levels 4/8 on the heal you actually need are better first targets than basic damage. No unique potentials are listed; Express Delivery's data conflict remains unresolved. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 2 at level 40, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
lpu-post.pve_note: Suitable for simple incoming damage when one-debuff cleansing is enough. Repeated heavy debuff waves or the need for predictable mitigation favor a stronger support.
lpu-post.pvp_note: She lacks a listed Barrier or speed-control answer to an opening burst. Do not plan an opener around rolling SPD Up or receiving an uncertain Express Delivery target.

kit_explanation.name: Proper Response
kit_explanation.explanation: Proper Response is a basic single-target attack that adds Chill. There is no listed heal on the basic or resource-spending support loop. Nova only adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Swift and Safe Delivery
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Swift and Safe Delivery heals one ally from Vera's maximum HP and removes one debuff from that ally. Levels 4 and 8 each shorten cooldown. It is a limited cleanse, not removal of every debuff.

kit_explanation.name: One Step Toward My Dream
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. One Step Toward My Dream heals the whole party from Vera's maximum HP. Its description conditions Express Delivery on the target having a buff; the effect record says already-buffed allies receive one random buff. That buff can be ATK Up, DEF Up, SPD Up or Continuous Recovery. Do not promise the recipient or the outcome. Nova lists extra outgoing healing and restores Vera's Toughness, though its timing is worded ambiguously.

kit_explanation.name: Veteran Courier
kit_explanation.explanation: Veteran Courier increases maximum HP from 3% at level 1 to 12% at level 4. It adds no listed reaction, automatic cleanse or turn-progress tool.

pros: Simple direct one-target heal with a one-debuff cleanse.
Separate party heal covers damage spread across allies.
Both heals benefit from the same HP build.
The ordinary heal cooldowns each have two reduction milestones.
cons: Express Delivery's recipient conflicts across source fields.
Random buffs cannot replace a deliberate offensive or defensive tool.
No listed Barrier, party cleanse or action-gauge support.

teams.name: Protected recovery (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily supplies Barriers and DEF Up, Dana supplies ATK buffs and damage, and Carnelia handles disruption while Vera heals.
teams.playstyle: Use protection to prevent lethal hits first; let Vera heal actual damage rather than chasing Express Delivery.

teams.name: Deliberate buffs (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily protects Carnelia and Charlotte supplies intentional CRIT Rate support; Vera fills the recovery slot.
teams.playstyle: Buff the carry before its action and use Vera's direct cleanse when one debuff threatens it; treat the random buff as incidental.

alternatives.why: Maid Ceres is a higher-rated sustain option with direct party cleansing, repeatable conditional extra heals and a team ATK buff.
alternatives.tradeoff: She is a separate character build; her cleanse still removes a limited number of debuffs per activation rather than guaranteeing all are gone.

alternatives.why: Waltz Asherah adds two-debuff group cleansing and allied next-turn progress alongside healing.
alternatives.tradeoff: She lacks Vera's random buff pool, which is usually a predictability advantage; availability and existing investment may still favor keeping Vera temporarily.

lpu-post.research_note: The reviewed community index has no published ordinary-version build. Blossom and Bunnygirl builds must not be applied to this ordinary kit. The community page reviewed covers Stellar Sigil Blooming, so its Arcana list does not establish ordinary-version combat performance.

noa-observer.summary:
Naru is a single-target attacker with a simple debuff setup: Beyond Expectations! attempts SPD Down, then Behold My Skill! deals more damage to a debuffed enemy. The bonus accepts any debuff, so an ally can establish the condition without waiting for Naru's ultimate.

She works best behind an ally who already applies a useful debuff. That saves her long-cooldown ultimate from becoming mandatory setup for a 10% special bonus. ATK, critical consistency and speed support the damage slot, while Emily and a healer cover survival. Check the encounter’s immunity rules before investing heavily in Effect Hit for a slow the target cannot receive.
noa-observer.watch: Her passive only adds ATK, and her ordinary attacks provide no area damage, healing or protection. The special's bonus is 10%, not a reason to spend several turns setting up a weak target. Effect RES Down belongs to the ultimate's Nova version, not every cast.
noa-observer.dependency_note: She can apply SPD Down herself, but partners with reliable useful debuffs reduce setup dependence. A protector and healer cover her missing survival tools; an all-Star team is unnecessary unless it serves another kit.

skill_order.name: Beyond Expectations!
skill_order.why: If relying on her own debuff, get level-6 cooldown and levels 4/8 SPD Down chance.

skill_order.name: Behold My Skill!
skill_order.why: Then get cooldown levels 4/8 and damage on the debuffed-target attack; prioritize it sooner if allies already cover debuffs.

skill_order.name: Eyes on Me!
skill_order.why: Basic damage follows the two cooldown skills.

skill_order.name: Career Ambitions
skill_order.why: Passive ATK improves output but unlocks no extra control mechanic.

rotation: If the priority target already has a useful debuff from an ally, use Behold My Skill! without first spending the ultimate solely for setup.
Otherwise use Beyond Expectations! when SPD Down can actually help, then exploit a still-active debuff with the special on a later opportunity.
Use Eyes on Me! in gaps. Reserve the ultimate's Nova for a valuable Toughness or Effect RES Down application, and do not claim ordinary casts provide that resistance debuff.

best_partners.why: Bell supplies Silence or ACC Down for Naru's conditional special while removing buffs and handling area damage.
Naru's Star attacks feed Dana's unlocked Leap passive; Dana can buff Naru if she is the highest-ATK other ally.
Emily provides ATK Up and a Barrier to protect Naru's damage turns.
Ceres heals, cleanses and buffs ATK so Naru can spend actions attacking rather than recovering.

noa-observer.build_tip: ATK and critical consistency with enough SPD to exploit active debuffs. Add Effect Hit only when SPD Down is relevant, and keep enough survival to reach the next action. Her 6,319 listed maximum ATK is a database endpoint, not a measured outcome. Journey option: The Indomitable Masterpiece is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
noa-observer.tier_reason: The C+ PvE / D+ PvP ratings fit a limited single-target kit with a small debuffed-target bonus and one ordinary control effect. She can use an existing build in a debuff team, but stronger attackers add much broader utility.
noa-observer.investment: Take the special's cooldowns if allies establish debuffs; otherwise improve the ultimate's cooldown and chance first. No unique potentials are listed. Do not assume a future star milestone supplies area damage, turn manipulation or stronger support. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 10 at level 200, listing +12 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
noa-observer.pve_note: Useful only if her direct damage and SPD Down are sufficient for the fight. Immune bosses remove her self-setup route, although another valid debuff can still satisfy the special if the encounter permits one.
noa-observer.pvp_note: Her low published PvP rating is consistent with limited control and no defensive tools. An upgraded 100% SPD Down chance is not guaranteed application, and Nova-only Effect RES Down should not be advertised as her ordinary support role.

kit_explanation.name: Eyes on Me!
kit_explanation.explanation: Eyes on Me! hits one enemy and adds Leap. Nova adds Toughness damage. No full-Leap activation or special resource-spending mode is listed.

kit_explanation.name: Behold My Skill!
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Behold My Skill! hits one enemy, grants one turn of ATK Up and deals 10% more damage if that enemy has a debuff on attack. Levels 4 and 8 shorten cooldown. Any applicable debuff qualifies; Naru need not be the caster.

kit_explanation.name: Beyond Expectations!
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 5 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Beyond Expectations! hits one enemy and attempts two turns of SPD Down. Chance rises from 75% to 100% at levels 4/8, and level 6 shortens cooldown. Nova also attempts two turns of Effect RES Down and adds Toughness damage; ordinary casts do not reduce Effect RES.

kit_explanation.name: Career Ambitions
kit_explanation.explanation: Career Ambitions increases ATK from 3% to 12% across passive levels. It provides no listed reaction, team buff or next-turn progress.

pros: Any active enemy debuff can enable her special's damage bonus.
Can establish her own SPD Down when enemies are susceptible.
Nova ultimate adds an optional Effect RES Down application.
An ally’s debuff lets her begin with the special instead of setup.
cons: Only single-target damage and no party utility in the ordinary kit.
Passive adds ATK without an additional engine.
Limited debuff access and a small conditional damage bonus compared with stronger attackers.

teams.name: Star debuff support (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell supplies debuffs and dispel, Dana uses Naru's Star attacks for Leap and Ceres supplies recovery.
teams.playstyle: Attack a debuffed target with Behold My Skill! rather than duplicating setup; assess survivability because there is no dedicated Barrier protector.

teams.name: Protected target focus (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell establishes control, Emily shields Naru and Ceres heals, giving Naru a safe conditional single-target role.
teams.playstyle: Protect before incoming burst and choose a debuffed priority target; this lineup trades some damage slots for safety.

alternatives.why: Bell is higher-rated in both modes and offers area damage, Silence, buff removal and defeat-based turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: She may already be the debuff provider rather than a replacement slot; building her costs resources, and Naru's exact Nova Effect RES Down is not replicated.

alternatives.why: Cristelle is higher-rated and rewards a debuff team with chain damage, Burn extension and personal turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her reactive skill requires ally attacks and her best resource support comes from Sun attackers; replacing Naru can require changing the team rather than only one slot.

noa-observer.research_note: The reviewed community index has no published ordinary-version build. Blossom and Bunnygirl builds must not be applied to this ordinary kit. The community page reviewed covers Stellar Sigil Blooming, so its Arcana list does not establish ordinary-version combat performance.

maid-spear.summary:
Claire is a single-target attacker who gives herself brief SPD Up and gains progress toward her next turn from Final Service. That ultimate gains more progress if she already has a buff, so a real ally buff is useful rather than treating every attack as an identical rotation.

Give Claire a lasting allied buff before Final Service if you want its full 30% upgraded action progress. Emily supplies both that condition and a Barrier, solving two practical needs at once. Build ATK and critical consistency with enough speed to offset her slow starting profile. Chill is not a hidden transformation here, and extra gauge does not guarantee an uninterrupted sequence.
maid-spear.watch: Her listed maximum SPD is 90, and the special's SPD buff lasts only one turn. She has no ordinary debuff, ally buff or protection. Final Service's turn progress is not an immediate extra turn, and a buff must still be present when its condition is checked.
maid-spear.dependency_note: Her attacks work on their own, but an external lasting buff makes Final Service's extra progress easier to use. She needs healing and protection rather than an attribute-matched teammate for its own sake.

skill_order.name: Final Service
skill_order.why: Level 4 improves cooldown and level 8 improves the ultimate's turn progress, her main distinguishing utility.

skill_order.name: Menacing Blue Thorn
skill_order.why: Then get cooldown reductions at levels 4/8 to use SPD Up more often.

skill_order.name: Perfect Strike
skill_order.why: Basic damage is later if Claire remains a committed carry.

skill_order.name: Punctuality
skill_order.why: Passive ATK is useful but creates no new timing mechanic.

rotation: If Claire has a useful active buff, use Final Service for its additional turn progress when a priority target is available.
Use Menacing Blue Thorn for damage and SPD Up, but check the remaining buff duration before assuming it will still qualify on a later turn. A partner's longer buff is more dependable.
Use Perfect Strike during cooldown gaps. Do not wait for full Chill expecting penetration, a transformation or a free follow-up that is not listed.

best_partners.why: Emily gives Claire a three-turn ATK buff and Barrier, providing both a useful buff condition and protection.
Ceres supplies team ATK Up, healing and cleansing, helping Claire stay active.
Charlotte's CRIT Rate buff and possible ATK Up can qualify Claire's buff condition while improving damage.
Bell supplies buff removal, Silence and area damage, covering jobs Claire cannot perform.

maid-spear.build_tip: ATK, reliable CRIT Rate and CRIT DMG, with SPD to address her low listed maximum. Add enough HP/DEF to survive until her next action; pure speed cannot replace missing protection. Journey option: Cleaning, and an Unexpected Guest is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +5% at Arcana level 1. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
maid-spear.tier_reason: The C+ PvE / C PvP ratings fit a straightforward single-target kit with modest personal tempo and little team utility. Buffed Final Service is a sensible use case, but does not supply the utility of stronger duelists or control attackers.
maid-spear.investment: Take Final Service's level-4 cooldown and level-8 turn-progress upgrades, then the special's cooldowns. No potentials are listed. Avoid heavy spending on a promised full-Chill mechanic or exact star breakpoint absent from the profile. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. Claire’s Unique Potential belongs to Bunnygirl Claire in savior_sources; the character_id match does not establish it for this version. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
maid-spear.pve_note: Suitable for an already-built single-target damage slot with reliable buffs. She brings no boss debuff, wave attack or sustain, so judge whether her direct damage earns the slot in the particular encounter.
maid-spear.pvp_note: She needs buffs and protection to reach repeated turns, while opponents can remove buffs or disable her. A 30% buffed turn-progress gain at the upgraded skill level should not be presented as an uninterruptible loop.

kit_explanation.name: Perfect Strike
kit_explanation.explanation: Perfect Strike hits one enemy and adds one Chill. Nova adds Toughness damage. There is no listed full-Chill resource payoff elsewhere in this kit.

kit_explanation.name: Menacing Blue Thorn
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Menacing Blue Thorn hits one enemy and gives one turn of SPD Up. Levels 4 and 8 reduce cooldown. Its Nova also grants one turn of ATK Up after the attack, so do not count that newly granted ATK buff as boosting the same hit.

kit_explanation.name: Final Service
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Final Service hits one enemy and advances Claire's next turn by 10%, rising to 20% at level 8, plus another 10% if she has a buff. Level 4 reduces cooldown. At its highest listed level that is 30% total when the buff condition holds, not a guaranteed immediate turn.

kit_explanation.name: Punctuality
kit_explanation.explanation: Punctuality increases ATK from 3% to 12% across passive levels. It has no listed reaction, automatic speed increase or additional ally effect.

pros: Final Service gets a concrete extra benefit from existing allied buffs.
Personal SPD Up supports repeated attacks.
Simple single-target use with no external reaction trigger required.
A teammate’s lasting buff can enable the ultimate without spending her special first.
cons: No area attack or enemy debuff.
Low listed maximum SPD and only a one-turn SPD buff.
No self-heal, Barrier or ally support beyond damage.

teams.name: Buffed finisher (theorycraft)
teams.why: Emily gives a lasting buff and Barrier, Ceres heals, and Bell handles dispel/Silence around Claire's single-target attacks.
teams.playstyle: Keep an actual buff active for Final Service and choose the enemy Bell has made vulnerable.

teams.name: Critical support (theorycraft)
teams.why: Charlotte supplies crit support, Emily protects Claire and Ceres sustains the team.
teams.playstyle: Use Vow on Claire before her action when needed, then Final Service with an active buff; this lineup favors survival over wave clearing.

alternatives.why: Fei is a higher-rated Moon single-target alternative with evasion reactions, ATK Down and full-Chill DEF penetration.
alternatives.tradeoff: Her damage depends partly on being attacked and evading; a new build is required and evasion is not reliable against every enemy.

alternatives.why: Lacy is higher-rated and offers SPD Up, an ATK-reducing enemy mark and conditional self-healing.
alternatives.tradeoff: She changes attribute and uses a mark-dependent response engine rather than Claire's simple buffed ultimate; availability is not assumed.

maid-scissors.summary:
Scarlet is a single-target Burn attacker. Her ultimate applies Burn and may add another instance, then Let's Heat Things Up! deals more damage against a burning enemy. Her passive only increases HP, so most of her offensive value comes from active skills and ATK investment.

Choose her when maintaining Burn is part of a larger team plan, especially beside Cristelle. Her special needs Burn already present for its 15% bonus, so check the target before committing the attack. ATK and useful Effect Hit support that job, with speed and protection keeping her active. Against cleansing or Burn immunity, a more immediate attacker often fills the slot better.
maid-scissors.watch: Her special does not apply Burn itself. The second Burn is probabilistic outside the ultimate's Nova version, and Burn can be resisted, cleansed or blocked by immunity. She has no area hit or listed team buff.
maid-scissors.dependency_note: She can apply her own Burn, but its cooldown and the brief extra Burn make an allied Burn source useful. Cristelle specifically turns Scarlet's Sun attacking skills and Burn into a larger linked team plan.

skill_order.name: Think You Can Withstand This?!
skill_order.why: Get level 6 for Burn access and levels 4/8 if the extra Burn matters to the team.

skill_order.name: Let's Heat Things Up!
skill_order.why: Then take cooldown levels 4/8 and damage on the burning-target payoff.

skill_order.name: I'll Cut You Up!
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later choice for a committed Scarlet carry.

skill_order.name: I'll Take You On!
skill_order.why: Passive HP can help survival but does not create an offensive engine.

rotation: Apply Burn with Think You Can Withstand This?! or let a partner establish it first.
Use Let's Heat Things Up! while Burn remains on the selected target. Do not assume an expired or cleansed Burn still grants the bonus.
Use I'll Cut You Up! during cooldown gaps. Spend Nova on the ultimate only when the extra Burn attempt and Toughness damage justify the resource.

best_partners.why: Cristelle can apply broad Burn, extend a target's Burn and gain Ignition from Scarlet's attacking Sun cooldown skills.
Charlotte can supply CRIT Rate and an upgrade-dependent ATK buff, and adds ATK Down for defense.
Ceres supplies healing, cleansing and party ATK support that Scarlet lacks.
Emily protects Scarlet with a targeted Barrier and buffs her ATK without needing Scarlet to debuff first.

maid-scissors.build_tip: ATK improves direct attacks and ATK-based Burn. Add SPD and damage consistency, then enough Effect Hit if Burn application matters; do not assume CRIT DMG improves every Burn tick. Journey option: The Great and Amazing Bunny Girl is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
maid-scissors.tier_reason: The C+ PvE / C PvP ratings fit a narrow Burn specialist with limited utility and a basic HP passive. She has a justified role beside Cristelle, but higher-utility attackers contribute more when Burn is ineffective.
maid-scissors.investment: Start with the ultimate's cooldown and meaningful Burn upgrades, then the special's cooldowns. No unique potentials are listed. Keep spending proportional to her Burn-team role rather than expecting a hidden breakthrough to add broad utility. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. Ready and Willing! belongs to Bunnygirl Scarlet in savior_sources; the character_id match does not establish it for this version. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 10 at level 200, listing +12 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
maid-scissors.pve_note: Useful where Burn persists on a priority target and a team can exploit it. Against Burn immunity or frequent cleansing, both damage-over-time value and the special's conditional bonus lose appeal.
maid-scissors.pvp_note: She needs a protected turn to apply Burn and another opportunity to exploit it. Immediate control or buff removal from another attacker may be more useful than a short secondary Burn.

kit_explanation.name: I'll Cut You Up!
kit_explanation.explanation: I'll Cut You Up! is a single-target basic that adds Ignition. Nova adds Toughness damage. No full-Ignition transformation is listed.

kit_explanation.name: Let's Heat Things Up!
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Let's Heat Things Up! attacks one enemy, gives Scarlet one turn of ATK Up and deals 15% more damage if the enemy already has Burn on attack. It has no listed Burn application. Levels 4 and 8 reduce cooldown.

kit_explanation.name: Think You Can Withstand This?!
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 5 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Think You Can Withstand This?! attacks one target and attempts a two-turn Burn at a listed 100% chance, plus a separate one-turn Burn whose chance rises from 50% to 75% at levels 4/8. Level 6 reduces cooldown. Nova raises the extra Burn's listed chance to 100% and adds Toughness damage; it does not promise immunity bypass.

kit_explanation.name: I'll Take You On!
kit_explanation.explanation: I'll Take You On! adds maximum HP, from 3% to 12% across passive levels. It does not list counterattacks, extra Burn or damage scaling from HP.

pros: Can establish the debuff required for her own special bonus.
Attacking Sun cooldown skills have explicit synergy with Cristelle.
ATK investment supports both direct attacks and Burn.
The ultimate attempts two separate Burn applications.
cons: No area damage, healing or ally protection.
Secondary Burn is unreliable without the relevant Nova enhancement.
Burn resistance or removal cuts into both linked offensive tools.

teams.name: Burn and chain (theorycraft)
teams.why: Scarlet supplies Burn, Kyra supplies other debuffs and Ceres sustains the group while Cristelle cashes in debuff count.
teams.playstyle: Coordinate Burn before Scarlet's special and Cristelle's ultimate; do not delay urgent cleansing or a finish for a perfect debuff count.

teams.name: Protected Burn attacker (theorycraft)
teams.why: Charlotte supports critical hits, Emily shields Scarlet and Ceres heals.
teams.playstyle: Use buffs deliberately, apply Burn to the priority target and attack while it remains; this defensive lineup may lack wave-clearing speed.

alternatives.why: Cristelle is higher-rated and adds reactive broad Burn, Burn extension, chain damage and personal turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: She depends on ally attack triggers and debuff uptime; replacing Scarlet loses one compatible Sun Burn supplier and requires a separate build.

alternatives.why: Carnelia is higher-rated and offers area damage, Buff Block and turn delay when broad utility matters more than Burn.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not provide Burn for a Burn-specific team, so a role change may require rebuilding the lineup.

magician-sniper.summary:
Clarissa is a simple single-target attacker with enemy SPD Down and personal SPD Up. Her passive only adds CRIT Rate. She can contribute a clear job with an existing build, but offers little team protection or offensive support beyond slowing one target.

Use her when one enemy’s speed matters and an existing build makes direct damage sufficient. The special’s ordinary slow and its Nova gauge reduction are different tools, so decide whether the extra 15% delay deserves the shared resource. ATK and critical damage follow actual crit needs. If the target ignores slowing, compare her remaining damage with a more versatile attacker.
magician-sniper.watch: Her ordinary special reduces SPD, not action gauge. The direct reduction of progress toward an enemy's next turn belongs to its Nova version. Her passive crit bonus and listed maximum 26% CRIT Rate should not be added together blindly if the displayed stats already include progression.
magician-sniper.dependency_note: Her own speed buff and attacks function without a specific teammate. Partners should provide healing, protection and stronger buffs or debuffs; the ag-manip tag refers to her conditional Nova option.

skill_order.name: Shooting by Instinct
skill_order.why: Take cooldown levels 4/8 if recurring SPD Down is her reason for the slot.

skill_order.name: This Is How You Shoot a Gun
skill_order.why: Then improve cooldown levels 4/8 and damage on the stronger attack with SPD Up.

skill_order.name: Winding Windpath
skill_order.why: The crit passive helps damage consistency, but check actual displayed crit before more investment.

skill_order.name: Step Back a Bit
skill_order.why: Basic damage is a later upgrade after the cooldown skills.

rotation: Use Shooting by Instinct when a susceptible priority enemy needs slowing; use its Nova only when the extra turn delay merits the shared resource.
Use This Is How You Shoot a Gun for damage and SPD Up, especially when another ally already covers SPD Down.
Use Step Back a Bit while cooldowns recover. Do not spend multiple basics chasing an unlisted maximum-Leap transformation.

best_partners.why: Dana can buff Clarissa if she is the highest-ATK other ally; Clarissa's Star attacks feed Dana's unlocked passive.
Emily's targeted ATK buff and Barrier protect an attacker who has no self-heal.
Frey provides Barriers, cleansing and enhanced healing to Star Clarissa.
Bell supplies buff removal and Silence that Clarissa lacks, and can contribute area damage.

magician-sniper.build_tip: ATK and CRIT DMG after checking actual CRIT Rate, then SPD and survival. Avoid overbuilding Effect Hit for a one-turn slow if the relevant enemy cannot be slowed. Journey option: Ready, Aim, Fire is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +6% at Arcana level 1. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
magician-sniper.tier_reason: The C+ PvE / C PvP ratings fit a narrow single-target damage kit whose main utility is SPD Down. Existing investment can make her usable, but stronger attackers bring area damage, buff removal or more substantial turn control.
magician-sniper.investment: Prioritize cooldown milestones at levels 4/8 on the skills you use, then damage. No unique potentials or hidden passive trigger are listed. Do not spend heavily expecting full Leap to unlock another mode. These are kit-based priorities: stored maximum stats and higher skill/passive levels do not describe a zero-star copy. The local records do not establish a reliable star requirement. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +3 CRIT Rate; it is not part of the starting stat line.
magician-sniper.pve_note: Use against a priority target where SPD Down matters and area damage is unnecessary. Boss immunity removes her main debuff utility, leaving straightforward single-target attacks.
magician-sniper.pvp_note: Her Nova special can delay an enemy turn, but ordinary casts only apply SPD Down. She has no listed cleanse, protection or buff removal to secure that sequence.

kit_explanation.name: Step Back a Bit
kit_explanation.explanation: Step Back a Bit attacks one enemy and adds Leap. No listed skill consumes full Leap for a special payoff. Nova adds Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Shooting by Instinct
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 5 turns, falling to 3 with its listed cooldown upgrades. Shooting by Instinct attacks one enemy and attempts one turn of SPD Down with a listed 100% base chance, still subject to applicable defenses. Levels 4 and 8 reduce cooldown. Only Nova adds a 15% reduction to the enemy's progress toward its next turn.

kit_explanation.name: This Is How You Shoot a Gun
kit_explanation.explanation: Listed cooldown: 6 turns, falling to 4 with its listed cooldown upgrades. This Is How You Shoot a Gun hits one enemy and gives Clarissa two turns of SPD Up. Levels 4 and 8 reduce cooldown. It does not provide an ally buff, DEF Down or area attack.

kit_explanation.name: Winding Windpath
kit_explanation.explanation: Winding Windpath adds CRIT Rate, increasing from 3% to 12% across four levels. No reactive attack or additional turn-progress effect is listed.

pros: Simple target selection and no required teammate trigger.
Personal SPD Up supports subsequent turn frequency.
Nova special adds a concrete enemy turn-progress reduction.
Her passive reduces the gear pressure needed for critical consistency.
cons: No area damage or ally buff.
Passive adds only CRIT Rate, with no broader engine.
Main utility is limited against slow-immune targets.

teams.name: Star support damage (theorycraft)
teams.why: Clarissa feeds Dana's Star-attack passive while Emily protects a carry and Frey heals.
teams.playstyle: Check Dana's automatic ATK-buff recipient, keep Clarissa safe and use her special only on a target whose speed matters.

teams.name: Control-assisted targeting (theorycraft)
teams.why: Bell removes buffs and Silences, Emily shields Clarissa, and Ceres supplies group healing.
teams.playstyle: Focus a vulnerable enemy after Bell's disruption; do not stack defensive support at the cost of failing a damage check.

alternatives.why: Bell is a higher-rated Star ranger with area ACC Down, buff removal and Silence, offering much broader utility.
alternatives.tradeoff: Bell lacks Clarissa's exact Nova turn-delay special and has defeat-dependent momentum; obtaining and building a replacement is a separate cost.

alternatives.why: Lacy is higher-rated in both modes, with strong personal speed, a broad ATK-reducing mark and conditional self-healing.
alternatives.tradeoff: Lacy changes attribute and team interactions, so replacing Clarissa also removes a Star attacker from Dana's resource engine.

magician-sniper.research_note: No ordinary-version build was published in the reviewed build index. Blossom or Bunnygirl recommendations are different kits; this ordinary-version advice is kit-based. The community page reviewed covers Stellar Sigil Blooming, so its Arcana list does not establish ordinary-version combat performance.

counterside-hilde.summary:
Hilde is a Sun defender whose HP supports both damage and barriers. Her opening passive shields the other allies, Buster Overdrive gives her a durable personal defensive state, and Dragon Buster helps her resist debuffs and take hits. Her taunt is selective rather than teamwide.

Use her opening protection to let a slower carry establish its damage plan. HP improves both survival and her HP-scaled attacks, while speed helps renew her own defensive buffs. Her ultimate picks its Taunt target by action progress, so inspect the enemy queue. Opening barriers buy time; they do not replace ongoing healing.
counterside-hilde.watch: Opening ally barriers happen at the first battle start and last one turn; Buster Overdrive's barrier-like defense protects Hilde, not the whole team. Its taunt targets the enemy closest to its next turn, not an enemy you freely pick.
counterside-hilde.dependency_note: Use Hilde to buy time for a damage or support engine. She has no regular party heal or cleanse, so bring recovery for sustained fights rather than assuming a defender replaces it.

skill_order.name: Buster Overdrive
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves cooldown and level 8 completes the listed taunt chance; her personal defensive state is the key payoff.

skill_order.name: Dragon Buster
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown on Immunity/DEF Up; use for self-protection rather than only its damage.

skill_order.name: Twin Blade
skill_order.why: Damage upgrades are last; Nova basic can add a short self barrier when needed.

rotation: Use Buster Overdrive when the highest-action-gauge enemy is a useful taunt target and Hilde needs Fafnir's Descent. Consider the targeted enemy's actual next action before spending it.
Use Dragon Buster to establish Immunity and DEF Up before danger. At five Ignition it consumes stacks to shorten its own cooldown, but survival can justify using it earlier.
Use Twin Blade between cooldowns for Ignition; Nova adds a one-turn self barrier if that solves immediate damage pressure.
Have the healer restore allies after opening barriers expire. Do not treat Fafnir's Descent or a chance to guard as guaranteed protection of every ally.

best_partners.why: Hilde's Sun turns feed Charlotte's Ignition, while her opening barriers cover Song of the Toast setup.
Opening protection gives Tyria time to mark enemies; keeping Tyria alive also keeps her Thorns active.
Serpang heals the party, gives stronger recovery to Sun allies and can weaken the taunted enemy's ATK.

counterside-hilde.build_tip: HP is the first scaling priority for durability, barriers and HP-based attacks; add DEF, SPD and useful resistance. Effect Hit is relevant if the one-target taunt is central, but does not make it bypass Immunity. Journey option: Nostalgia Strikes Back is Endurance-tagged, supporting DEF for personal durability; its listed training effectiveness is +7% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
counterside-hilde.tier_reason: The stored A PvE / A PvP ratings fit solid self-defense and immediate ally barriers without broad ongoing team sustain. She is most valuable when opening protection and a specific taunt matter, less so when repeated team healing/cleansing is required.
counterside-hilde.investment: Buy Buster Overdrive level-6 cooldown and level-8 taunt chance, then Dragon Buster level 6. Valkyrie's Will scales guard chance from 10% to 30% and adds HP at higher passive levels. No potentials are listed; do not add passive guard chance to a stored maximum stat and assume the total without checking how it is represented. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 6 at level 120, listing +8 Effect RES; it is not part of the starting stat line.
counterside-hilde.pve_note: Her HP scaling lets defensive investment contribute damage. Use a healer for long bosses and remember that taunt-resistant bosses can ignore the control portion while her personal buffs still function.
counterside-hilde.pvp_note: Opening barriers are a reason to select her into first-round pressure, but a one-turn taunt attempt can be resisted or blocked. Buff removal can remove ordinary Immunity/DEF Up even though Fafnir's Descent is undispellable.

kit_explanation.name: Twin Blade
kit_explanation.explanation: Twin Blade is a single-target basic with ATK and Max HP scaling that grants one Ignition. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and a one-turn barrier based on Hilde's Max HP.

kit_explanation.name: Dragon Buster
kit_explanation.explanation: Dragon Buster hits one target on a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It grants Hilde two-turn Immunity and DEF Up; after attacking with maximum Ignition, it consumes all stacks to shorten its cooldown by one. Damage also scales with Max HP. Nova adds one fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Buster Overdrive
kit_explanation.explanation: Buster Overdrive attacks all enemies on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6, adds Ignition and grants three-turn Fafnir's Descent. That state gives 20% DEF and HP-scaled damage absorption. It attempts a one-turn taunt on the highest-action-gauge enemy, with chance rising from 75% to 100% through levels 4 and 8. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Valkyrie's Will
kit_explanation.explanation: Valkyrie's Will automatically gives other allies a one-turn HP-scaled barrier at the first battle start. Guard chance rises from 10% to 30% through passive levels, with later HP increases. This is opening protection and a chance-based defensive aid, not recurring party barriers each turn.

pros: HP investment improves durability, barriers and attack scaling together.
Other allies receive protection before Hilde takes a normal action.
Personal Immunity, DEF Up and undispellable Fafnir's Descent help her remain active.
Her ultimate pressures the enemy closest to taking a turn.
cons: No party heal or cleanse for prolonged damage.
Taunt is one target selected by enemy action gauge and can fail.
Recurring major protection is mainly self-focused after the opening ally barriers expire.

teams.name: Sun protected attackers
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Two Sun attackers benefit from Hilde's opening shields and Serpang's enhanced Sun recovery; Hilde's turns feed Charlotte.
teams.playstyle: Choose the Overdrive timing for its actual taunt target; keep Serpang's recovery for allies after their short barriers expire.

teams.name: Shielded follow-up core
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Hilde buys opening time for two attack-trigger engines while Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Build the engines without assuming Hilde can taunt an entire enemy team; use recovery when area damage reaches the backline.

alternatives.why: Emily is a higher-rated PvE defender/support when a carry needs a renewable targeted barrier and ATK Up plus party DEF Up.
alternatives.tradeoff: Hilde retains opening barriers for all other allies and an explicit taunt attempt; Emily is not a direct replacement for that opener.

alternatives.why: Dress Asherah is a higher-utility sustain slot when damage arrives as repeated chip or debuffs, offering party healing and cleanse.
alternatives.tradeoff: She does not replace Hilde's defender role, opening barriers or taunt; choose based on the threat rather than rating alone.

counterside-hilde.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

counterside-mina.summary:
Yoo Mina combines area Bleed application with a crit-driven personal turn cycle. She builds ATK after attacks, speeds toward her next turn when she crits, and can add area chain damage through Catalyst if that potential is available. She is a damage dealer rather than a control character.

Use her as an attacking carry with bleed utility, supported by protection and recovery. Critical hits matter for both action progress and her confirmed unique-potential follow-up, while successive attacks build the passive damage ramp. Bleed gives another pressure route against eligible targets. None of those effects grants safety, so an exposed Mina can fall before the ramp pays off.
counterside-mina.watch: Bleed needs to land and enemies need to take turns for its damage to matter. Pulse Impact's extra Bleed needs five Leap; it does not grant five Leap by itself. Her crit-gauge effect is not a guaranteed full extra turn.
counterside-mina.dependency_note: She generates her own Leap and self buffs. External protection, timely ATK support and an enemy resistance reducer are useful; she has no mandatory faction partner.

skill_order.name: Wolvesbane
skill_order.why: Level 6 reduces cooldown and level 8 makes each of the two Bleed attempts list 100% chance; the area hit also supplies ATK Up and Leap.

skill_order.name: Pulse Impact
skill_order.why: Level 6/8 improves special cadence and Bleed chance; this also establishes her own CRIT Rate Up.

skill_order.name: Pulse Revolver
skill_order.why: Basic damage is useful later as she builds Leap and passive attack stacks.

rotation: Use Wolvesbane when multiple targets can receive Bleed or when its ATK buff/two Leap are needed. Do not assume the post-hit ATK buff strengthens that same opening hit.
Use Pulse Impact when its CRIT Rate buff is missing; at five Leap it attempts an additional Bleed without stating that Leap is consumed.

Attack consistently to accumulate Experienced Rookie's ATK stacks and use crits for next-turn progress. With Catalyst available, prioritize a reliable critical hit on her own turn for its once-per-turn area chain damage.
Use Pulse Revolver between cooldowns and switch away from a Bleed plan if the enemy is immune or cleanses before its turns.

best_partners.why: Lyn's Clear Wind branch can grant three Leap to Star allies, helping Mina reach the special's extra-Bleed condition, and adds Star-team CRIT DMG support.
Emily supplies a barrier and ATK Up for Mina's ATK-based attacks and Bleed while keeping her alive through ramp.
Serpang's Effect RES Down supports Bleed attempts and his party healing covers Mina's lack of recovery; it is not an immunity bypass.

counterside-mina.build_tip: Favor ATK for attacks and ATK-scaled Bleed, enough CRIT Rate after her own buff for turn progress/Catalyst, then CRIT DMG and SPD. Effect Hit helps Bleed when enemies can be debuffed; it is not a substitute for crit consistency. Journey option: The Indomitable Masterpiece is Strength-tagged, supporting ATK for her attacking role; its listed training effectiveness is +9% at Arcana level 1. Its unique effect has a Bond threshold, so check the card before counting that bonus. This is a stat-fit option, not a proven best five-card setup.
counterside-mina.tier_reason: The stored A PvE / B+ PvP rating fits sustained damage and Bleed across waves with weaker immediate control. Debuffable long encounters favor her; cleanse, Immunity and fast PvP burst reduce her ramp and damage-over-time value.
counterside-mina.investment: Prioritize Wolvesbane and Pulse Impact level-6 cooldown/level-8 Bleed reliability. Experienced Rookie increases per-attack ATK from 2% to 4%, capped at five stacks, and crit-triggered turn progress from 9% to 15%. Catalyst is a listed unique potential for once-per-own-turn critical area chain damage, with an effect record of 30% ATK; no unlock threshold is given. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established. A separate progression check is Resonance grade 4 at level 80, listing +4 Effect Hit; it is not part of the starting stat line.
counterside-mina.pve_note: Area Bleeds are useful when several enemies survive long enough to take turns. Against a lone immune boss, evaluate her direct attacks and crit cycle rather than counting missing Bleed damage.
counterside-mina.pvp_note: Pressure can build if Bleeds stick, but she cannot stop the enemy from acting or cleansing. Her own CRIT Rate buff helps after setup; the first attack still needs gear or support if a crit is important.

kit_explanation.name: Pulse Revolver
kit_explanation.explanation: Pulse Revolver hits one enemy and adds one Leap. Nova adds damage and fixed Toughness damage. Leap modestly boosts damage against Moon enemies and enables the special's full-stack bonus.

kit_explanation.name: Pulse Impact
kit_explanation.explanation: Pulse Impact attacks one target on a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It gives Mina two-turn CRIT Rate Up and attempts two-turn Bleed, rising from 75% to 100% through levels 4 and 8. If Leap is already full after attacking, it attempts another two-turn Bleed. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Wolvesbane
kit_explanation.explanation: Wolvesbane attacks all enemies on a listed five-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It grants two-turn self ATK Up and two Leap, and attempts two separate two-turn Bleeds per enemy. Each attempt rises from 75% to 100% through upgrades. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Experienced Rookie
kit_explanation.explanation: Experienced Rookie automatically builds 2–4% ATK after each attack, stacking five times according to passive level, and grants 9–15% next-turn progress on a critical hit. Later passive levels also add a separate ATK increase. This is progress toward another turn, not a full extra turn per crit.

pros: Area attack can spread two Bleeds per enemy.
Own critical buff supports both damage and turn acceleration.
Catalyst offers additional area damage on a crit if the potential is available.
Successive attacks build her passive ATK ramp up to five stacks.
cons: Bleed is poor into Immunity or frequent cleansing.
No native protection, healing or enemy turn denial.
Attack-stack ramp and post-hit buffs make instant opening damage a weaker assumption.

teams.name: Star crit damage and Leap
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Lyn can supply Leap and CRIT DMG to Star Mina, Emily supplies targeted protection and ATK, and Dress Asherah heals/cleanses.
teams.playstyle: Use Lyn's Star-support branch when it helps Mina reach full Leap; avoid counting its alternate single-target branch as the same buff action.

teams.name: Debuff-supported Mina
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Professor M adds dual attacks and a special-skill mark, Hilde opening barriers, and Serpang healing/resistance reduction.
teams.playstyle: Keep Mina highest ATK if she should receive the dual attack; place resistance reduction before attempting key Bleeds when safe.

alternatives.why: Rosaria is a higher-rated area-damage option with area DEF Down and immediate 50% next-turn progress.
alternatives.tradeoff: Mina keeps repeated Bleed pressure and the Catalyst potential rather than Rosaria's Inferno resource cycle.

alternatives.why: Lyn provides higher-rated PvE wave/focused flexibility and direct Star-team support.
alternatives.tradeoff: Mina offers Bleed pressure without needing to choose Lyn's stance branch; Lyn does not replace damage-over-time application.

counterside-mina.research_note: Community build reviewed against the stored kit. Some detailed equipment recommendations require paid access; priorities here are kit-based, not a tested damage ranking.

counterside-rosaria.summary:
Rosaria is a fast Chaos area attacker who turns critical hits into Inferno stacks for a focused follow-up window. Difference in Class combines a large hit, DEF Down and 50% progress toward her next turn; Ruler's Judgement spends Inferno, adding an automatic basic at three stacks.

Choose Rosaria for immediate area pressure that can turn into a focused follow-up. The ultimate attempts two turns of DEF Down, returns 50% Action gauge and grants Throne, improving basic damage and speed. Critical hits across multiple targets help prepare the three-Inferno special and its extra basic. Build critical consistency before chasing that payoff. Her single emergency survival event gives time for recovery, but it does not keep her alive through every later burst.
counterside-rosaria.watch: Her protection against dropping below 40% HP happens only once per battle. It is not permanent invulnerability. Against one target, one area critical hit cannot be assumed to supply all three Inferno stacks.
counterside-rosaria.dependency_note: Rosaria supplies her own Inferno route, Agitation and area DEF Down. External early crit support and recovery improve consistency; another Chaos unit is not required merely to make her kit function.

skill_order.name: Difference in Class
skill_order.why: First priority: level 6 reduces cooldown and level 8 raises DEF Down to its listed 100% chance.

skill_order.name: Ruler's Judgement
skill_order.why: Level 6 improves cadence and damage upgrades strengthen Inferno spending.

skill_order.name: Ashen Inferno
skill_order.why: Basic damage matters when the ultimate is unavailable because it also builds Agitation and can produce Inferno.

rotation: Use Difference in Class into multiple targets when its DEF Down and critical-hit Inferno generation can set up the team. Nova adds 30% CRIT Rate for this attack, not permanently.
Check Inferno before Ruler's Judgement: one or two stacks add damage, while three also trigger Ashen Inferno automatically. A needed kill can justify spending below three.
Use Ashen Inferno between cooldowns to build Agitation and increase the chance of an Inferno stack; this chance scales with Agitation rather than every basic granting one immediately.
After her one-time survival effect activates, heal or shield her before another dangerous hit. The 50% gauge gain advances her next turn but is not an explicit extra turn.

best_partners.why: All In gives party CRIT Rate Up before Rosaria's area attack, improving the chance of building Inferno from multiple targets.
Emily protects Rosaria with a targeted barrier and ATK Up, especially valuable after the one-time survival trigger is spent.
Party healing and cleanse restore Rosaria after her low-HP safeguard, while allied turn progress helps continue the damage window.

counterside-rosaria.build_tip: Build reliable CRIT Rate, ATK and CRIT DMG, then SPD; add Effect Hit if area DEF Down is essential. Stored 109 SPD and five Toughness describe the database maximum profile, not a guaranteed opening advantage over geared enemies. The End Wears the Face of a Girl fits Strength training; its unique adds two Strength during training after 30 Bond.
counterside-rosaria.tier_reason: The stored S+ PvE / S+ PvP ratings fit immediate area pressure, area DEF Down, substantial turn progress and a one-time survival safeguard. Multi-target fights are especially favorable for Inferno generation; lone bosses reduce that particular opening payoff.
counterside-rosaria.investment: Buy Difference in Class levels 4/8 for DEF Down chance and level 6 for cooldown, then Judgement level 6. Tyrant of the North adds ATK at higher passive levels and extends the conditional low-HP ATK buff from one to three turns, but does not turn the once-per-battle protection into recurring safety. No potentials are listed. Skill/passive levels are not mapped to star unlocks here; stored effect records and maximum stats are not a promise of zero-star performance. No exact copy threshold is established.
counterside-rosaria.pve_note: Use the ultimate on meaningful waves rather than always saving it for a boss; multiple critical targets can establish the three-Inferno special window. On single bosses, basics and Agitation become a more important resource route.
counterside-rosaria.pvp_note: Her opening area damage/DEF Down and safeguard give a clear PvP role, but Immunity can block DEF Down and opponents can finish her after the one protection event. Keep healing ready rather than deliberately accepting repeated lethal hits.

kit_explanation.name: Ashen Inferno
kit_explanation.explanation: Ashen Inferno attacks one enemy and adds Agitation. Through the passive it can also create Inferno, with chance increasing by 20 percentage points per Agitation stack up to five. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Ruler's Judgement
kit_explanation.explanation: Ruler's Judgement hits one enemy on a listed four-turn cooldown reduced at level 6, adds Agitation and spends all Inferno. One stack adds 10% damage, two add 20%, and three add 20% plus an automatic Ashen Inferno. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage.

kit_explanation.name: Difference in Class
kit_explanation.explanation: Difference in Class attacks all enemies on a listed six-turn cooldown reduced at level 6. It attempts two-turn DEF Down, from 75% to 100% through upgrades, advances Rosaria's next turn by 50% and grants three-turn Owner of the Throne for basic damage and SPD. Each target critically hit grants Inferno, capped at three. Nova adds fixed Toughness damage and 30% CRIT Rate for this hit.

kit_explanation.name: Tyrant of the North
kit_explanation.explanation: Tyrant of the North automatically supports basic-to-Inferno generation. Once per battle it prevents a damage event from dropping HP below 40% and grants ATK Up if she ends the attack at 40% or lower; that buff lasts one to three turns by passive level. Higher passive levels also add ATK.

pros: Ultimate delivers damage, DEF Down and substantial next-turn progress in one action.
Three Inferno turns the special into damage plus an automatic basic.
One-time HP safeguard can keep her alive through an otherwise devastating hit.
Throne supplies 15% SPD alongside its basic-attack damage increase.
cons: Survival protection is once per battle and does not replace healing.
Three Inferno from one ultimate depends on multiple successful critical targets.
DEF Down can be resisted/blocked and she brings no cleanse or party protection.

teams.name: Protected area burst
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Frey supplies early crit support, Emily buffs/shields Rosaria, and Dress Asherah heals after the safeguard or cleanses disruption.
teams.playstyle: Place crit support before Difference in Class where turn order allows; spend Inferno based on its real count.

teams.name: Area pressure plus pursuit
teams.why: Theorycraft, not combat-tested: Hilde buys opening safety, Professor M calls the highest-ATK attacker into basics and marks a special target, and Dress Asherah sustains.
teams.playstyle: Keep Rosaria highest ATK if she should receive forced basics; focus Judgement on the marked priority enemy after the area opener.

alternatives.why: Carnelia offers Buff Block, enemy turn-progress reduction and a once-per-battle lethal-damage response, a sidegrade when disruption matters.
alternatives.tradeoff: Rosaria retains area DEF Down and a large immediate self gauge gain; Carnelia's denial uses different target and buff conditions.

alternatives.why: Lyn is a sidegrade for PvE teams needing Star-specific support and a choice between waves and focused critical damage.
alternatives.tradeoff: Rosaria offers area DEF Down and a personal survival safeguard without Lyn's stance planning.
